#1502. Opinion: Liverpool have found their perfect Alisson successor, but it's not who you think

Alisson is one of Liverpool's biggest-named players to be linked with an exit this summer.

The Brazilian's contract is set to expire in June 2027 and, right now, it doesn't feel like the Reds are going to offer him a new deal.

Indeed, rumours about both ends of the deal have been emerging and, even though the former Roma man has been an important asset for Liverpool this term, his age coupled with the sheer number of goalkeepers the Reds have on their books make a deal difficult.

Obviously, Alisson's time at the club has been well regarded. He's won two Premier League titles and one Champions League trophy.

But, since he's now in the twilight stages of his career, Liverpool need to approach this deal with caution and weigh up their options before making a final decision.

Lucas Chevalier wants to leave Paris Saint-Germain, Liverpool could make a move

Having a decent goalkeeper is one of the most important things for any football team.

Even if you have one of the best teams in the world in terms of outfielders, if your goalkeeper is poor, they're more than likely going to let you down.

This was the case when Giorgi Mamardashvili played last season with fans demanding that a new 'keeper was signed.

Initially, the Georgian was expected to take over from the Brazilian but, thanks to how poorly he performed, that didn't end up being the case.

Mamardashvili's poor form led to fans wondering who their next goalkeeper could be with a fresh update from L'Equipe now making that more than clear.

"Lucas Chevalier is ready to leave Paris Saint-Germain this winter. But there are many conditions for a departure. PSG will notably have to find a replacement before considering letting him go," they wrote.

Lucas Chevalier would be an out of the box signing for Liverpool

When Chevalier was brought to PSG by Luis Enrique, fans, pundits and journalists all thought that the Frenchman was destined to become their first choice.

Obviously he had some big shoes to fill after Gianluigi Donnarumma exited for Manchester City but, for Enrique's style of play, the Frenchman was the better option.

But, for one reason or another, the 25-year-old didn't hit the right notes and has been downgraded to their back-up by Matvey Safonov.

Neither of them are considered among the world's best but, Chevalier is almost certainly a better option for Liverpool than Mamardashvili would be.

Others such as Bart Verbruggen and Diogo Costa have also been linked with Liverpool but, since Chevalier actually wants to exit, a deal for him might be easier for Liverpool to agree on with PSG.

Nobody knows what the future has in store for any of Liverpool's first team squad but, if Chevalier is a player welcomed through the Anfield doors, the Reds will be in a decent place, even if he is replacing Alisson.

#1501. Self-serving Scottish clubs were always going to ensure Craig Mulholland's youth football revolution was doomed to failure

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 12:01 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:03 EST, 24 November 2026

Given how quickly things have unravelled under Sebastien Pocognoli, serious questions are now being asked of those in power at the Scottish Football Association.

Ian Maxwell and Craig Mulholland, the chief executive and chief football officer who led the recruitment process, certainly talked a good game when Pocognoli was appointed.

However, when Mulholland took up his position in the summer, his remit was much broader than merely the appointment of a new head coach for the national team. He was tasked with trying to initiate a much-needed revamp of youth development throughout Scottish football.

Only a few months into the job, those plans have already hit the buffers due to resistance from clubs, despite the obvious need for more young Scottish players to play more first-team football.

The SFA had proposed including two Under-21 players starting in cup competitions and the same age group playing a minimum of 6 per cent of all available minutes across a season in league competition.

SFA chief football officer Craig Mulholland has met resistance in his bid to shake up the game

When it immediately became clear that several clubs in Scotland weren’t keen on that, a new watered-down version was then put back on the table.

Now there have been reports that those plans might be booted even further into the long grass and possibly won’t even be voted on at all this season.

As is always the case, the self-serving interest from clubs in Scotland will always trump the need for national reform.

But that is only part of the story. What is also of serious concern is the lack of quality coaching afforded to players in academies across the country.

If that was to be addressed, clubs would perhaps feel more obliged to play more younger players if they were ready for first-team football.

It is a multi-faceted problem – and one which Mulholland is no closer to solving. Clubs are selfish and will serve their own needs, with no obligation to buy into any new proposals.

The SFA could stand firm and try to force some of these plans through as non-negotiable. A tough stance, albeit one that risks becoming messy.

But nobody should be naïve enough to believe that self-interest from the clubs is the root of all problems here. It is much, much deeper than that.

#1499. Opinion: Sensational player has officially announced himself as Liverpool's newest star

Liverpool have a new star. One player has officially announced himself as a key player with a fantastic performance.

Liverpool went into this season with a very imbalanced squad. It was one that required a lot from new head coach Andoni Iraola, essentially asking him to improve and experiment with players to get the most out of it.

Of course, that's largely the job of a head coach but it's rare that so much experimentation was necessary from a UEFA Champions League side that won the Premier League two seasons ago. But that's what Liverpool offered Iraola after two transfer windows that tore up large portions of the team.

No defensive midfielders, no recognised right-back, four left-wingers, no right-wingers, and one fit centre-forward. Hardly a 'win now' group of players. Iraola, though, has worked some real magic.

And that includes solving the defensive midfielder problem. At least for now.

The midfielder problem was a surprise one. We fully expected Liverpool to invest in the middle of the pitch over the summer but they simply ignored the issue. Even more bizarre was a decision to sell Curtis Jones without any sort of replacement.

It left Iraola short but it's a problem he appears to have fixed. Trey Nyoni has stepped up incredibly well, moving from a mere youth player who hoped for minutes to a genuine starting threat in the span of just a few months.

Wednesday night, though, felt like an announcement of sorts. Nyoni started away from home in the UEFA Champions League and thrived, holding down the midfield against a rampant Club Brugge.

Liverpool’s clean sheet made them the first team to hold out against Brugge for a very, very long time. The first team to beat Brugge in months, too.

Nyoni played his part. He wasn’t necessarily a defensive force by the way he won tackles here, it was more about his efforts on the ball to keep Liverpool ticking over.

92 per cent pass completion away from home in the Champions League is fantastic. It’s even more fantastic that he did it while completing 11 line-breaking passes - this wasn’t a case of Nyoni simply picking the simple ball every time.

That 11 was the third-highest figure in the match and second-highest for Liverpool (Jeremy Jacquet had 13). It’s exactly the kind of midfield play that the Reds have been crying out for and doing it at a difficult ground in the premiere competition is just outstanding from a 19-year-old.

Nyoni is special and this felt like an announcement. Confirmation that he is a proper star player and one Liverpool can count on in major fixtures.

#1497. Opinion: Richard Hughes' bargain deal has saved Liverpool's season

Liverpool finished the 2025-26 season rather poorly.

They were so bad that Arne Slot was actually relieved of his duties.

Admittedly, this came as a bit of a surprise to most people as fans thought that Fenway Sports Group were going to try and stick with the Dutchman for at least one more season.

Obviously, that didn't end up happening and in the end, Andoni Iraola took over and is currently leading the Reds to a fourth-place finish.

Their performances may have improved but, that doesn't mean that they should settle for fourth, especially since they spent over £150 million on new players in the summer.

Despite this, it's good that things seem to be going well with one of Richard Hughes' last deals potentially saving Liverpool's campaign.

Jeremy Jacquet was a bargain buy from Richard Hughes

When the £55 million fee for Jeremy Jacquet was first revealed, most people thought that Liverpool massively overspent on him.

The centre-back is only 20 years old and has had no experience of football outside of Ligue 1.

He was also playing for a Rennes team which weren't seen as one of France's best which led many to believe that he was just outperforming his teammates, rather than actually playing well.

However, since coming into Liverpool's starting XI, Jacquet has changed the minds of the doubters and has quickly entered the conversation as one of the Premier League's best-performing defenders.

The Frenchman has played an awful lot of football for Liverpool this term and has had a couple of different partners in the centre of defence.

But, every challenge he has faced has led to his skills improving which is why the Reds' season could have been saved by the youngster.

Liverpool would be a lot worse off without Jeremy Jacquet among their ranks

As mentioned, Jacquet is now being mentioned as one of the Premier League's best young defenders.

The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he quickly rectifies any mistakes he makes is impressive.

On the ball, he's extremely confident and, if needed, he can ping a pass across the pitch.

Without Jacquet among their ranks, Liverpool would have to start with Joe Gomez or Ronald Araujo in the centre of their defence.

And, while Araujo has played as a centre-back for the Reds this season, if he was used there in each and every game, their right-back situation would be very dicey.

Jeremie Frimpong isn't up to scratch and, with Conor Bradley still side-lined due to injury, someone such as Dominik Szoboszlai or Gomez would have to be played out of position to cover that role.

So, the fact that Jacquet is a Liverpool player is a massive help to them and is likely one of the main reasons why they're only seven points adrift of first-placed Arsenal.

#1496. GdS: ‘EuroMilan: the final call’ – four necessities to get the European campaign back on track

AC Milan have made a false start in their Europa League campaign, and they are running out of chances to put things right.

After losing three of their first four games in Europe, this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below) writes that Milan must win away from home against Olympiacos to keep their hopes of reaching the round of 16 alive.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In Athens, Ruben Amorim will put out his strongest side to try and do exactly that. Christian Pulisic and Diego Moreira will operate on the flanks, while Omari Hutchinson is set to feature behind Gonçalo Ramos. They have broken the mission down into four parts.

In Europe – a stage where Milan traditionally feel at home – the team has only truly looked comfortable against RB Salzburg, where they cruised past their opponents. Bournemouth proved to have too much, and even at San Siro Benfica and Ferencváros emerged with wins.

One fact remains: while Milan are flying in the league, their attempt to take off in Europe never quite got off the ground. There is a gap that must be bridged: the distance between the Milan seen in European competition and the side so highly regarded in the league.

This extends to individual performances: the highly-praised Rabiot and Moreira have been instrumental in pushing Milan toward the Champions League spots domestically, yet they have yet to carry that form into Europe.

The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play. The Belgian has 4 goals and 4 assists in the league, yet has failed to produce a decisive moment in continental competition. It is time to bring that form onto the continent.

In the league, we see a Milan that never leaves its strongest players on the sidelines. In the wake of the defeat to Ferencváros – which followed a victory in the derby – Amorim remarked: “Perhaps we aren’t ready to be competitive every three days.” Now, the team must prove him wrong.

Hopes for European qualification depend on climbing from the current 28th-place position, which requires goals. Those goals are expected to come from Gonçalo Ramos. In the Rossoneri’s only European victory so far, he did get on the scoresheet, but it was the final one in a 4-0 rout.

So, it could hardly be described as a decisive goal. That is exactly the kind of contribution needed this evening at the Karaiskakis Stadium, where the Diavolo will fight for a chance to rejoin the pack within reach of the play-off spots at the very least.

Ramos is the man for the job: he is the current No.9, he has just returned to scoring in the league after a drought, and with January approaching, there is the prospect of a fresh influx of goals. Following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim hopes for a repeat in Athens.

The narrative that he is a ‘team-oriented’ striker holds water and has served as a valid defence against those questioning his lack of goals given he ranks second in the league for successful hold-up plays, third for flick-ons, and boasts impressive statistics in ball recovery and defensive actions.

While these figures highlight his excellent team contribution, the financial investment of over €70m is also significant. From a forward who is a two-time European champion, it is only fair to expect goals that truly make the difference.

Another objective for this European night is to prove the team’s stature even without the immense Luke Modric, who is sidelined due to injury. Ardon Jashari will take his place, making Milan less focused on possession and more on aggression.

The style of play will mirror that of their opponents: individual duels – and, by extension, the intensity and approach to the match – will be more decisive than ever. While the squad has often been heavily rotated in previous European fixtures, this time it will feature the strongest XI available.

Jashari’s dynamism will need to come to the fore. Without Luka’s class and command of the tempo, the team’s playmaking dynamic shifts. Milan must turn this into an action-packed encounter, full of constant twists and turns, to avoid being sidelined by their opponents.

Assisting in this effort will be Rabiot and Pulisic, the latter acting as a vital link between the midfield and the attack. The required intensity should translate into a greater presence in the opposition’s hal. Ideally, right inside the penalty area.

Paradoxically, following the celebration against Frosinone, Amorim was the least satisfied: he had wanted more sustained pressure near or inside the opponent’s box. Now, necessity dictates this approach: a controlled game must give way to an all-out assault.

Beyond Jashari – who is expected to provide more running and pressing – Moreira remains another key weapon, thanks to his surging runs down the flanks. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Hutchinson serve as options Amorim can call upon during the match should the team need a spark.

Climbing the standings is a must. Milan may sit fourth in the league, but they cannot afford to be twenty-eighth in the Europa League table. Moving up won’t be easy: the Greeks remain unbeaten (three wins and a draw) and have conceded only one goal.

It is the joint-best defensive record in the UEL (along with Bayer Leverkusen). That is hardly an encouraging statistic for a Milan side that must score in order to win, because as things stand total elimination is on the cards.

This would be a disgrace for a club aiming to reclaim its place as a major player on the international stage. There is still time to recover, however. Looking at the last two editions, 14 points (2024-25) and 16 points (2025-26) were enough to get into the top eight. Milan are on three, with 12 up for grabs.

So, Amorim’s side could even aim for direct qualification. However, a complete turnaround would be needed. So, the play-offs are more realistic, and – based on the figures from the last two editions – 9 or 10 points would be required in this case.

Milan would thus need to obtain another six or seven points from their upcoming matches against Sunderland (at home), Levski Sofia (away), and Ararat-Armenia (at San Siro). By no means an easy task, however.

#1494. Man United Confidential: Carrington crash adds to Mauricio Pochettino's woes, as new boss set to cut players' days off... and why the wait goes on for coach Silvia Tuya

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 12:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:16 EST, 24 November 2026

As if having his first training session as Manchester United head coach sabotaged by a drone wasn’t dramatic enough, Mauricio Pochettino’s second day at work saw access to the club’s training base blocked by a serious road accident.

The collision between a vehicle and a cyclist on one of the two approaches to Carrington, where United’s players and staff are regularly seen driving through a security checkpoint, meant it was closed off for several hours on Friday while an ambulance and police cars attended the scene.

Greater Manchester Police say the cyclist was taken to hospital to receive treatment for injuries that were not life-threatening and no arrests were made.

However, anyone leaving Carrington had to take an alternative route in the opposite direction. That included the players after training and Pochettino and his staff following his first pre-match press conference.

The accident on Friday completed an eventful 48 hours at Carrington after a rogue drone operator filmed 12 minutes of Pochettino’s first training session and posted it on YouTube. He later took the video down and apologised for the intrusion, which United sources said was the right thing to do – even though they had not contacted the uploader directly and do not intend to take legal action against him.

They insisted there was not a breach of security at Carrington, but claimed a number of laws had been broken. Insiders promised a robust response to any further incidents to protect the rights of the club and its staff, and warned that those responsible would be ‘exposing themselves to significant legal and financial risk’.

It's been a testing first few days for Mauricio Pochettino as Manchester United boss

One of the unexpected issues to hamper the Argentine was a drone filming his first training session

Meanwhile, players leaving Carrington last Friday had to take an alternative route after a serious road accident near United's training ground

Confidential understands Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems as soon as possible.

The squad were pictured arriving around 8.30am as they looked to regroup after the 4-0 hammering at Anfield and begin their preparations for the Champions League tie against Sporting Lisbon in Portugal on Wednesday night.

The Argentine is eager to spend as much time as possible with the players on the training ground, having only taken over as United boss last Wednesday – four days before the Liverpool clash.

United now face 11 games in 43 days and sources believe there may not be too many days off as Pochettino tries to haul his team out of the relegation zone and ensure qualification for the knockout stage of the Champions League.

At least the indications are that he will allow the players to stay at home the night before games at Old Trafford, rather than having them cooped up in a hotel like some previous United managers.

Pochettino ordered the United players into Carrington an hour early on Monday morning to flush the Liverpool defeat out of their systems

Matheus Cunha won’t play any part against Sporting following his red card in United's last Champions League tie against Roma three weeks ago.

Confidential has learned the Brazilian was set to claim the player of the match award after scoring two late goals in the 3-2 win over Roma, only for UEFA to step in.

UEFA rules prevent a player who has been sent off from receiving the award and so the selector – in this case Steve Cooper, the former Leicester, Nottingham Forest and Swansea boss who is now one of the governing body's technical observers – was forced into a late switch, picking Bruno Fernandes instead.

Cunha’s absence will be keenly felt in Portugal. He played no part in Tuesday’s training session at Carrington, instead working on his own in the gym.

At a time when United have the most porous defence in Europe’s top five leagues and Matthijs de Ligt, Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez and Ayden Heaven are all struggling for form, Pochettino is going to need Harry Maguire.

Pochettino overlooked the experienced Englishman from the start for the trip to Anfield but ended the match with Maguire on the pitch and he was United’s best defender on another desperate afternoon.

Maguire is walking the tightrope of a ban as he remains on four yellow cards after 11 league games. Players are hit with a one-match ban once they receive five or more yellows prior to the conclusion of the 19th league game of the season – eight matches from now.

Even after Yoro's red card at Anfield was overturned on appeal, Pochettino can ill-afford to be without Maguire going forward.

Pochettino is going to need the experience of Harry Maguire to hold his defence together but he faces a ban if he is booked again

United are still waiting to see if Pochettino’s strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya can join his staff at Carrington despite hiring new fitness coach Sam Wilson.

Wilson has joined United following his departure from Parma in October, having only moved to the Italian club as head of performance in the summer after 12 years at Arsenal.

It is understood Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team because she is waiting to see if a work permit will be approved.

She joined the US national team staff in October 2024 shortly after Pochettino, and travelled with him, first-team coach Miguel D’Agostino and analyst Alec Scott when they flew from Cincinnati to Manchester by private jet last week.

Strength and conditioning specialist Silvia Tuya has not yet been confirmed as part of Pochettino’s backroom team

Some of the early changes under Pochettino have been more subtle than others. Observant fans may have noticed that when the club announced the team to face Liverpool at 3.15pm on Sunday, it was in positional order.

Previously, United’s line-up has been listed numerically, leaving fans to deliberate over the formation. But Pochettino liked to name his team positionally at Tottenham and Chelsea, and admitted in a Q&A on MUTV last week that he wants to do the same at United.

It was clear from the club’s social media post on Sunday that Pochettino would be sticking to the 4-3-2-1 formation favoured by Michael Carrick, with Patrick Dorgu returning on the left wing and Cunha leading the attack.

Not that it lasted very long, as Pochettino admitted he was forced to put his game plan ‘in the bin’ inside eight minutes when Yoro was sent off.

This weekend’s match-up between United and Brentford brings together the most ill-disciplined English team in all competitions and the dirtiest team in the Premier League.

No English team has had more players sent off this season than United’s four – Yoro twice, Cunha against Roma and Martinez against Chelsea.

Meanwhile, Brentford are bottom of the Premier League’s disciplinary 'points table' thanks to their three red cards and 22 yellow cards. So expect referee Rob Jones to be a busy man on Pochettino’s home debut.

Leny Yoro brings down Alexander Isak at Anfield and is sent off - his second red card of the season

Richard Arnold, who preceded Omar Berrada as United's chief executive, pocketed a £5.53m pay-off to stand down after Ineos moved into the club

While Omar Berrada found himself back in the firing line last weekend, the man he succeeded as United’s chief executive was cutting a much more relaxed figure.

Richard Arnold, who led United between February 2022 and December 2023, was spotted enjoying himself on Chester’s popular Eastgate Street on Saturday night – 24 hours before a beleaguered Berrada watched United’s 4-0 thrashing 30 miles down the road at Anfield.

After stepping up to replace Ed Woodward, Arnold was in charge of United for the period spanning United’s strategic review which led to Sir Jim Ratcliffe acquiring 29 per cent of the club. Once it became clear that Ineos would take over the day-to-day running of United, he accepted a £5.53million pay-off to stand down, with the club’s general counsel Patrick Stewart stepping in on an interim basis.

Arnold is now enjoying a quieter life as an executive director at Norton Motorcycles and, it would appear, nights out close to his home near Chester.

It was there that he met a group of United protesters outside his local pub in June 2022 and admitted that the last 12 months had been ‘a f****** nightmare’ and United had ‘f****** burned through cash’. Nothing much seems to have changed since then.

#1493. Fabrizio Romano confirms it: Liverpool could sign striker for €35m

Fabrizio Romano has confirmed Liverpool's opportunity to sign a striker for €35m. But will they go for it?

The January transfer window is very nearly here and Liverpool may just have work to do. There's a sense that while the Reds are playing well under Andoni Iraola, they're doing so with something of a makeshift squad.

Or at least, a squad that isn't very balanced. There's room for improvement, with Liverpool lacking a proper defensive midfielder, seemingly unsettled on any right-back, and lacking any wingers who naturally play from the right.

If they get one or two players? It could well transform them from a very good, competitive team to one actually trying to win the major honours. And Iraola is certainly suggesting with his efforts that the potential is there.

But Liverpool would need to nail their signings and that means adding the right people for the right roles. One of the more interesting links, however, comes in a little-talked-about position.

Fabrizio Romano on Gustavo VarelaLiverpool have been linked with Gustavo Varela, who is currently lighting up Serie A with Monza. He's got 11 goals and an assist in his 11 league matches this season, including a brace against Fiorentina at the weekend. It's a strange one, though. Liverpool don't necessarily need a striker, given Alexander Isak is the clear first-choice and scoring goals, while Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo can also play there. Of course, there's also Hugo Ekitike - we do expect the Frenchman will be back this season, even if he's been out long-term. Exactly how much of an option he is this campaign isn't clear but it feels highly unlikely that Liverpool would sign someone to essentially replace him.

Liverpool have been linked with Gustavo Varela, who is currently lighting up Serie A with Monza. He's got 11 goals and an assist in his 11 league matches this season, including a brace against Fiorentina at the weekend.

It's a strange one, though. Liverpool don't necessarily need a striker, given Alexander Isak is the clear first-choice and scoring goals, while Bradley Barcola and Cody Gakpo can also play there.

Of course, there's also Hugo Ekitike - we do expect the Frenchman will be back this season, even if he's been out long-term. Exactly how much of an option he is this campaign isn't clear but it feels highly unlikely that Liverpool would sign someone to essentially replace him.

Unless they feel a new striker is necessary to compete for trophies this season and the next. And they might. Ekitike is a gamble at this stage.

It certainly appears that the chance to sign Varela will be there. Fabrizio Romano has confirmed that he's available for around €35m, which is potentially a steal if his goal scoring numbers hold up.

Though, Serie A's history is littered with strikers who started a season remarkably well only to fade away gradually, never replicating the form again. So while Varela is playing brilliantly, he'd be an enormous risk.

#1492. Cambuur vs Sparta Rotterdam - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 26 Nov 2026 18:20, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:56

High-flying Cambuur will look to continue their resurgence when they host Sparta Rotterdam at Kooi Stadion on Saturday evening.

On the other hand, the visitors head to Leeuwarden aiming to end a run of consecutive defeats and arrest a slump in form which has seen them lose four of their last five matches.

Like fellow newcomers ADO Den Haag and Willem II, Cambuur made a difficult start to life back in the top flight, collecting just one point from their opening five matches before claiming their first win of the season against NEC on September 12.

Johan Plat’s men have barely looked back since. Saturday’s 3-2 victory over Utrecht was their sixth win in nine matches across all competitions (D2, L1), the second-best record in the division over that period, behind only Ajax.

Now eighth in the Eredivisie table, the Yellow-Blues are closer to the European places than the relegation zone - a prospect that seemed inconceivable after they opened the campaign with four straight defeats by a combined score of 16-4.

Only seven of Cambuur’s 18 points so far have come in home matches, leaving them with much improvement in front of their fans, where November 8’s 5-2 thrashing at the hands of reigning champions PSV Eindhoven marked a fourth defeat in seven outings this term.

Saturday’s hosts are also winless in their last five home matches against Sparta dating back to January 2026 and could only muster one point across both meetings of their most recent Eredivisie campaign in 2022-23, leaving further room for apprehension within the home crowd.

After winning five consecutive Eredivisie matches either side of the new year, Sparta would have been optimistic about 2026. However, following a tumultuous couple of months, they will now be desperate to avoid ending the year in the bottom three.

Appointed to steady the ship following the departure of long-serving manager Maurice Steijn, Rogier Meijer has yet to spark a turnaround at Het Kasteel, and the former NEC boss is under increasing pressure to improve results.

Sunday’s 5-1 defeat to AZ Alkmaar was Meijer’s heaviest since taking charge in July, with Sparta having now conceded at least twice in 11 consecutive matches, giving them the division’s third-worst defensive record behind Willem II and FC Utrecht.

Only Groningen and Utrecht have scored more than De Rood-Witte Gladiatoren’s 22 goals among the bottom-half teams, so finding the net has not been a problem for Sparta and reducing their defensive frailties could help spark an upturn in form.

In the second of two consecutive away matches against newly-promoted sides, Saturday’s visitors will look to respond to a disappointing 3-1 defeat to ADO Den Haag last time out.

Sparta have scored four of their 15 away goals between the 15th and 30th minute, while Cambuur have conceded seven of their 20 home goals during the same period, giving Meijer’s men a prime window of opportunity to strike.

Sparta Rotterdam form (all competitions):

Jamal Amofa is expected to miss the rest of the season after suffering a cruciate ligament injury in October.

Twenty-four-year-old Jorn Berkhout was left out of the matchday squad against Utrecht due to injury, making his involvement on Saturday uncertain.

Nicolas Binder and Ilyes Hamache have each scored in three of Cambuur’s last five league matches and will be key to the hosts’ attacking threat.

Bruno Martins Indi is ineligible to feature for Sparta after he was sent off for two bookable offences six minutes apart against AZ.

He joins fellow defenders Teo Quintero and Nick Verschuren as the visitors continue to suffer from defensive absentees, which have plagued their season to date.

First-choice goalkeeper Michael Brouwer was absent last time out, so Filip Bednarek, who is averaging a 52% save accuracy, looks on course to deputise once again.

Jansen; Bouah, Baouf, Van Duijl, Costarelli; Souren, Maertens; Ceka, Arguioui, Hamache; Binder

Sparta Rotterdam possible starting lineup:

Bednarek; Kuipers, Vianello, Young, Martes; Hatenboer, Baas; Van Bergen, Mito, Babadi; Zonneveld

Cambuur’s recent form gives them confidence, and despite their poor record in this fixture, they remain favourites to claim victory.

We are tipping the home side to carry the day when all is said and done.

#1491. The cheats prosper: Man City thrash 10-man Liverpool

Just when the Premier League and the world outside of east Manchester and Abu Dhabi needed Liverpool to step up, to strike back, to make a point, they faltered. Maybe it was unfair to expect them to do so, given the circumstances. But unfairness, lack of clarity and uncertainty are all prevailing moods in English football at present.

How we had rubbed our hands in anticipation of Manchester City having to play their first league fixture here at Anfield after being found guilty of industrial-scale fraud with 114 of the 115 financial charges being proven against them.

It felt apt that it was at the home of Liverpool, who, along with Arsenal, possess the strongest sense of grievance at having been denied trophies and glory by City’s cheating. As expected, there were banners everywhere at Anfield. “A generation of supporters cheated,” one read and it summed up the depth of the anger.

Their fans would surely create the kind of bear-pit atmosphere that would leave City in no doubt at the vitriol that will rain down on them from now on. At every away ground. Liverpool could set the tone. The defiance.

This is a team who can stir the blood, surf the emotion and triumph against the odds more than any other; who have a proud history of doing so. Who feel the injustice at its most acute and could feed off that.

In the end Liverpool suffered their first defeat of the season. Their first under Andoni Iraola. And comprehensively so. It could not have come at a worse time for them and for the Premier League, and for the fans of every other club who wanted to see City humbled. On the pitch.

There was another sense of injustice. Up until the dismissal of Ryan Gravenberch, Liverpool were the better side. Especially as they attacked the Kop in the second half, drawing saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma, and began to build the kind of momentum that has, over the years, appeared to suck the ball into the net.

Ryan Gravenberch is OFF 🟥 https://t.co/IVIHNzqw6k

The midfielder’s first yellow card looked harsh. His second, for a foul on substitute Jérémy Doku was less so (but still not clear-cut) and it meant Liverpool had to play the final third of the game with 10 men. Instead of weaponising that; they wilted and the fans directed their frustration at referee Chris Kavanagh, believing he was lenient towards City.

This is not a slight on Iraola, but it is hard to imagine Jürgen Klopp not riding that wave of emotion more effectively and wringing more out of the available players. Turning to the fans; imploring them; cajoling them.

Instead it was City making the statement with an extraordinary power play as they scored three times in 13 minutes, inspired by Doku, whose cameo made him man of the match. That City could hold the winger back, on the bench, only to introduce him with such devastating effect again pointed to their phenomenal strength in depth.

They are again three points clear at the top, with six wins from six games, ahead of champions Arsenal and there is a frightening awesomeness about them at present that will make the Premier League shudder. For several reasons. What if they run away with it this season before being sanctioned, probably sometime in the spring? Where will that leave the competition?

In the face of City’s power and the adversity of losing Gravenberch, Liverpool simply could not cope. They were already depleted – without Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexander Isak, Hugo Ekitike and Cody Gakpo – and needed some of their other big signings to respond.

But this was not a good day for Bradley Barcola or Florian Wirtz, in particular, and it felt telling that the latter was withdrawn soon after Erling Haaland opened the scoring. He could, in fact, have also been sent off after catching Elliot Anderson late. The German’s contribution was once more woefully negligible; worryingly marginal. He was lightweight and so, ultimately, were Liverpool.

It captured City’s swagger, their sense of responding to what they regard as an injustice – that they maintain will be overturned on appeal – the sense they are going to continue to create an almighty headache for the Premier League. “Cheats,” loudly boomed around Anfield from the home fans before the PA played Fleetwood Mac’s Tell Me Lies at the final whistle, as the players walked off. Those signs of defiance were not matched on the pitch. Although it may be a song City will get used to hearing for the rest of this extraordinary, unprecedented campaign.

Enzo Maresca hailed Manchester City’s ability to “make our own noise” after their emphatic 3-0 win at Liverpool.

In the first fixture since being found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges laid against them for serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules, City made their statement on the pitch as they re-established a three-point lead at the top of the table.

“It was not easy for the players after the last two, three weeks, but they dealt with it very well,” Maresca, the head coach, said. “I said during the week we need to learn to deal with the outside noise because of the situation, because that will be there. But we have to make our own noise.

“Zero-three at Anfield away is a great result, for sure. I think all the organisation needs a win like this. It’s good for all [of] the club.”

Maresca said City will have to get used to such hostile occasions, with Liverpool fans making clear their anger over the judgment, and added: “All the away games are going to be with noise.”

Maresca confirmed that chief executive Ferran Soriano and director of football Hugo Viana had travelled on the team bus to Anfield in a sign of unity.

“Ferran was there, Hugo was there. We were all together,” Maresca said. “For the importance of the game, Liverpool away, Anfield away. It’s good to be together.”

The Italian claimed that despite the verdict, and the attention and uncertainty as to what will happen next, it had not affected his squad.

“The players just focus on the football. They are not thinking about the future,” he said. “It’s how we learn to deal with the noise. It’s our duty to make noise and to do that we win games. You cannot imagine how happy I am. Hopefully I am going to speak about this situation when we are going to win the appeal.”

The Liverpool boss told BBC MOTD: “I think the first part is that we played two different games. One until the red card, and then after. For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us.

“The first yellow card was just a kick in the toe. It was nothing. It was a normal foul. It was the moment when we were pushing more. The momentum was coming for us and the atmosphere in the stadium was so nice. We conceded very little in the first half. We did a really good job. The second half, we were translating into chances.

“You learn a lot in games like today. I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It’s a loss and we didn’t get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot.”

Gravenberch is bossing this game in midfield. Another powerful run from deep results in a delightful nutmeg on Fernandez, who slips over. Liverpool’s energy has been really impressive. City need to ride out this early storm.

It’s getting heated at Anfield! Mac Allister and Anderson clash sparking a scuffle between both sets of players. It threatened to boil over for a second, but the drama quickly calms down and play resumes after the referee has a word with the two captains.

Inflatable bananas to signify nostalgia for the late 1980s, when these were all the rage after the club’s relegation to Division Two? The Premier League reveals that City’s owners inflated “sham” sponsorship deals by £830.69m between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

It later amends the statement to “wherever wrongdoing is established”.

The UAE then warns Andy Burnham that it will pull billions of pounds of investment out of the UK in retaliation for the guilty verdict against City.

City argue that their sponsorship deals were part-funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club’s owners, in their appeal, which claims bank statements and witness accounts provide “irrefutable evidence” to support their case.

There were four days between the news leaking that Manchester City had been found guilty of the majority of charges first levelled at them by the Premier League in February 2023 and the independent commission findings dropping.

Staff, then, had had a bit of time to process a guilty verdict although little, it seems, could adequately prepare them for the excoriating tone and content of the commission’s ruling.

“The thing that has shocked me more than anything is the language the commission used to describe the club’s conduct,” one staff member told Telegraph Sport this week.

“We had been waiting for a very long time to see what came out of these Premier League charges and lots of different things go through your head. But I just wasn’t expecting that. I’m still a bit shell-shocked by the ferocity of what the commission said. I think that’s what’s worried me.”

Since City last kicked a football in anger, they have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges levelled at them by the Premier League in a verdict that has shaken professional football to its very core. The club have appealed and the extent of their punishment now rests with an independent panel. Until then, though, the show goes on and City’s players and staff must compete knowing that their every move now comes with a caveat.

City have put up a united front and on Thursday Maresca and Haaland duly delivered the party lines, the City head coach revealing that the feeling among his charges was “fantastic”. “[My players] know what we can control is the football side – they are not worried at all about different things,” Maresca said, before adding that he trusts the club “completely”. The Italian doubled down on his remarks in his Friday press conference.

City maintain their innocence and many of Maresca’s peers have remained tight-lipped on the case, though Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick admitted this week he has questions, while Régis Le Bris urged football’s governing bodies to be “relentless” in safeguarding competitive integrity.

Given all that has happened, it would be easy to forget that this is, for now, a top-of-the-table clash and has been one of the Premier League’s marquee rivalries since the days of Guardiola-Jürgen Klopp. Liverpool fans have never been ones to roll out the red carpet when City are in town, but the ill feeling and belligerence will only intensify at Anfield this time around owing to the events of the past weeks.

City are top of the league having won all five of their league matches so far, while Liverpool have huffed and puffed to sixth, remaining unbeaten.

Milan travel to the Greek capital hoping to get their Europa League campaign up and running. They have won just one of their opening four league phase fixtures, which was a 4-0 drubbing of RB Salzburg.

Defeats to Benfica, Bournemouth and Ferencvaros – all without scoring a single goal – have seen the Rossoneri slide into the bottom 12 positions in the table. With only 12 points up for grabs, they must start to put things right. By contrast, Olympiacos have won three of four, and sit sixth.

Jota Silva spoke to Gianluca Di Marzio about tonight’s game in Athens, admitting that the Rossoneri are a team that they respect despite their slow start in Europe. His words are via MilanNews.

“It will be a great match, between two teams that usually play in the Champions League. Milan are a well-equipped opponent with an extraordinary history: they are a team we all respect. We are two historic and important teams: they, like us, are having a good season.”

They only have three points in the Europa League…

“They will certainly want to fight to advance to the next round of the European competition. They have players of excellent quality, including many internationals and many highly experienced players. Amorim is a fantastic coach and needs no introduction.”

What’s your message for the fans, who will once again fill the stadium?

“As with every match, we promise to give it our all this time. We face a tough opponent. It’s another important match, and we have a very significant evening ahead of us. We want to finish the game with a win and get the three points.”

Having come through Inter’s youth academy, do you have any extra motivation for facing Milan?

Could this match also be a calling card for you for the Italian national team? Also, how much have Milan changed since you faced them with Inter?

“Considering that I’ve been here for almost three years and that my career is going well, I don’t see the match against Milan as a positive or negative opportunity for the national team.

What do you expect from Milan in tomorrow’s match, and how do you see them competing for the title?

“It will be a tough and intense match, with both teams pressing hard. I think it will be a very close game, and we’ll try to give our best. As for the league, everything is still open. We’re only at the start of the season, so I can’t give a precise assessment right now.”

#1489. Opinion: Liverpool given green light to sign £46m sensation

Liverpool have been linked with a lot of players over the last few years.

Over £600 million has been spent on them and, more change is still needed.

Obviously, this isn't the outcome that the Anfield outfit will have wanted but, it's the hand that they've seemingly been dealt.

All of their rivals are constantly looking for ways to upgrade their team and, the more that they manage to do this, the better they become and the more difficult they are to beat.

Fans expected Liverpool to be competing for silverware this term but, now that feels like it all rests on their transfer plans with the club now being handed a green light to sign one of their targets.

Barcelona want to sign Ayden Heaven which could give Liverpool the green light to sign Ronald Araujo

One of the main positions that Liverpool needed to upgrade in the 2026-27 transfer window was their defence.

Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate both exited Anfield for free and, the performances of Jeremie Frimpong and Conor Bradley were shoddy.

Throw in the fact that Bradley managed to suffer yet another long-term injury and, Liverpool were left with a bit-part defence.

That's why Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo were brought in.

Nobody knew how each defender would perform due to their lack of Premier League experience but, to the surprise of many, they've been two of the Reds' best players.

But, because Araujo is only on a season-long loan, his future is still undecided or, it was until this fresh update from BBC Sport.

"Fulham and Barcelona are among the clubs to have expressed an interest in Heaven, with both having tried to sign him when he decided to leave Arsenal," they wrote.

"The England U20s defender's preference is believed to be a loan move, though he would also entertain permanent offers.

"At United he has largely been used as a back-up option and, after enjoying a run in the team under former manager Ruben Amorim, he lost his place under Michael Carrick. He returned to the side only after an injury crisis hit the club last season.

"Heaven is also capable of playing at left-back and in midfield, but does not expect to be trusted as a regular starter amid the instability at Old Trafford, with the club 19th in the league.

"He is under contract until 2029 in a deal that includes an option for an extra year."

Ayden Heaven joining Barcelona could force Barcelona to sell Ronald Araujo

Araujo's versatility is one of the best things about him.

The defender can be comfortably used as a centre-back or a right-back with Iraola using him in both positions this term.

Indeed, the Uruguayan's injury history is a bit of a worry but, touch wood, he's managed to keep fit while playing for Liverpool so far.

As mentioned, Araujo's future isn't set in stone yet but, if Barca manage to sign Heaven from Manchester United, it feels like Araujo would fall further down Hansi Flick's plans.

This could mean that the La Liga giants are willing to negotiate a cheaper deal for the centre-back which, judging by the recent developments from Liverpool, is exactly what they want.

Here's hoping that a deal can be reached soon and that Barcelona find a successor for their captain soon.

#1487. CorSport: Cardinale goes ‘all-in’ – Milan’s strategy risky with squad costs already up €40m

Owner Gerry Cardinale is ready to put his money where his mouth is when it comes to building an AC Milan team that can win trophies.

Cardinale has already spoken publicly about his desire to strengthen the squad available to Ruben Amorim with some further reinforcements in January. While money will not be spent for the sake of it, the American seems infatuated by Endrick, and he certainly will not come cheap.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Corriere dello Sport (via PianetaMilan) confirm this morning that Milan are preparing for ‘significant investment’ in the January window, but they also take a look at the Rossoneri’s financial situation, trying to determine whether these costs are sustainable.

Looking at the summer transfer window, €160m was invested on incomings with the club-record signing of Goncalo Ramos as well as the additions of Mario Gila and Diego Moreira. Another €70m could be spent in the winter on Endrick, making it €230m in 2026-27.

Then, two renewals were closed, while work is still underway for Adrien Rabiot. Christian Pulisic went from €3.5m to €5m net per season, while Strahinja Pavlovic went from €1.7m to €3m net per season.

As the newspaper reports, the cost of the squad has already increased by €40m this season. With these investments and without any major sales, the 2026-27 budget could close with a deficit of €140-150m.

The club have room to keep the squad ratio under control, but sporting results will be needed to support it. Otherwise, there’s a risk of ending up under another Settlement Agreement with UEFA, which brings further constraints.

A full-back and centre-back have been tipped to arrive too, which would make things even more precarious. Corriere dello Sport conclude that Cardinale’s move is risky, and it will require almost guaranteed Champions League qualification for the year.

#1486. Ipswich Town vs Aston Villa - prediction, team news, lineups

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 19:00, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:36

Aston Villa travel to Portman Road to face Ipswich Town on Saturday evening seeking to climb back into the top half of the Premier League table.

Both meetings between these two sides during the 2024-25 season ended in entertaining draws (2-2 in Suffolk and 1-1 at Villa Park), leaving the Tractor Boys still searching for their first top-flight triumph over the Lions since February 1993.

Tipped by many to struggle before the season began, Ipswich are yet to spend a single day sitting in the Premier League relegation zone since securing promotion, but their recent form has seen them slip closer to the bottom three.

After winning three of their first six top-flight games this term (L3), the Tractor Boys have failed to come out on top in any of their last five fixtures (D2 L3), suffering defeats to Bournemouth (2-1) and Tottenham (2-0) either side of the international break.

Gary O'Neil acknowledged that his team “didn't get to our level enough” against Spurs and they now sit down in 16th place in the table, just two points above the drop zone with games against Villa, Coventry City, Leeds United, Newcastle United and Brighton & Hove Albion up next.

Another “soft” goal was conceded by Ipswich last time out, and they have now shipped a total of 22 goals in 11 Premier League matches – the third-most in the division – while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in each of their last 30 top-flight games; only West Brom between August 2010 and May 2011 have endured a longer run in the division’s history (34 games).

Ipswich have also proved largely incapable of mounting second-half comebacks, failing to win any of the 22 Premier League matches in which they have trailed at half time since the start of the 2024-25 season (D3 L19). Striking first on Saturday could therefore be crucial for O'Neil’s side as they bid to upset Villa.

Since securing a 2-1 home victory over Man City on October 24, Aston Villa have failed to win any of their last six matches in all competitions (D3 L3), suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday.

Unai Emery’s side previously played out a frustrating goalless stalemate at home to Sunderland in the Premier League, their third top-flight draw in a row that leaves them sitting 12th in the table and seven points behind fourth spot where they finished last season.

Villa – who have not drawn four consecutive Premier League matches since September 2011 – are preparing for a historic milestone on Saturday, as they play their 5,000th match across the top-four tiers of English football (W2,050 D1,199 L1,750), becoming the 16th club to reach the landmark.

Emery is keen to see his team rediscover their clinical touch in front of goal sooner rather than later, as Villa have failed to score in four of their last six games, not registering a single shot on target against Galatasaray.

Heading into Saturday’s clash in Suffolk, Villa have not lost any of their last 10 visits to Ipswich (D6 L3) in all competitions (W5 D4) since a 1-0 EFL Cup loss back in December 1992, while they are unbeaten in all 22 of their league matches against promoted sides under Emery (W15 D7).

Ipswich left-back Leif Davis has emerged as a doubt after he was forced off with an ankle injury in the defeat at Spurs. O'Neil has no other first-team injury concerns, though.

Abdoul Ouattara could be tasked with filling in at left-back if Davis is unable to feature, with either Darnell Furlong or Dara O'Shea starting at right-back in a four-man defence.

Zian Flemming was handed his first league start for Ipswich last time out, but he could be replaced up front by Emersonn, while Abdul Fatawu, Florentino Luis, Jack Clarke and Jacob Greaves will also be pushing to start after beginning as substitutes last weekend.

As for Aston Villa, Amadou Onana (knee) and Matteo Ruggeri (hamstring) remain sidelined through injury, while Matty Cash (concussion) will be assessed ahead of kickoff.

If Cash misses out, Aaron Wan-Bissaka will likely battle with Taylor Harwood-Bellis for a start at right-back, while Pau Torres is expected to be recalled at centre-back at the expense of former Ipswich man Tyrone Mings.

With Alejandro Garnacho facing an uncertain future at Villa, Emery is likely to favour Alysson and Johan Manzambi in wide positions, providing support in attack for striker Nicolas Jackson who has netted six goals in 10 Premier League games this season.

Walton; O'Shea, Diop, Greaves, Ouattara; Lukic, Palacios; Clarke, Enciso, Maeda; Emersonn

Suzuki; Harwood-Bellis, Lindelof, Torres, Maatsen; Kamara, Goretzka; Alysson, McGinn, Manzambi; Jackson

While Portman Road remains a far more forgiving environment for O'Neil’s side, who have collected seven of their 11 points on home soil this term (W2 D1 L2), Villa should relish the opportunity to rediscover their scoring touch against a porous Ipswich defence shipping an average of two goals per game.

Although the Tractor Boys are capable of keeping things competitive in Suffolk, we are backing Emery’s men to shake off their recent slump and grind out a hard-fought victory.

#1485. This is going to hurt: Liverpool reportedly preparing for massive departure

Liverpool are preparing for a massive departure that will change the side dramatically. This one is going to hurt.

Liverpool have said goodbye to a series of legends over the last few years. It really started in 2021 when Gini Wijnaldum left for Paris Saint-Germain and then Sadio Mane decided to leave for Bayern Munich a year later. Slowly but surely, Jürgen Klopp's team has disappeared.

Jordan Henderson, Roberto Firmino and Fabinho left in 2023. Klopp himself left in 2024, as did Joel Matip and Thiago. 2025 was a big one - Trent Alexander-Arnold joined Real Madrid. Then things got even more heartbreaking in 2026 as Mohamed Salah, Andy Robertson and Ibrahima Konate departed.

Salah's exit was arguably the most difficult of the lot. That was the biggest sign that things had moved on - the icon of Klopp's team deciding it was time to leave.

And now 2027 awaits and things are set to continue down the same path. The final stars of that great side have expiring contracts and it increasingly looks like it's time to say goodbye.

Liverpool are reportedly preparing the exit of Alisson Becker, whose contract will expire at the end of the campaign. Alisson's deal was due to end in 2026 but the Reds triggered an option to extend it by a year.

Juventus did try to get a deal done last summer regardless of that, offering a minimal fee to Liverpool. Nothing came of it, however, as no one at the Reds seemed keen to sell the Brazilian.

But Alisson may leave next year. Liverpool won't want him to go but offering a new contract to a goalkeeper with his injury history feels like a big risk. A risk they may not want to take if other options are available.

Of course, 'other options' of Alisson's calibre are few and far between. L'Equipe, though, understand that Liverpool have found one. They're eyeing Robin Risser of RC Lens, who was voted the best in Ligue 1 last season.

The 21-year-old is being discussed at Anfield internally as a potential option should Alisson leave. It's the first real sign we've had that the club are very much open to moving on from arguably their greatest-ever goalkeeper.

But we wonder if that could change because of Risser. There's intense competition for him and if he picks somewhere else, we imagine Liverpool will 'settle' for renewing Alisson's deal.

It's very much wait and see, then, but the Reds are certainly preparing for Alisson's exit.

#1483. 'Moments aren't enough': Inside Ethan Nwaneri's struggles on loan at Borussia Dortmund ahead of his return to the Emirates tonight - as Arsenal face dilemma over talented youngster suffering crisis of confidence

Published: 21:00 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:27 EST, 24 November 2026

Despite being shipped off to Germany’s finest finishing school for young English talent, Ethan Nwaneri’s time at Borussia Dortmund is already at a crossroads.

The 19-year-old joined the Bundesliga side on a season-long loan in September after enduring a frustrating five-month spell at Marseille earlier in the year.

This was supposed to be the loan move to reinvigorate one of England’s best young forwards, at a club well-versed in doing exactly that.

Nwaneri became the fifth Englishman aged 21 or under to sign for Dortmund in the past decade, following in the footsteps of Jadon Sancho, Jude and Jobe Bellingham, and Jamie Gittens. The stars seemed aligned for Nwaneri to shine.

But the opposite has happened. Having impressed and forced a Hoffenheim own goal off the bench on his Dortmund debut, Nwaneri started the team’s next four Bundesliga matches, but was hooked off around the hour mark in each one. The teenager has not made a starting XI since a goalless draw with Union Berlin on October 17.

It is understood Arsenal – who host Dortmund in the Champions League tonight – are closely monitoring the situation around Nwaneri’s lack of minutes, and there is a January recall clause in his contract. The clause was initially inserted as insurance in case an attacking injury crisis arose at Arsenal. Nwaneri's lack of minutes wasn't expected.

Ethan Nwaneri is on loan at Borussia Dortmund from Arsenal but has struggled for minutes – he last started a match on October 17

The 19-year-old is one of the most talented youngsters to emerge from Arsenal's prolific Hale End academy, but his career is in danger of stalling on loan in Germany

So why isn’t his move at Dortmund, a club that made their name by developing young players, working out?

Well, Nwaneri's short career so far has been a complicated one, featuring enormous highs and challenging hurdles. To understand his trajectory, you have to look back at his time at Hale End.

Having risen through the academy rapidly upon joining aged eight, Nwaneri burst onto the first-team scene in September 2022 against Brentford, becoming the youngest player to appear in the Premier League, aged 15 years and 181 days.

Mikel Arteta still values the player but hinted on Monday that he needs to produce more than just ‘moments’.

‘You can have patches, but to find that consistency and to play a big amount of minutes and have a huge impact in big football clubs like Arsenal or Dortmund, it's extremely difficult,’ he said.

‘That's the reality. You can just shine in moments, but moments are not enough. Now you need to show the consistency. Ethan has the capacity and the mentality to do that, and it takes some time.’

There's a feeling at Arsenal that Nwaneri has time on his side and shouldn’t be written off. He signed a five-year deal in August 2025 after all, with a plan to fully integrate the attacker into the first-team squad. His brother Emerson, 16, is thriving with the Under 18s.

However, if Nwaneri were to be sold in future, he would, as an academy graduate, generate pure profit on Arsenal's accounts.

‘His time at Borussia has been a disappointment so far because he was brought in to help immediately after Giannis Konstantelias tore his ACL,’ says Sebastian Wessling, who has covered Dortmund for 15 years at the Funke Media Group.

‘They tried to bring Nwaneri in, the summer before. So having tracked and spoken to him previously, they thought he would be ideal for short-term help. But he really hasn’t been that, it’s not worked out well so far.

‘He’s found it difficult to contribute with goals, assists, or just generally in Dortmund’s offensive game.

‘What the coach is looking for is a player to make a lot of runs in behind. Whereas Nwaneri looks to drop deep and have time on the ball, which the manager, Niko Kovac, isn’t looking for.’

'He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play,' says Dortmund expert Sebastian Wessling of Nwaneri

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week

Nwaneri's lack of confidence and progress feel striking. This summer, he joined England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida, and was an unused substitute in the warm-up match against New Zealand. Nwaneri was alongside Bournemouth's Alex Scott, Fulham's Josh King and Liverpool's Rio Ngumoha – both Scott and Ngumoha have since made their senior England debuts, while King made Thomas Tuchel's squad this month. All three are flourishing as Nwaneri struggles to even feature.

To make matters worse for him, back at Arsenal 16-year-old Max Dowman is competing for a place in the starting XI. Nwaneri may have bundles of talent, but he is yet to fully kick on.

Wessling adds: ‘He lacks confidence and I think that shows in his play. Niko wants him to be brave on the pitch, but he plays it very safe.

‘When he did feature, he often played short passes and didn’t advance Dortmund’s play. He’s not a total disappointment, but he hasn’t really contributed.’

There is still a serious player in Nwaneri, as seen in his two assists for England Under 21s in their 3-2 victory over France last week. He is eligible to feature at the Emirates tonight, and will be desperate to show Arsenal what they are missing.

In any case, his next two months at Dortmund will reveal plenty about his future. It’s now about consistency – more than mere ‘moments’.

#1481. Leeds vs. Coventry: Head-to-head record and past meetings

By Oliver Thomas | 26 Nov 2026 19:15, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 21:15

Elland Road will stage Saturday afternoon's Premier League contest between Leeds United and Coventry City.

Both teams enter this fixture after picking up maximum points last weekend, with Daniel Farke's side securing an impressive 4-1 victory at Chelsea and Frank Lampard's men beating Crystal Palace 3-2 on home soil.

Leeds have climbed to seventh in the Premier League table after 11 matches, while Coventry currently sit 14th and three points above the relegation zone.

Here, Sports Mole takes an in-depth look at the head-to-head record and previous meetings between the two sides.

Leeds United and Coventry City have faced each other a total of 87 times across all competitions, and it is the Whites who lead the head-to-head record with 45 wins to the Sky Blues' 19, while 23 draws have also been played out.

November 1920 was the first time these two sides butted heads in the old Division Two, with both teams sharing the spoils in a 1-1 draw on Coventry's turf. Leeds responded with a thumping 4-0 home victory in the reverse fixture just a month later, but the Sky Blues got their revenge almost two years later with a slender 1-0 home success.

Leeds won 11 of their 18 Division Two encounters with Coventry (D2 L5), before both teams locked horns in Division One for the first time in November 1967, with a 1-1 draw played out at Elland Road.

The Whites then enjoyed a eight-game winning league run over Coventry up until October 1971 when they lost 3-1 away from home. Leeds responded by putting together a run of nine games unbeaten before the Sky Blues did the double over the West Yorkshire outfit in the 1976-77 campaign, winning 4-2 at home and 2-1 away.

Coventry's fortunes against Leeds improved between the late 1970s and late 1990s, posting five wins and seven draws in 17 games across all competitions (L5).

In the Premier League era (since 1992-92), Leeds and Coventry have faced each other 18 times in the top division of English football, with the Whites winning eight and the Sky Blues winning only three, with seven draws also recorded.

Coventry won two of their three Premier League meetings in the same season, with a 2-1 home victory in September 1996 followed three months later by a 3-1 away victory, courtesy of goals from Darren Huckerby, Dion Dublin and Gary McAllister.

These two wins for Coventry were part of a five-match winless Premier League run for Leeds in this fixture, but they have since won four and drawn two of their last six top-flight battles with the Sky Blues up until January 2001 (a 1-0 home win for Leeds in which Robbie Keane haunted his former club with the only goal of the game).

Each of the last 14 meetings between Leeds and Coventry have been in the Championship, with Leeds winning eight of those (D3 L3) including home (3-0) and away (2-0) victories in the 2024-25 season en route to securing promotion as champions under Daniel Farke.

#1479. Senne Lammens' Man United future called into doubt following Champions League clanger

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:37, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:39

Manchester United could look to bring in competition for number one goalkeeper Senne Lammens next year, according to former Red Devils captain Ashley Young.

Lammens has made a series of mistakes in recent matches and has only managed to keep one clean sheet for the Red Devils this season.

The Belgium international conceded a penalty against Sporting Lisbon in the Champions League on Wednesday evening and then dropped a clanger late on to allow Luis Suarez to make it 2-2 in Portugal.

Lammens also made a high-profile mistake for Belgium at the 2026 World Cup against Spain, and Young has said that the 24-year-old may be on the verge of being dropped.

Young has even suggested that Man United could look to bring in competition for Lammens next year if his struggles continue.

"You look at the World Cup and the mistake he made, it's effected him massively. You just see it's mistake after mistake after mistake. He could be one mistake away from being dropped," Young told BBC Sport. "You've got Karl Darlow and Tom Heaton that are not really going to push Senne Lammens for that No.1 jersey, I do think Mauricio Pochettino is going to look and think 'If I can one of the keepers out of the door, and get someone in January to be pushing Lammens, then I will be doing that'. There's far too many mistakes."

Man United head coach Mauricio Pochettino refused to criticise Lammens after the clash with Sporting despite the goalkeeper's unconvincing performance.

"This type of thing happens. That is football. Football is about making mistakes," Pochettino told reporters when asked about Lammens.

"I always want to support my player. I think we need to talk about responsibility. In this type of action our defensive line needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult.

"It's not to blame the defensive line, but it's two things that we need to improve - details that we need to work on. We need to manage his type of situation better."

Lammens arrived at Man United from Club Brugge in the summer of 2025, and he has represented the Red Devils on 49 occasions, conceding 74 goals and keeping just nine clean sheets.

The Belgian is expected to keep his spot between the sticks for Man United's Premier League clash with Brentford on Saturday afternoon.

#1478. Opinion: Liverpool will sign perfect player for Andoni Iraola, he'll only cost £19m

Andoni Iraola has done a pretty decent job since being appointed as Liverpool's manager.

He's managed to get his team to fourth in the Premier League table with only seven points separating them from first-placed Arsenal.

Obviously, this is still a decent number of points to chip away at but, if the Gunners continue dropping points by drawing games against teams such as Newcastle, the Reds could find themselves back in the title race soon.

Nobody knows what lies ahead for any team but, if Liverpool manage to pull off even half of the transfers they've been linked with, they'll be storming their way up the table.

And to make things even sweeter, the perfect signing for Iraola has just emerged.

Arhcie Brown has a £19.2 million release clause in his contract

So many areas among Liverpool's ranks still need upgrading.

This is a horrible thing to write as, across the last couple of years, well over £600 million has been spent on new players by the Reds.

Some of the transfers that they've made have worked out for the better but, others haven't quite hit the mark.

Milos Kerkez is an example of this because, even though he has had a fair few decent performances, his inconsistency is terrible.

Some days he can be seen as the Premier League's best left-back and, on others, he could end up being the worst player on the pitch.

This has forced fans to ask for a new left-back with Florian Plettenberg now sharing a rather intriguing update on Liverpool target, Archie Brown.

"Archie Brown has a release clause worth around €23m, valid for both the winter and summer transfer windows. The 23 y/o is a regular starter at Fenerbahçe and has also impressed with some very strong performances in the Champions League," he wrote.

"Under contract until 2028, a move is planned, with Premier League clubs already making enquiries."

Archie Brown would fit straight into Andoni Iraola's plans

Not only would Brown be classed as homegrown but, he'd also be one of the cheapest transfers on the market.

Recent links with Liverpool and Alejandro Balde have emerged with Barcelona demanding close to €50 million for the Spaniard.

Others such as Daniel Svensson have also been linked with a move but, again, Borussia Dortmund want over €40 million for him.

Each of these players would be exceptional additions but, Brown for €23 million (£19 million) is a deal that's too good to pass up.

He put in the performance of a lifetime when Liverpool faced Fenerbahce earlier in the season and, if he can replicate that form in the Premier League, the Reds would be onto a winner.

Liverpool signing Brown would also give Kerkez a genuine challenger for his position which might even help him develop his performance.

Since the price for Brown is so good, Liverpool will have to act fast and get straight on with securing his services when the January transfer window opens up, otherwise, they'll end up kicking themselves for missing out on it.

#1477. Inzaghi recalls beating Liverpool in Athens and ’emotional’ affection from Milan fans

In the hearts and minds of AC Milan fans around the world, Pippo Inzaghi’s name is inseparably linked to Athens.

Inzaghi gave Milan their seventh Champions League title on 23 May 2007 in the Greek capital with a brace that swept Liverpool aside. The first goal was an Andrea Pirlo free-kick that he deflected in, the second an assist from Kaka that he rounded Pepe Reina from and slotted in.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It was he who allowed the Rossoneri to take their long-awaited and long-desired revenge on the Reds after the Istanbul defeat two years earlier. That feat – at the Spyros Louis Olympic Stadium and not at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium – has remained in the minds of all Milan fans.

It is the most recent of the Champions League titles raised to the sky, and while Inzaghi’s mind is on finishing the job with Palermo (top of Serie B), he will watch his old side on TV tonight. The former striker spoke to La Gazzetta dello Sport.

Dor you and for Milan, thinking back to Athens is never trivial…

“Absolutely. In Athens I experienced one of the most important nights of my career, so it’s a city I associate with special memories and that’s why it will always remain close to my heart.”

Tell us three memories from that game. Let’s start with a pre-match one…

“The anticipation of the match: I knew how important that final was and I felt it could be a special evening.”

“The highlight was, of course, the second goal. A moment later, I realised the cup was really close.”

“After that final, I didn’t sleep for ten days. I woke up in the middle of the night thinking that victory with my goals had been a dream.”

Given what that cup represented, that is, the famous ‘after Istanbul, there’s always Athens’ that was printed on the back of AC Milan’s second shirt this season, is the 2006-07 Champions League a joy comparable to Italy’s World Cup victory in Berlin a few months earlier?

“They’re two different memories because they’ve both enriched my footballing life. Winning the World Cup is the ultimate accolade for any footballer.

“Athens, however, also had a special meaning for Milan’s history: we were coming off a disappointment that I’d experienced from the outside, from the stands [he was injured] and I could finally be on the pitch to contribute to the victory.

“Fate gave me a second chance, and it went as you all know… However, I wouldn’t rank the two nights of glory because I carry them with me in different ways.”

Before Milan-Atalanta, when you came to San Siro, you understood from the huge applause and chants how much the Rossoneri fans still love you and you said: “Every time I come back here it’s like it’s the first time.”

“Returning to San Siro and feeling that affection was truly emotional for me, especially because it was the first time for my son Edoardo, who is now five years old.”

What does it mean to you, years after leaving AC Milan as a player and the 2014-15 season in which you were the coach, to still be so loved by the fans?

“I spent extraordinary years at Milan: the bond with the fans was born from goals, victories, but also from the commitment I always tried to put in. Knowing that all this has gone down in history is a priceless gift.”

What do you hope for Milan on their return to Athens tonight, needing a win given their position in the Europa League table?

“I hope we can face the match with character and return home having experienced a great European night. I know how much that shirt means and how much the fans expect from a match like this. I hope the team can give them joy and a victory.”
