#1476. Man United must build on improved Sporting Lisbon display in vital Premier League clash with Brentford

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 19:51, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 19:55

Manchester United will continue their Premier League campaign against Brentford on Saturday afternoon, and Sports Mole's Football Editor Matt Law has discussed all of the latest talking points surrounding the 20-time English champions.

Man United conceded the most goals, 36, the most penalties, five, and the most red cards, five, of any Premier League team this season.

The Liverpool game was controversial as well, with the red card for Leny Yoro that has since been rescinded. Isak does not have even a little bit of control of the ball. He has ballooned it 10 metres in front of him, and still, he is given the red card for that one.

That was a huge turning moment in the game. That is not to say that United should be going on and losing 4-0 at Anfield, even with 10 men, but it is a game-changing incident.

It leaves United on one Premier League win this season, down in 19th spot in the table, eight points from 11 games, which is absolutely horrendous. What I would say is it was a tough start for Pochettino. It was a big game at Anfield against the Liverpool side that played well.

If you concede that red card and then the fact they score from the free kick, that is a real hammer blow, and then you have to hold on and try to keep it 1-0 going into the second half.

United could not do that. The performance level was well off it again. They conceded four goals in each of their last two Premier League games. It is 23 goals conceded now in the Premier League in 11 games.

This team just cannot keep clean sheets for love nor money, in the Premier League, in any competition. Not kept a clean sheet since the win over Sabah in the Champions League, their first Champions League game in the league phase.

If you keep a clean sheet, you have got a really good chance of winning football games. If you concede two a game, three a game, you are just not going to pick up wins.

The game against Sporting Lisbon was one we could do a two-hour podcast on. The first penalty against Sporting is very soft.

If that is a penalty then we might as well pack up and do podcasts on something else, because I do not want to be a part of a game that says that is a penalty. The Senne Lammens one is a penalty. What is he doing? He is flying out.

Then the goal that was disallowed for Amad, how that is a foul from Tielemans I will never know. An absolute horrific decision. The Fernandes penalty is a penalty for me.

I think it is a straightforward decision. I do not think it is a foul on Senne Lammens, and I also do not think it is a foul for the last goal.

Dorgu got penalised for jumping into the goalkeeper, but they are either both fouls or neither are fouls. The contact on Senne Lammens for the Sporting equaliser was soft. I do not think that should be disallowed.

I do not think the United goal should be disallowed. The late red card was clumsy from Tielemans. It is not vintage football, it is not vintage Man United. They struggled in the final third of the field. Zirkzee came into the side and did okay.

An interesting stat from that game was that United had 12 high turnovers against Sporting, their most in any game this season.

It did feel like they were winning the ball back higher. They were definitely pressing more as a unit. The shape of the team was better. They need a centre forward. If they had had Sesko last night and that threat in behind, you feel like they could have picked up all three points.

They were decent on the ball, recovered well from going behind in the game. Sporting are a good side and have had good results in the Champions League this season.

They are a really strong team with really good players. There were positives from the Sporting Lisbon game, and it leaves them in a decent enough position in the Champions League.

They need to beat Leipzig in the next European game if they are really going to push on. They have got Bayern Munich and Villarreal as well, and those are going to be difficult games.

From the Champions League point of view, I still think they are in a decent enough position to finish in, whether that is the automatic qualification places or ultimately the play-offs.

Dealing with the Premier League is where they need to focus. They have got three games in a row now before the Leipzig game: Brentford, Newcastle away, Coventry at home.

The next two home games are absolutely massive. If they get turned over here and then go to Newcastle and do not manage to get a win, and then Coventry pick something up against them, it is very difficult.

I do not think United are getting relegated this season. I say that out of hope. I think they are going to be busy in January. They are going to have to be inventive.

Around £50m is the figure they are going to have to spend. They need to bring in three players: definitely a striker, definitely a centre-back, definitely a full-back.

Carlos Baleba is going to be back sooner than expected. They are going to hope to get Rashford back at some stage in the not-too-distant future. Those two did train in the gym ahead of the Sporting game. Shaw was back on the bench as well.

Pochettino said he was proud of his players for their performance level in the Sporting game and for overcoming the adversity, because there were some really horrific decisions from the referee and VAR in that game.

United have not had the rub of the green. With the Fernandes goal and the divot, they showed the earlier clip and it was Fernandes himself who had made that divot in the turf.

He had had a heavy touch with his boot in the box, and they circled back and it was the one he had made. So he actually managed to assist himself with that bobble. There has been a lot that has gone against United this season.

This is a really big game on Saturday afternoon and one I am hoping they can win against Brentford. First Premier League win for Pochettino. Go to the Newcastle game, can you get a point? Can you go there and beat Coventry? Can you beat Leipzig? Football changes very quickly. If you put three or four good results together, everyone feels different.

It goes in cycles. A big football match. Brentford, it is one of those games that back in the day, United at home to Brentford, you would think it is a gimme, a home win.

But they are an excellent team, Brentford, sitting sixth in the table at the moment with 17 points. Going away from home brings its different challenges, and without Igor Thiago as well is a big one.

I did also want to mention Senne Lammens' form, which is a concern for me.

Going back to the middle of September, Paul Scholes said in a podcast, The Good, The Bad and the Football, that he questioned whether Lammens was good enough, at a stage when he was actually playing quite well.

And I have to be honest, I am in that camp now. He is making a lot of mistakes.

There was one in the Sporting game last night where they did not concede from it, but he pushed the ball back into the middle and no one was on the rebound to put it away. The mistake for the second goal was a big one as well.

His form is slightly concerning and his confidence looks shot at the moment. I think he starts here, but it will be interesting to see whether United ultimately think they might have to get another goalkeeper in at some stage.

#1475. Meet the world's most famous pub team: How a Sex Pistol, Superman and Vinnie Jones took Hollywood United  beyond Sunset Boulevard via private jet - and even rubbed shoulders with David Beckham's LA Galaxy

Published: 09:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 12:29 EST, 24 November 2026

They had a World Cup winner in defence, Superman in their squad and a Sex Pistol in charge of recruitment.

There's a clue in the name, but Hollywood United must have been the wildest, most star-studded pub football team of all time.

Ray Winstone, Jason Statham, Mike Myers and Vinnie Jones all turned out for a team that grew out of a gathering of British expats at the Cat & Fiddle pub in the late Eighties.

It being Hollywood, they travelled to matches by private jet and they even took on David Beckham in a charity match.

Now, as the Sex Pistols prepare to embark on a tour marking the 50th anniversary of their debut single, guitarist Steve Jones has revealed how he assembled the extraordinary side on Hollywood's Sunset Boulevard.

Among those who pulled on the shirt were France's World Cup-winning defender Frank Leboeuf, former Scotland captain Richard Gough and Brandon Routh, the American actor who played the superhero in the 2006 film Superman Returns.

Routh was given no special treatment by his team-mates, who would mockingly shout ‘Superman!’ whenever he made a mistake.

Hollywood United is the world's most famous pub team - featuring a littany of high-profile stars

Created by British expat and Sex Pistols star Steve Jones (right), United have rubbed shoulders with the likes of David Beckham

Vinnie Jones, meanwhile, had apparently lost none of the competitive instincts that characterised his career in English football.

In 2002, it was reported that he had been sent off just 15 seconds after coming on as a substitute in a Hollywood United friendly.

Anthony LaPaglia, the Australian actor who starred in the hit television series Without a Trace, was their goalkeeper.

There were members of the Sex Pistols, The Cult and Def Leppard, as well as actors such as Ralf Little.

But there were also rather less celebrated footballers.

‘The start of it was with me and Anthony LaPaglia; he was a goalie, and from there it turned into Hollywood United,’ Jones told the Telegraph.

‘We always used to play in a league with a bunch of regular blokes, carpenters and so on, then we got a few more faces who wanted to start kicking about with us like Vinnie Jones.’

The two Joneses met in a video shop in Los Angeles and the former Wimbledon hardman, who had embarked on a film career with Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, needed little persuasion to join.

‘He was up for a laugh, and he knows where to put a ball. Most of the team were amateurs, but we were decent and reached a certain level.’

In November 2007, Hollywood United took on Beckham's LA Galaxy in a charity match.

England manager Steve McClaren had flown to California to assess Beckham's fitness ahead of a European Championship qualifier against Croatia. It's not clear whether he attended the match, which Hollywood United lost 12-4. Beckham scored twice, as did Leboeuf and over 5,000 spectators raised more than $100,000 for victims of the California wildfires.

Steve Jones, now 71, had himself broken one of football's golden rules by changing his allegiance.

Vinnie Jones (left) and Ray Winstone (right) have turned out for the amateur football team

Actor Anthony LaPaglia lets the team travel on his private jet to matches across America

Having followed QPR as a schoolboy in west London and also been associated with Fulham, he became a Chelsea supporter after moving to California and getting sober.

Chelsea's games were available on American television and his lifelong friend and fellow Sex Pistol Paul Cook was already a diehard Blues fan.

Hollywood United played at Griffith Park, beneath the famous Hollywood sign, but their adventures would take them considerably further afield.

LaPaglia would arrange private jets to transport the players to matches.

Gough recalls one trip when the team flew to Vancouver for a charity match before heading straight to the Mexican resort of Puerto Vallarta to play a side of former Mexico internationals.

Vinnie Jones also told the Guardian in 2007 that Hollywood United had fielded nine former international footballers in a single match.

The club's ranks included former Liverpool and Newcastle defender Barry Venison and United States internationals Alexi Lalas and Eric Wynalda.

Winstone, a lifelong West Ham fan, found playing in the Californian heat rather more demanding than he had anticipated.

He later recalled being so exhausted by the time the ball reached him that he was barely able to kick it. And he wasn't particularly impressed by the willingness of former Chelsea defender Leboeuf to pass the ball, describing the Frenchman as a greedy player.

Among those watching from the touchline was the actor John Hurt, who was in town filming Indiana Jones and the Kingdom of the Crystal Skull with Winstone.

Some of the rock stars had impressive footballing pedigrees.

Ian Astbury, the lead singer of The Cult, had played boys' club football in Glasgow alongside future Everton and Scotland striker Graeme Sharp.

Gough, meanwhile, struck up a conversation with a team-mate from Northern Ireland without having the slightest idea he was Vivian Campbell, the guitarist of Def Leppard.

Sex Pistol Jones, who has lived in Los Angeles for more than 40 years, is returning to Britain next month for a tour marking the 50th anniversary of the release of Anarchy in the UK.

He still regularly attends football matches whenever he is back in England, although he has little time for the corporate hospitality enjoyed by many of his celebrity contemporaries.

‘I don't care where I sit, but I'm not interested in sitting in some box with a bunch of t***ers.’

#1474. Opinion: Julian Ward will be forced to change Liverpool's transfer plans

Julian Ward has a lot of decisions to make ahead of his first transfer window as Liverpool's new sporting director.

The Englishman took over from Richard Hughes as the Reds' new director after Hughes chose to seek pastures new and join Al-Hilal.

Hughes has spent the most money of any Liverpool sporting director ever and, the Reds still need to add more new players to their ranks.

It's unclear whether this is because of all the changes at Anfield or if it's because of another reason.

But, if Ward thought his job was going to be easy, he can think again as he may already be forced to change his winter transfer plans.

Victor Munoz's injury could massively hurt Liverpool

Liverpool's attack was one of the main areas that they focused on improving this summer.

Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz were brought in for a combined total worth over £150 million.

And, while both players have had their moments, it still feels like Liverpool could do with adding another player or two to their ranks.

But, since there are also many other areas among their first-team squad that also need changing, it didn't really feel like any deals for attackers were going to occur in January.

However, Munoz was unfortunately forced off the pitch during the Reds' 3-0 win against Club Brugge on Wednesday evening.

So, depending on how long he's out for, the Reds may need to turn their transfer plans upside down and add another attacker to their ranks.

Liverpool will be hoping that Victor Munoz isn't out for too long

Recently, Munoz has been finding his feet at Anfield.

The attacker was clearly brought in during the summer transfer window to be a back-up.

He only cost the club around £35 million which, in this day and age, is a steal.

His initial performances weren't all that great but, over the last couple of weeks, he's got himself into a purple patch of form with his blistering pace being one of his best assets.

In addition to this, Munoz is only 23 years old so, he still has a lot of his career ahead of him which means that he's probably going to get better.

So, a long-term injury is definitely not what he needs right now.

Nobody knows exactly what has happened to the Spaniard yet but, the Reds will certainly be hoping that it's nothing too serious.

#1472. Painful Coventry defeat will send shudder of fear through Newcastle

Newcastle United suffered a painful, chastening defeat, comprehensively beaten by Coventry City in a performance that should send a shudder of fear through Tyneside.

It was a dreadful night for the visitors, who conceded four goals for the second successive away game. The manner in which they fell apart was damning. Whatever the supposed style of play, it is not good to watch: long balls are pumped forward for short strikers to chase or compete for in the air against far taller centre-backs. Away from home, it is becoming ineffective.

Newcastle are too easy to create chances against and there is not much that gets you excited when they attack.

Matthias Jaissle’s side did create chances against Coventry, but are not clinical and do not inspire confidence they can be with the players they have. Defensively, they escaped earlier in the season, but are now being exposed and punished. “Not good enough in both boxes,” was Jaissle’s blunt verdict. “To concede eight goals in two away games is not good enough.”

Matthias Jaissle on this evening's defeat at the Coventry Building Society Arena. https://t.co/216NW6Laz8

Newcastle’s misery was in stark contrast to the joyous celebrations from Coventry. This was a thoroughly deserved first home win of the season for Frank Lampard’s side.

“It was an outstanding performance,” the manager said. “We knew we would have to suffer at times against a team like Newcastle. But we were really good at the basics, winning the second balls, winning the duels, those moments are critical. It’s not always about pretty patterns, it’s about work ethic.”

The win lifts Coventry level on points with Manchester United and will give them fresh confidence at this level. This could be the start of something special for them.

As for Newcastle, this raises uncomfortable questions about their summer recruitment, with so many expensive players on the bench or playing badly. It also means people will query whether Jaissle’s implementation of “vertical football” is working. The fact Lampard talked so openly about winning the duels to set up the win will anger the German.

Jaissle can point to two bad misses from one of the new arrivals, Matias Fernandez-Pardo, a £51m buy from Lille, in the first half. But his team are too easy to play through and the defence is an accident waiting to happen.

Even after Sven Botman’s stunning strike offered them a way back into the game, they capitulated at the back as Lewis Hall – who was off colour all evening – and Joelinton’s mistakes gift-wrapped a third for Ellis Simms. A fourth followed for Stephen Mfuni.

Ellis Simms off the bench with a big impact! 💥 https://t.co/XynFVxwERV

You can get a sense of what sort of mode a team are in within the first few passages of play and Newcastle were not sharp or precise. It was sloppy.

That was certainly true of goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who was off his line in no-man’s land trying to snuff out a through ball that he was not going to get. He stood up to deflect it away, but then rashly chased after it, diving at full stretch at the feet of Coventry’s Sidiki Cherif and failing to get the ball. Jack Rudoni coolly sent the Czech goalkeeper the wrong way from the spot.

Newcastle had been awful in their last away game at Leeds, another 4-1 thrashing, and there were many of the same faults on display.

It was not a good first half for Fernandez-Pardo up top. They are mystified in Belgium why he believes he is a centre-forward rather than a winger and he did not do himself any favours here. Newcastle’s best move of the game resulted in Lewis Miley playing in Jacob Murphy down the left. His cutback was perfect for Fernandez-Pardo to sweep home at the near post but instead of trying to make contact, he dummied it, thinking Harvey Barnes was better placed. He was not. It was a baffling piece of centre-forward play.

It had been the easiest 40 minutes Lampard’s side have had since they were promoted, but Newcastle still should have scored before the break.

Nico González spotted the run of Fernandez-Pardo through the middle. He wriggled clear of Bobby Thomas and sat down goalkeeper Carl Rushworth, but the Coventry centre-back got back to block his shot.

Newcastle pressed the self-destruct button early in the second half. A long throw into the box was half cleared. There was a half-hearted attempt to close Cherif down from Yoane Wissa and then a shot that somehow went through a crowd of three Newcastle defenders, including the legs of Botman, and nestled in the bottom corner.

Sidiki Cherif with a STUNNING finish on his first Premier League start! 🤩 https://t.co/EoTB8VCHuR

It should have been three. Again Wissa was partly to blame, losing the ball in midfield to set Coventry on the counter-attack. When Botman made a mess of a clearance it spun perfectly into the path of Cherif. The net should have bulged but the £20m summer signing from Fenerbahce scuffed wide.

The visitors needed something special to get back into it and it came from the most unlikely of sources as Botman unleashed a rocket from 25 yards.

Sven Botman, that is SENSATIONAL! 🤯 https://t.co/GalkqMs5ZE

In a flash the balance of play shifted in Newcastle’s favour. They poured forward in search of the equaliser. Jaissle switched to a 4-4-2 with Will Osula joining Fernandez-Pardo up front, but instead of pulling level, Coventry pulled further ahead.

"We need to improve the things we can control, and right now that's a lot" 🗣️ Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle expresses his disappointment after his side's loss to Coventry 👇 https://t.co/fatJkZYyRM

Very, very satisfying. It’s so hard to win. We played like the team we want to be here. A team you look at and go there’s so much energy and spirit in the group. It was good to get a win. We worked very hard for it. It’s so hard to get wins, especially on the road. And now we’re back at home and we have to work on those attributes [that earned us the win] at Forest. We rotated pretty well, there are different aspects of the game we want to improve on regardless of shape.

A win for Newcastle United this evening will take Matthias Jaissle’s side up to fourth in the Premier League and vindicate the members of the club’s hierarchy who insisted they had appointed an elite manager to replace Eddie Howe.

It will also suggest they got their summer rebuild right and everything will point to an exciting future for a new look team.

Yet, should Newcastle lose against a Coventry City side – newly promoted to the top flight and yet to win at home this season – ripples of discontent will spread through the fanbase and everything about the summer, from managerial appointment to player recruitment will be called into question.

That may seem like an odd thing to write given how wildly different those reactions are but that is where Newcastle find themselves at the moment. We do not actually know if they are any good or what the expectations should be for a young team with a rookie Premier League head coach.

There remains an undercurrent of anxiety among supporters who have seen so many of their best players leave over the last 12 months and be replaced by young, emerging talent from across Europe.

The 4-1 thrashing at Leeds in their last away game was a painful reminder of the team’s vulnerability. They were bullied and outclassed.

Newcastle have not put together an impressive 90-minute performance since the opening day draw with Liverpool, yet that defeat to Leeds was also the only game they have lost. in all competitions. We will know a lot more about them after this. This is a game they are expected to win, so the ramifications of a defeat will be more severe.

When Brian Kilcline was at Notts County, the manager Jimmy Sirrel became a little perturbed by the nickname his young centre-back had carried since his school days. It might have been nice alliteration, but “Killer Kilcline” was not exactly the image he wanted his team to portray.

“Also the lads shouting, ‘get him Killer’ tended to alert referees,” Kilcline recalls.

So Sirrel decided he would put it to the County fans. He organised a competition to establish a better moniker for his foursquare defender.

“You know what they came up with?” Kilcline says. “Curly Wurly. Like the chocolate bar. It was to do with my hair, which was naturally curled. By the way, it was never a perm. But I mean, come on. I can’t imagine Curly Wurly would have intimidated anyone.”

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League match between Coventry City and Newcastle United from the Ricoh Arena. Newcastle have played only once there in the league – a 4-1 victory in the Championship back in 2010 when Chris Hughton’s side stormed the league. Their last top-flight visit to the city was way back in 2000, the year Cov’s 34-season spell in the top division ended. Alan Shearer Kevin Gallacher scored at Highfield Road on that occasion, a year after they were sent packing 4-1 by Gordon Strachan’s side by virtue of goals from Carlton Palmer, Paul Williams, Robbie Keane and Mustapha Hadji.

Today’s visit begins with Newcastle in 11th, having bounced back from their Monday night mauling at Elland Road to beat Hull 23 days ago. So bunched is the table, though, that victory tonight would propel them up to fourth. Coventry, by contrast, are 19th after one win and four defeats from their opening five games. If they win they would join Manchester United on six points and leap to 14th, one place ahead of Nottingham Forest, the team they beat last time out before the international break.

Frank Lampard’s side responded superbly after being hammered 5-0 by Brighton in their last home game, tightening up in midfield and defence and finding precisely Forest’s weak spots that Oliver Glasner has been unable so far to armour-plate. Taiwo Awoniyi, who was sent off during that defeat by Brighton, is absent serving the second leg of his three-match suspension and Hajii Wright and Aurele Amenda are still some way off returning. Tino Livramento pulled out of the England camp with injury and is likely to be sidelined for a while longer but Matthias Jaissle was more optimistic about his raft of other doubts: William Osula, Lewis Miley, Amar Dedic, club captain Dan Burn, Anthony Elanga and Jacob Ramsey.

#1471. Chances to put things right in Europe: The five key battles in Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan will return to a city where they have a glorious history, but this time in dire need of a win to get their European campaign going.

Tonight’s Europa League game against Olympiacos feels a long way away from those Champions League final triumphs in Athens against Barcelona (1994) and Liverpool (2007). However, Ruben Amorim’s side still face a must-win test.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having lost three of four in the UEL thus far, Milan are currently outside even the top 24 places, so they must secure the majority of the remaining 12 points on offer to climb. Their hosts tonight have started much better and are inside the top eight, with 10 points on the board.

Amorim will go with a strong side, or the best possible at least with the injury situation. Pietro Terracciano, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Luka Modric, Samuel Chukwueze, Strahinja Pavlovic, Davide Bartesaghi, Matteo Gabbia, Alexis Saelemaekers and Francesco Camarda are all out.

We start with a duel on Milan’s right flank between Diego Moreira and Bruno Onyemaechi. For the Nigerian defender, it will be just his seventh start of the season (out of 15 games played) and this might be arguably his toughest test yet.

Moreira meanwhile has been outstanding in Serie A, with four goals and four assists to his name already. Yet, he hasn’t really got going in Europe yet just like the whole team, given he doesn’t have a goal contribution outside of domestic action. Tonight is a chance to get the ball rolling.

The main threat for Olympiacos is without doubt the attacking midfielder Jota Silva. The former Besiktas man is already on six goals from his 14 appearances (plus one assist) and has really made the No.10 role his. That said, he too is without a goal or assist in Europe so far.

Meanwhile, this is a huge opportunity for Ardon Jashari, as he admitted in his pre-match press conference. The Swiss did very well off the bench against Frosinone and Modric’s injury has opened up a spot for him to take the reins this evening, though he has not always delivered so far when given that task.

Moving back to Milan’s attack, a big night awaits for Goncalo Ramos. He scored in the 4-0 rout of RB Salzburg but is dry in Europe aside from that. The Portuguese ended a one-month goal drought on Sunday by scoring against Frosinone in a move he started and finished, which offers encouragement after a difficult start in red and black.

His opponent will be someone who knows Milan very well, but from the other side of the city. Lorenzo Pirola spent several years in Inter’s academy and has found himself in Athens as one of the leaders of the Olympiacos defence. Tonight will carry a bit of extra meaning, especially amid talk of a potential call-up from Roberto Mancini.

🇵🇹 #Ramos ends his drought! Will a goal like this unlock the #ACMilan striker? 🔓

🎧 Latest podcast: https://t.co/QfaRwdNXza pic.twitter.com/nafNdAUzuL

— SempreMilanTV (@SempreMilanTV) November 25, 2026

Armando Gonzalez is the one who will lead the line for the home side at the Karaiskakis Stadium. The 23-year-old Mexican has scored once so far in the Europa League, but he has three goals overall in four starts and is vying for that starting No.9 position.

Koni De Winter was solid in Sunday’s win meanwhile, and yet he is in need of a performance having really struggled in his battle with Lenny Joseph in the defeat to Ferencvaros last month. The Haitian international – not even their normal starting striker – constantly got the better of the Belgian, who has been up and down in recent weeks.

Finally, we end with the contest between two midfield veterans: Remo Freuler and Adrien Rabiot. The latter has become the anchor of the Erythrolefkoi midfield, and he knows the Rossoneri very well having played for many years in Serie A. The 34-year-old Swiss international also has four assists from a deep-lying playmaker role.

Meanwhile, it has been a tale of two competitions for Rabiot, just like Moreira. The Frenchman has tallied 5 goals and 6 assists in Serie A, but only one assist in European play, and he actually drew criticism after his performances against Bournemouth and Ferencvaros. It is time to bring that league form onto the continent.

#1470. Real Betis vs Rayo Vallecano - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matt Law | 26 Nov 2026 20:17, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:19

Real Betis will be bidding to return to winning ways in Spain's top flight when they resume domestic affairs at home to Rayo Vallecano on Saturday afternoon.

The Seville outfit lead the overall head-to-head record between the two sides 21 victories to Rayo's 13, while 16 of their 50 previous matches have finished all square.

Real Betis will enter this weekend's match off the back of a 2-0 win over Slovan Bratislava in the Champions League, with the result leaving them sixth in the overall table, claiming 12 points from their five games in the league stage of the tournament.

Manuel Pellegrini's side boast a record of eight wins, three draws and two defeats from their 13 league matches this season, with 27 points leaving them in fourth spot in the La Liga table, five points ahead of fifth-placed Real Sociedad.

Real Betis are only four points behind third-placed Atletico Madrid, but they were held to a 1-1 draw by Sevilla in the Seville derby last weekend.

El Glorioso were last victorious in the league on November 8, beating Elche 2-0, while their last defeat at this level was a 5-2 home reverse to Barcelona on October 17.

Real Betis will be in Copa del Rey action against CD Extremadura on December 1 before facing Atletico Madrid in La Liga ahead of their next Champions League fixture with Como.

Rayo, meanwhile, will enter this match off the back of successive defeats to Real Sociedad and Valencia in Spain's top flight, and it has been a tough season to date for the capital outfit.

Benat San Jose's side have a record of three wins, three draws and six defeats from their 12 matches to sit in 16th spot in the division on 12 points, level on points with 18th-placed Getafe.

Rayo have the third-worst away record in Spain's top flight this season, picking up just two points from six matches, which is a concern ahead of this game.

Los Franjirrojos have actually drawn their last four matches against Real Betis, while they have not been beaten by the Seville outfit since September 2023.

The two teams played out a 1-1 draw in the corresponding game during the 2025-26 campaign, and it was also 1-1 when they locked horns in the same stadium in December 2024.

Real Betis remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension, while Dani Ceballos, Giovani Lo Celso, Iker Losada and Jose Morante are out through injury.

Cucho Hernandez scored twice against Slovan Bratislava on his return from injury on Tuesday evening, and the 27-year-old is now set to come in for his first league appearance since the middle of October.

Antony and Isco are both set to retain their spots in the final third of the field, while Pablo Fornals is likely to be joined by Marc Roca in the middle of the midfield.

As for Rayo, Augusto Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Oscar Valentin are out through injury, but the capital outfit have no fresh fitness concerns.

Sergio Camello has been in strong form this season, scoring seven times in 13 appearances, and the 25-year-old will continue in the final third of the field.

There could also be another spot at centre-forward for Randy Nteka despite the fact that the 28-year-old is still waiting for his first goal of the campaign.

Valles; Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, Garcia; Fornals, Roca; Antony, Isco, Ezzalzouli; Hernandez

Audero; Ratiu, Lejeune, Sadick, Tsiaishvili; Palazon, Ciss, Lopez, De Frutos; Nteka, Camello

Rayo have found it difficult on their travels this season, and we are expecting Real Betis to secure all three points even though their preparation time for the match will be short.

#1469. Moreirense vs Santa Clara - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:33

Looking to record back-to-back home victories for the first time this season, Moreirense welcome top-four hopefuls Santa Clara to Parque de Jogos Comendador Joaquim de Almeida Freitas on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts sit ninth in the Primeira Liga table, six points adrift of fifth-placed Arouca and seven behind the Azorean visitors, who occupy fourth position.

Moreirense spent much of the previous campaign in contention for a European place but eventually finished seventh, and they are currently some way off the pace in the race for a top-five finish following an inconsistent start to this season.

Vasco Botelho da Costa's men have won just four of their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L5), while struggling at both ends of the pitch, having scored 13 goals and conceded 18, the weakest defensive record among the current top-half sides.

The Moreira-based club enter this encounter on the back of a 1-0 defeat to Sporting Lisbon, which ended a two-match winning run following victories over Estoril Praia and Estrela Amadora.

Although losing by a single goal away to Sporting is hardly the most disappointing result, Da Costa will be concerned by a pattern that has seen his side suffer their last three defeats by the same 1-0 scoreline, including a Taca de Portugal exit at the hands of second-tier AVS.

Moreirense have also struggled for consistency on home soil this season, winning just two of their five league matches at Parque Moreira de Conegos (D1, L2), although a 2-1 victory over Estrela in their most recent outing at the venue gives them an opportunity to secure consecutive home wins for the first time since April and May.

Santa Clara, meanwhile, have enjoyed an impressive start to the Primeira Liga campaign, collecting 21 points from their opening 11 matches (W6, D3, L2), although Petit's side have recently seen the resilience that characterised their early-season performances begin to fade.

After going unbeaten in their first eight fixtures (W5, D3), the Azoreans have lost three of their last four competitive outings, beginning with a disappointing Taca de Portugal exit against lower-division Mafra before suffering a league defeat to Benfica.

Although they bounced back with a victory away to Maritimo, Santa Clara were beaten 2-1 by Gil Vicente in their most recent top-flight outing before playing out a 2-2 draw against Valladolid in a friendly on November 11.

Nevertheless, Petit's men remain among the hardest sides to break down in the division, having conceded just eight league goals, with only leaders Porto (five) boasting a better defensive record, while Santa Clara have scored twice as many at the other end.

Their away performances have been particularly impressive, with the Azoreans collecting 13 points from five league trips (W4, D1), giving them the third-best away record in this season's Primeira Liga behind Porto and Benfica.

However, the visitors have struggled in this fixture in recent times, going winless in their last four league meetings with Moreirense and losing three, including both encounters last season, which ended in 1-0 defeats.

Moreirense will welcome Tiago Andrade back into contention after the winger recovered from the muscle problem that ruled him out of the trip to Sporting.

Meanwhile, Alexandre Parsemain (leg) and Joao Veloso (muscle) remain doubts, while Francisco Domingues and Kiko Bondoso are still recovering from their respective muscle injuries and are expected to remain unavailable.

With Parsemain's availability uncertain, Leonardo Vonic could lead the line once again, although Yan Maranho is another option in that position.

Santa Clara have considerably greater selection problems, with first-choice centre-backs Pedro Pacheco and Emanuel Moreira both suspended following their disciplinary issues against Gil Vicente, with the former receiving a red card and the latter missing out through an accumulation of bookings.

Petit's defensive options are further limited by the potential absence of Guilherme Romao, who is sidelined with injury, though Pedro Ferreira could return this weekend if he is fully fit following a nose issue.

As a result, Ythallo could make his senior debut alongside Henrique Silva in central defence, although both have limited first-team experience, having featured predominantly at youth level and as a substitute, respectively.

Goncalo Paciencia returned from injury as a second-half substitute last time out and could lead the line here, potentially leaving Fernando to make way.

There is also good  news in goal,  with Lucas Franca having recovered from a muscle injury and expected to return to contention for the starting role.

#1466. David Raya's shoulder injury isn't 'too serious', confirms Mikel Arteta - as relieved Arsenal boss reveals stricken goalkeeper won't need surgery and COULD face Manchester City

Published: 09:10 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 12:39 EST, 24 November 2026

Mikel Arteta said David Raya’s shoulder injury isn’t ‘too serious’, sparking hope that the goalkeeper could return within weeks.

Raya was forced off in the 70th minute of Arsenal’s 2-2 draw against Newcastle on Saturday at St James’ Park, hurting his left shoulder in a collision with William Osula. He looked in agony as he left the pitch.

His No 2 Kepa Arrizabalaga is instead expected to play for the north London club in their Champions League match against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday.

Though Arteta confirmed Raya doesn’t require surgery and didn’t yet rule him out for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Manchester City.

‘He’s (Raya) not fit for tomorrow, but it doesn’t look too serious,’ said Arteta. ‘We need some more tests tomorrow, but it’s quite encouraging. It seems to be better than expected.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had. The first test shows something much more encouraging.

Arsenal's No 1 David Raya underwent an MRI scan the day after going off against Newcastle

‘There is no need for surgery, which was the main fear because that would have ruled him out for months.’

Asked whether Raya could play at home to Man City, he added: ‘Tomorrow we’ll have more tests and we will know. I think we’ve seen what David brings to the team as well.

‘That’s why we are very protective with Kepa and (third-choice) Illan (Meslier). Everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen.’

Raya has been sensational for the Premier League champions and his absence is likely to hurt the best defensive unit.

'That's a massive worry,' Ian Wright said on Sky Sports when the stopper went down. 'I don't want to say I'm petrified simply because Kepa is in goal, he's the guy who has got to try and keep the goals out for us now.

'But yeah, that is a massive blow. Someone like him, Declan Rice, Gabriel, it is very tough to replace those guys.'

Meanwhile, Bruno Guimaraes said Arteta is ‘crazy’ about the small details that will take him to ‘another level’.

Since his summer move from Newcastle, the 29-year-old has scored vital goals against Sunderland and Leeds - but is yet to complete a full 90 minutes in the Premier League.

Raya hit the turf in pain and went off the pitch clutching his arm to indicate that something serious had happened

‘I now definitely understand my role in the team and the way Mikel wants me to play but I can still play much better,’ said the Brazilian.

‘I think Mikel (Arteta) is unbelievable. He as a manager is so focused on small details, the way you control the ball, the way that you cannot be aligned with your opposite side.

‘Some details I have never heard before, I just found out with him here. He is crazy a little bit about these small details and I try and take (in) as much as I can because he is so passionate about them.

‘He showed me some clips (from when I was) in Newcastle and some clips here, where he thinks I can do things differently. He's trying to take me to another level.’

Arsenal's clash with Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night will feature a new innovation for its TV audience watching on Prime Video. Called 'Progressive Actions' it highlights the passes and ball carries that drive a team up the pitch, and the often-unsung players behind them. Developed by Prime Video's team of producers, engineers, AI experts, and on-air analysts, Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built specifically for the UEFA Champions League. It joins the growing suite of features on Prime Vision, the alternate feed which serves as a laboratory and incubator for new features that often advance to the main broadcast.

Progressive Actions is built on proprietary AI-powered models that identify a Progressive Action based on how far the ball travels in each phase of the pitch, with the threshold becoming shorter closer to the opposition goal where defences are more compact and space is harder to find. The metric mirrors the data used behind the scenes at Europe's elite clubs, yet has historically been difficult to show during a live broadcast. As a player makes a Progressive Action, an on-pitch graphic will show where the action started and ended, the player involved, and the distance the ball advanced, allowing fans to see the game as a coaching team would, in real time.

'Prime Vision is where we develop new features that shine a spotlight on the metrics, actions and players that impact a game most, yet aren't always captured by traditional statistics or broadcast techniques,' said Andrew Hornett, Director of Live Sports Production for Europe at Prime Video.

'Every team has players whose influence goes far beyond the scoresheet, the ones doing the crucial work in the build-up, moving the ball forward two or three passes before an assist. Progressive Actions is designed to capture that impact, measuring and visualising these actions during a live broadcast. Fans will see them in real time as they happen, but we'll also aggregate the data across the game, so you can see which players have had the biggest impact on the match.'

The feature will debut in the UK and Ireland on Tuesday and will also be available for fans in Germany and Italy. Fans can access Prime Vision, with features including Progressive Actions, via their remote from the match detail page or the in-game menu during any live UCL fixture on Prime Video.

Progressive Actions is the first Prime Insight built from the ground up specifically for Prime Video's UEFA Champions League coverage, and sits alongside Tactical Map, Momentum, Physical Insights, Advanced Analytics, Passing Options, and Player ID in Prime Vision's growing suite of features designed to take football fans closer to the game, all available on the alternate feed during every UEFA Champions League match live on Prime Video. Prime Insights were first developed for Prime Video's coverage of Thursday Night Football, its exclusive weekly NFL package in the US, where AI-powered features including the award-winning Defensive Alerts have become a staple of the coverage, advancing from the alternate feed to the main broadcast each week.

#1463. Academico de Viseu vs Alverca - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adeyeye Oluwapelumi | 26 Nov 2026 20:43, Last updated: 26 Nov 2026 20:49

Coming off a three-week break from competitive action, Academico de Viseu and Alverca meet at Estadio do Fontelo on Saturday evening in what will be their first-ever encounter in Portugal's top flight.

The hosts occupy sixth place in the Primeira Liga table, eight points and five positions ahead of their visitors, who are four points above the relegation play-off spot.

Academico de Viseu have made an encouraging return to the top flight after a 37-year absence, having collected six wins from their opening 11 league fixtures (D2, L3), scoring 15 times and conceding 13 at the other end.

Bruno Pinheiro's side, who failed to record a victory in any of their first four outings this term, enjoyed a particularly impressive spell between September 6 and November 1, winning six consecutive league matches, including a famous triumph away to Sporting Lisbon on October 25.

However, that winning run in the top flight came to an end last time out, when the Viseu club suffered a 1-0 defeat to Nacional in Funchal after conceding a late winner to Matchoi Djalo.

The result also means Academico have now alternated between defeats and victories across their last five matches in all competitions, including cup losses to lower-division Fatima in the Taca de Portugal and Primeira Liga champions Porto in the Taca da Liga.

Returning from a three-week hiatus, the Viseu club will be glad to be back at Fontelo, where they have won each of their last three matches, beating Vitoria de Guimaraes, Estoril Praia and Rio Ave by 2-1 scorelines after losing their opening two fixtures at the ground this term.

Like the hosts, Alverca also started the campaign slowly, failing to record a victory in any of their opening five fixtures, but enjoyed a three-match winning run between September 12 and October 12, beating Nacional, Rio Ave and Famalicao.

However, the Ribatejo club have slipped back into familiar struggles, having since gone winless in four matches across all competitions, starting with a Taca de Portugal elimination at the hands of second-tier Tondela before suffering narrow league defeats against Arouca and Benfica.

Sergio Ferreira's team then drew 1-1 with Casa Pia in their most recent outing, with Ian Luccas finding the net in the 66th minute to rescue a point, while the goal ended a three-match run without scoring.

Two wins from their last three league games on the road suggest Alverca have also held their own away from home, although they have been vulnerable when not at their best, losing three of their five away league outings this season.

There is also little to draw from history, given the Ribatejo club are without a victory in their previous three meetings with Academico, losing twice in that spell, although their most recent visit to Viseu ended in a 2-2 draw in February 2025 in Liga 2.

Academico de Viseu form (all competitions):

With no reported injury or suspension concerns, Academico head coach Pinheiro could retain a similar lineup to the one that featured against Nacional, with goalkeeper Ewerton shielded by the defensive quartet of Anthony Correia, Nikolaos Michelis, Robinho and Miguel Angel Brau.

Andre Clovis has scored five of the Viseu club's 15 league goals this season and also provided an assist, with the Brazilian expected to lead the line here.

Alverca could be without Rayan Lucas, who remains a doubt after suffering another setback with his left knee, although the midfielder has returned to integrated training.

Nabil Touaizi is also expected to miss out after suffering a relapse of a right-calf injury, while Bastien Meupiyou and Sabit Abdulai remain sidelined following knee surgery.

Meanwhile, goalkeeper Noah Raveyre is another absentee, with his return expected in early December.

Academico de Viseu possible starting lineup:

Ewerton; Robinho, Correia, Michelis, Brau; L Silva, Messeguem; Guilherme, Kahraman, Mortimer; Clovis

Mendes; Boyan, Gomez, James; Spencer, I Luccas, Gui, Chissumba; Chiquinho, Camara, Figueiredo

Academico have struggled to find the net in recent weeks, but their overall league form and stronger position in the table make them worthy favourites against an Alverca side that have scored just once in their last four matches, so a home victory looks plausible.

#1461. Big Decision From Manchester United Captain As Pochettino Is Set To Take Over

Manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

The calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

The refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

United should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

If Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso has reportedly told Malo Gusto to find a new club, according to CaughtOffside, who are citing Simon Phillips’ Substack. The report claims the 23-year-old France international does not suit the wing-back system Alonso has built at Stamford Bridge. It also floats a surprise swap that would send Gusto to Liverpool and reunite Alonso with Jeremie Frimpong, his former Bayer Leverkusen right wing-back.

Liverpool’s interest has history. They tried to sign Gusto on loan on deadline day, but Chelsea refused anything short of a permanent deal. Their right-back problem has run since Trent Alexander-Arnold left. Frimpong cost around £29.5million and has battled injuries and form, while Ronald Araujo is a centre-back covering on a season-long loan from Barcelona.

Gusto’s standing has slipped quickly. He started three of the first four league games, yet Josh Acheampong has since taken his place, and reports say he will be fourth choice behind Acheampong, Marco Palestra and Reece James once James returns from injury in early 2027.

His strength is defending, with 73 tackles and 36 chances created in 45 appearances last season. The weakness is end product, because three goals and five assists are modest for a wing-back who must supply Alonso’s right-hand width.

Frimpong supplies exactly that. The 25-year-old Dutchman scored 28 of his 30 Leverkusen goals under Alonso and thrives on pace and early crosses. Defending is his flaw, at 5ft 8in and with a poor injury record at Anfield.

No. Chelsea are fifth with 16 points from 10 games, but they have lost four, including 1-0 at Sunderland last Sunday and 3-0 at Brentford, and they concede too easily. Frimpong would add another attacker to a right side that already has James, Acheampong, Palestra and Pedro Neto, and he does nothing for a shaky back line. With no European football this season, Chelsea don’t need that many right-sided options anyway.

The money matters too. Both players have contracts until 2030 and similar valuations, so a straight swap brings Chelsea no cash and leaves Liverpool with their problem solved.

Sell Gusto instead, preferably abroad, since Paris Saint-Germain have been linked and Chelsea are reportedly open to cutting their asking price. Then spend that fee on a defensive midfielder or centre-back, because that is where Alonso’s team needs help.

With the Magpies, the Lodi-born midfielder played 110 games, scoring 10 goals, before moving to Tottenham Hotspur in the last summer window for €108m. There, he has linked up with Roberto De Zerbi, someone who also has Milan in his heart.

There continues to be sporadic rumours about a return to the Rossoneri one day, but given his value it remains a pipe dream for now. Tonali was interviewed by Fútbol Emotion Italia and he recalled some significant moments that he had at Milan, with his comments relayed by Calciomercato.com.

“I have two stories with AC Milan. The first is up until I was 20, when I had never fully embraced the AC Milan world. The second is from 20 onwards for the following three years,” he began.

“I was a fan for a long time. Then when the matches allowed it, maybe there was a game at San Siro when in Serie B we almost always played on Saturdays, we often went to watch. It was something passed down in the family from my father, so I’ve always had it even since I was a child.

“Then past 20 years of age it changed, because as a player you can’t maintain the same relationship with the team that you have as a fan. I did that the first year too, but I felt it too much, so after that I experienced it differently.

“But maybe it was even more beautiful because you put the fan aside and you started to realise that I suddenly found myself there, with the team of my heart and in a stadium like San Siro.

“The first year wasn’t easy, I found myself struggling a bit. But it went well for me also from the point of view of playing without fans. It wasn’t nice, but for me personally as a player at that moment it was good because there was less pressure.

“But all in all it was bad because that year without fans it all seemed like friendlies, it didn’t feel like football. Milan means a lot to me.”

#1458. Real Madrid's £68m Nico Paz transfer plan faces fresh uncertainty as Jose Mourinho responds

By Naim Beneddra | 26 Nov 2026 20:55

Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho has declined to discuss the potential return of Nico Paz to the Santiago Bernabeu amid conflicting reports in Spain over the club's intention to activate their £68m buy-back option for the Como midfielder.

The Argentina international continues to impress in Italian football, registering six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, further enhancing his reputation as one of Europe's most exciting young attacking midfielders.

Madrid retained the option to bring Paz back in the summer of 2027 when an agreement was reached with Como in June to allow the 22-year-old to continue his development in Serie A. However, despite recent suggestions that the Spanish giants have already decided to exercise that option, uncertainty remains over their plans.

Asked about Paz during his press conference ahead of Tuesday's Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, Mourinho offered a typically brief response: "He's not my player."

The Portuguese manager's reluctance to discuss a player contracted to another club should not be interpreted as opposition to the transfer, although his response offered little clarification following contrasting reports in the Spanish media.

Cadena COPE reported last week that Real Madrid intended to activate their €80m (£68m) buy-back option next summer, with Como having reportedly been informed of the decision.

However, according to Jose Felix Diaz of AS, Madrid have yet to reach a definitive conclusion and could wait until the spring before deciding whether to bring their former academy prospect back.

The club's official statement in June confirmed the existence of a unilateral buy-back option for the 2027-28 season. Crucially, the agreement allowing Paz to remain in Italy for another year was reached at the player's own request, underlining the importance he attaches to regular first-team football at this stage of his career.

The biggest sporting consideration for Madrid remains the presence of Jude Bellingham, whose performances under Mourinho have strengthened his position as the team's principal attacking midfielder.

The England international has scored seven goals and provided five assists in 18 appearances this season, including a goal and an assist in Tuesday's 5-1 victory over PSV. Madrid are also reportedly in advanced negotiations over a new contract for Bellingham, whose existing agreement runs until 2029.

Paz's versatility would give Mourinho some scope to accommodate both players. The Argentine is capable of operating from the right or in a slightly deeper midfield position, although those roles would bring him into direct competition with Arda Guler, Brahim Diaz and Bernardo Silva.

Madrid must also consider how the squad will look next season, with Rodrygo expected to return from injury and Franco Mastantuono due back from his loan spell. Summer signing Yan Diomande represents another significant investment in the attacking department.

Spending £68m on Paz could still make considerable financial sense given his age, development and potential resale value. However, the circumstances that prompted him to remain at Como last summer have hardly changed, particularly with Bellingham enjoying such an influential role under Mourinho.

Waiting until the spring would allow Madrid to assess both Paz's progress and the needs of their own squad before committing to a substantial expenditure. With their final buy-back opportunity approaching, the Spanish giants must determine whether they can offer the Argentine the regular football that has allowed him to flourish in Italy.

#1457. Lionesses take step closer to World Cup but do not look like they can win it

England may have edged a step closer to booking their place at next summer’s Women’s World Cup but they do not yet look like a team who can win it.

This two-legged qualifying play-off with Greece was always going to be somewhat academic. Greece are ranked 58th in the world and have never qualified for a major tournament. But they could – and should – have taken the lead before England eventually broke the deadlock through Georgia Stanway just before half-time.

The goals flowed more freely in the second half, but Greece deservedly found the net themselves and are not yet out of the tie. There is every chance of the Lionesses winning the second leg in Leicester on Tuesday more comfortably, but not being able to put teams to the sword is exactly why they ended up in the play-offs in the first place.

The best teams are ruthless and unforgiving – and England did not display those traits here. They snatched at chances, and several players were guilty of firing wide. There were also defensive problems. Greece got in behind England’s back line too often and the goal they scored was far too easy for them.

“I think we made it [the game] a bit harder,” England manager Sarina Wiegman said. “Greece were very well prepared. They were very well organised and well disciplined. Of course I’m happy with the 3-1, I’m not happy with the one.

“We could have scored more goals, we should have. The final stage, the final pass needs to be better. I think we were a little bit in moments really good on the ball and in other moments not so good, and we could have made better decisions too. Lots of things to take from today.

“Sometimes we played really well, sometimes we were a bit sloppy, so sometimes we were a bit frustrated and I think that’s what you saw.”

Avoid defeat in the second leg and England will play the winners of Ukraine v Slovakia. Ukraine, whom the Lionesses beat 6-1 and 3-0 earlier in their campaign, have a 3-1 lead from their first leg. Perhaps the pedestrian nature of this game was partly because it felt inevitable England would win. They did enough to get over the line but still lacked a clinical edge.

It had been four months since they were thrashed 4-0 by Spain, a defeat which relegated them to the play-offs instead of automatic qualification. They had won every other game in their group before that capitulation, but with Spain topping the group on goal difference, England only had themselves to blame for not scoring more goals in their other fixtures. Breaking down ultra-defensive teams has long been an issue for this Wiegman side and they knew that was what they would be facing in this double-header against Greece.

It did not help that many of Wiegman’s players have been struggling for form in the Women’s Super League this season. Wiegman was also without the ever-reliable Lucy Bronze, who dropped out of the squad on Thursday because of injury. That meant Maya Le Tissier was handed a start at right-back while Laura Blindkilde Brown was preferred to Jess Park in the No 10 position.

Greece were far more open than many would have expected, with several gaps in their defence for England to exploit. They also created problems for themselves by insisting on playing out from the back.

England thought they had taken the lead in style when goalkeeper Fafailia Petaloti gave the ball away needlessly. Lauren James took advantage of Petaloti being off her line and produced a tremendous lob from 25 yards out. But the forward was offside when she picked up the ball and the goal was ruled out by VAR.

The excellent Kathryn Batte has run the rule over potential alternatives to Lucy Bronze.

The 35-year-old right-back is out injured, but Ella Toone was called up in her place, rather than a direct replacement.

“Bronze, who is two appearances away from reaching 150 caps for her country, has picked up an injury and returned to Chelsea for treatment,” Batte writes.

“The Lionesses will be missing one of their most reliable players for the matches on Friday and Tuesday, but it gives Sarina Wiegman an opportunity to look at potential replacements for the future.

“Bronze, who has been an integral member of the team throughout Wiegman’s reign, turns 35 later this month. While she will be expected to be the first-choice right-back should England qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, the lack of a recognised back-up has been an ongoing problem.”

Sarina Wiegman revealed that while dropping Toone was a difficult decision, the midfielder’s reaction left a lasting impression on the coaching staff.

“When I gave her the call, of course that was a hard call, but she took that straight away,” Wiegman said. “Of course she was very disappointed, but the first thing she did was say: ‘OK, I’m going to get back, I’m going to do that.’”Wiegman was particularly pleased with how Toone handled herself both on the pitch and in front of the media before her late recall.

“That answer in the game, also the way she spoke about it, I thought that was really good,” the head coach added. “And then getting everything ready, I think that really impressed me. Well done, I would say.”

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of Greece vs England in the first leg of the 2027 Women’s World Cup play-offs.

The Lionesses kick off the two-legged tie tonight looking to secure a solid advantage ahead of Tuesday’s return tie at Leicester’s King Power Stadium. Although they finished level on points with group winners Spain, England’s goal difference sent them into the play-off path, setting up a first-ever senior meeting against a Greek side ranked 55 places below them in the FIFA rankings.

All eyes are on Sarina Wiegman’s selection choices following a turbulent week of squad news. The manager originally raised eyebrows last month by dropping Ella Toone and Chloe Kelly, stating bluntly that “the levels weren’t what I expect from them on the pitch.”

Toone quickly accepted the setback. Speaking after starting in Manchester United’s victory over Liverpool, the midfielder insisted: “It’s about me now. I’ve got to keep working hard and use it as fuel to come back even better.”

That opportunity arrived sooner than expected. An injury sustained by right-back Lucy Bronze - described by Wiegman as “really small” - forced the defender to return to Chelsea for assessment. Wiegman immediately turned to Toone, who flew directly to Greece from Spain, where she had been running her own self-directed training block during the international window.

With 69 caps and 24 international goals to her name - including crucial strikes in the Euro 2022 final and the 2023 World Cup semi-final - Toone brings proven big-match experience back into the setup at a critical moment.

We will bring you all the build-up, confirmed team news, and live play-by-play coverage throughout the evening.

#1456. Arsenal, Liverpool, Chelsea Chase £100m England Midfielder

Arsenal, Liverpool and Chelsea have all contacted Bournemouth about England midfielder Alex Scott, according to CaughtOffside, which cites The i Paper. Liverpool and Chelsea want to move in January, while Arsenal would rather wait until next summer. Bournemouth’s stance on selling the 23-year-old has softened, but the reported asking price is above £100m, and Scott turned down two contract offers over the summer.

The interest has clear reasons behind it. Andoni Iraola coached Scott at Bournemouth before taking over at Anfield in June, and Liverpool want to reunite them. Chelsea lost Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City in a £125m deadline-day deal and had a reported £64m bid for Scott rejected earlier in the summer. Arsenal already have Declan Rice, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Zubimendi and Myles Lewis-Skelly, so CaughtOffside sees Chelsea or Liverpool as the more logical destinations for his playing time.

Scott wins the ball, presses and carries it through midfield, and he started Bournemouth’s first five league games this season before a quadriceps injury on England duty in October kept him out for weeks. Fitness is the first concern, because knee problems have interrupted much of his time on the south coast. End product is the second. He has scored five league goals in 85 appearances since joining in 2023, so he will not solve a shortage of chances alone.

Not at £100m, and not as a January priority. Liverpool rank 18th for big chances after ten league games, according to This Is Anfield, and Scott offers energy rather than creativity. The real gap sits beside Ryan Gravenberch, where Curtis Jones left in the summer, and nobody arrived to share the defensive work.

Scott could be the aggressive partner in Iraola’s double pivot, freeing Dominik Szoboszlai and Florian Wirtz to play higher, yet that is a heavy fee for a player only just rebuilding match fitness, with Liverpool fourth and nine points behind Arsenal.

Chelsea’s case is simpler. The division’s biggest summer spenders lost their midfield engine and can justify the price more easily. Arsenal’s patience makes sense, since Rice, Guimaraes and Zubimendi leave no room for a £100m squad player. A Liverpool bid would only inflate the market Chelsea are already shaping. If Iraola wants a January signing, a specialist holding midfielder for far less money does more for the top-four push.

#1455. Liverpool Transfer News: Dutch Star’s Agent Tests Market

Liverpool transfer news: Ryan Gravenberch’s agent, José Fortes Rodriguez, is exploring ways to take his client out of Anfield, according to CaughtOffside. The site relays a claim from the X account @ITKSpace that Fortes has held “loose but direct contact” with several European clubs, none of them named. No formal exit request has been lodged, and the 24-year-old could still stay, so this reads like a camp checking the market rather than a player pushing to leave.

Liverpool hold the stronger hand. His six-year extension, signed in March, runs to 2032, so any buyer would face a substantial asking price. Real Madrid have been linked before, though nothing here says they are interested now.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 relies on two central midfielders, and Gravenberch, so commanding at the base of Arne Slot’s title-winning side, has struggled to settle. Iraola benched him for three straight games at one stage, he collected a second yellow card in the 3-0 home defeat by Manchester City on 11 October, and a heel problem has since kept him out of the Arsenal and Fenerbahçe games. He has no goals and one assist in the league this term.

His strengths are clear. At 6ft 3in he carries the ball through pressure and starts attacks from deep. Defending space and tracking runners is the weakness, and it shows when his partner also surges forward.

No, not this winter and not at a price set by his worst few weeks. Gravenberch is 24, tied down until 2032, and his market value has slipped sharply since last December, so selling now would hand a buyer the bargain that March contract was meant to rule out.

The real problem sits elsewhere. Iraola received no new midfielder in the summer, and his double pivot has no natural holding player. Gravenberch has admitted he prefers the number eight role, yet Mac Allister and Szoboszlai, who started the 3-1 win at Crystal Palace that lifted Liverpool to fourth, already occupy those spots. Nineteen-year-old Trey Nyoni has mostly played the deeper role this season.

Keep him through January, get him fit, and judge him again in a settled pairing. If Liverpool then sign a proper holding midfielder next summer, Gravenberch becomes a surplus eight, and a big-club bid at the right figure would deserve a hearing. Selling before that signing arrives just removes the one midfielder who can still carry the ball out of pressure.

#1453. GdS: Super in Serie A, struggling in Europe – the reasons behind the ‘two-faced’ Milan

AC Milan are having a positive start to the 2026-27 season in Serie A, but in the Europa League they have been poor. Why exactly is that the case?

Milan go into tonight’s game against Olympiacos needing a win in order to start putting things right in a competition in which they have so far lost three out of four. The top eight expectation has now vanished, with even a play-off spot in jeopardy.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Amorim has been coaching two teams since the summer: one which is excellent in the league with some ups and downs, and another that is frankly terrible when the Europa League anthem players.

Milan score 2.33 goals per game in the league on average, compared to just 1 per game in Europe. All four of those goals in the UEL came in the win over RB Salzburg too: they have drawn a blank in the other three.

Looking a bit deeper, Milan have less possession in Europa League matches (53%, compared to 59% in the league) but shoot 12.5 times per game, more than in Serie A. In Europe they get into the box more often: 26 touches in the opponent’s box compared to 23.

So, why do they score so much less despite being more threatening? Simply put, they shoot worse: the Rossoneri have a very high conversion rate in Serie A (26.4%) which plummets to 10% in Europe. This means that in the UEL it takes 10 shots to score a goal, while in the league it only takes four.

It’s not all mathematics. Anyone who has watched Milan in Europe have noticed their difficulties. At Bournemouth, they were never in the game, against Ferencvaros they collapsed, against Benfica they deserved to lose against a fellow contender.

With just hours to go before the match against the best defence in the competition, another test awaits. However, Amorim must find a way to concede less too. In Europe, Milan concede 1.92 xG per game, while in the league it’s just 1.28.

This all leads to a discussion about line-ups, and Amorim has rotated a lot outside of league action. The right defender has always been Filippo Terracciano or Fikayo Tomori, never Mario Gila. Without the Spaniard, there’s a noticeable difference.

In midfield, Luka Modric has never started, and Adrien Rabiot started only against Salzburg and Ferencvaros. Up front, Diego Moreira started only against Bournemouth. Life, with or without those three, changes completely.

Amorim already knows he won’t have Modric against Olympiacos, but he can plan with Rabiot and Moreira, concocting a strong side despite the injury issues. He’ll ask for overtime tonight and on Monday in Cagliari, knowing his side will then have almost a week to rest.

#1452. Villa Midfielder Has £80m Price Tag For Arsenal: Is He Worth It?

Arsenal transfer news: Aston Villa do not regard Boubacar Kamara as available, even with Arsenal interested, according to CaughtOffside. The report says an offer of around £80m could change that stance, although Villa negotiate from strength because the 26-year-old’s contract runs until 2030.

January looks highly unlikely. Villa have already lost Amadou Onana to a torn ACL suffered at the World Cup, and the Belgian is not expected back until around April. Unai Emery cannot lose a second holding midfielder in the middle of a season. The summer is different. CaughtOffside says Villa could entertain a significant bid then, provided they can reinvest the money in a proper replacement and strengthen the squad around him.

TBR Football reported in July 2025 that he sat on Arsenal’s long list of midfield targets, and his numbers explain why. Kamara has started all 10 of his Premier League games this season, completing 86.3% of his passes, including 83 line-breaking balls, while making 28 tackles and 40 recoveries. He wins 56% of his duels and can play at centre-back, which would give Mikel Arteta cover in two positions.

The weaknesses are just as clear. He has no goals this season, only three shots and an xG of 0.14, and he has committed 20 fouls and conceded a penalty. He also missed the closing weeks of 2024/25 through injury.

The role he would play is obvious: a ball-playing six next to Declan Rice. Martín Zubimendi occupies it now, and Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, six clear of Manchester City, with seven clean sheets.

No, not at that price. Arsenal spent £75m on Bruno Guimarães in August, and Arteta still has Rice, Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Martin Ødegaard and Myles Lewis-Skelly competing for the same central spaces.

FotMob values him at €49m, roughly £43m, so Villa would be asking close to double his market value for a player who turns 27 this month and offers little in the final third. Villa’s insistence on reinvesting the fee also hands them the leverage, which means Arsenal would pay a premium on a seller’s timetable.

The only sensible trigger is a departure, perhaps Zubimendi or the 30-year-old Merino, leaving Arsenal short of a proven Premier League six. Kamara is a better holding midfielder than most of the market, but a title-leading side already has that job covered, and £80m would buy cover rather than improvement.

#1451. Chelsea’s £43m Winger Gamble Is Stalling: Should They Accept A Discount?

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

Garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.
