#1450. Liverpool Open Talks With Argentine Midfielder: Is He Worth A New Deal?

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool have opened contract talks with Alexis Mac Allister, according to @tribuna_ftbl, with his current deal running until June 2028. The report arrives days after his father, Carlos, told ESPN that no discussions had started, although he hinted at news before the end of the year.

It also reverses the summer, when the club extended Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai but made no offer to the 27-year-old, something Mac Allister revealed in September while admitting he had stayed despite chances to leave.

His form explains the change. After a poor 2025/26 under Arne Slot, he has become Andoni Iraola’s first-choice midfielder alongside Szoboszlai, pushing Gravenberch to the bench. He has scored once in the Premier League and three times in the Champions League, including the winner against Atlético Madrid, and holds a 7.29 FotMob average rating across 758 league minutes. Liverpool sit fourth.

FotMob places him in the 88th percentile among midfielders for shot attempts, and he has said the man-to-man system suits him because it demands less communication than Slot’s approach. His weaknesses are just as clear.

His defensive contributions (45th percentile) and aerial duels (46th) sit below the midfield average, and pundit David Lynch has questioned whether his legs have gone in Iraola’s 4-4-2, where two central midfielders cover huge areas. He has also collected four league yellow cards already.

Yes, but not on the terms his summer rebound might demand. Ten league games of good form do not cancel a season in which he looked off the pace, so Liverpool should offer around three years, with wages pitched below the bumper deals Gravenberch and Szoboszlai signed.

The timing still makes sense. With 18 months left, he enters the final year next summer, when Liverpool would face either a discounted sale or a free departure. His FotMob valuation of €66m has almost halved from the €130m peak of September 2025, so selling now would lock in the lowest price.

Iraola also needs a controller to sit beside Szoboszlai’s runs, and no one in the squad does that better. The caveat is that Mac Allister turns 28 next month, so Liverpool must pair him with a quicker partner next summer rather than treat his renewal as the end of the midfield rebuild.

#1448. Please, Oliver, can we have some more? Celtic boss Martin O'Neill tells Danish midfielder Sorensen it's time to up his game

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 13:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 13:13 EST, 24 November 2026

Martin O’Neill has told Oliver Sorensen that it’s now time for him to deliver in a Celtic jersey.

The Danish midfielder arrived in Glasgow with a big reputation after coming in on a one-year loan from Parma. But in his seven appearances to date, the 24-year-old has failed to show why the Italian club paid Midtjylland £8.4million for his services a year ago.

With Mika Baur sidelined for up to ten weeks with an ankle injury, Sorensen is likely to be afforded further opportunities to show his worth. But with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, Luke McCowan and Joel van den Berg all showing up well in the weekend win over St Mirren, O’Neill has warned that Sorensen needs to do more if he’s to force his way into his side.

‘He has, by his own admission, found it difficult,’ said the Celtic manager.

‘I think that he also arrived late as well, trying to get to know people, trying to get his position, trying to get up to speed with what we do. And whatever we do, I bet you it’ll be something really different to what he was doing at Parma.

‘But now it would be up to him. And, certainly, it will be up to him to try and do something as quickly as possible, whether it’s in the next couple of weeks.

Danish midfielder Oliver Sorensen has been lesser spotted at Celtic this season

‘His strength is picking the ball up deep and running and going with it. I think that Van den Berg can do that as well. But that was the idea with losing (Arne) Engels, we were trying to get a like-for-like replacement.

‘At this minute, he has found it difficult. But he’s willing and he wants to learn.’

Celtic face Torreense on Thursday with the game being played in Leiria as the host club’s normal ground doesn’t meet UEFA stadium requirements.

After losing their first three Europa League games to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo, O’Neill’s men earned a lifeline in the competition when they defeated Besiktas last time out.

With ten points likely to be needed to secure progression to the play-off round, the Celtic manager feels it’s imperative that his side are on the seven-point mark after they take on Omonia on matchday six on December 10.

‘We just want to try and do well,’ he stressed. ‘I said after the Besiktas game that it gives you a chance.

Sorensen struggled along with the rest of his team-mates in a Europa League defeat at Benfica

‘Because nobody’s made it after having lost the first three games. So, the next two matches are vital for us.

‘You’d have to think that we’d need to get four points in the two games to give ourselves a chance.

‘After that you’ve got two left over, a home game (Marseille), which will not be easy. And then the away match (Union Saint-Gilloise).

‘It would be nice to carry it into January and still have a chance.

‘We’ve taken enough criticism for not doing well enough in Europe and rightly so. It’s the aim of the football club, it’s what we’ve always said, and that’s been really disappointing.’

Meanwhile, O’Neill believes Kieran Tierney is rediscovering the form which earned him a £25million move to Arsenal in 2019.

The full-back played the entirety of Scotland’s double-header with North Macedonia and Switzerland and lasted 71 minutes of the win over St Mirren – a game in which he claimed two assists.

O'Neill believes Kieran Tierney is close to the form that earned him a £25m move to Arsenal

Delighted that the player appeared to be putting fitness concerns behind him, O’Neill said: ‘Kieran has done great for me. He’s been brilliant, he really has, and he’s getting fitter too.

‘He will be big for us in Europe again. You look at the Besiktas game. Our winning goal late on came from his shot when he was still getting high up the pitch.

‘Kieran has done so well for us and there are signs that he’s back to the Kieran Tierney who got a move to Arsenal.

‘He defends well, he creates goals and he comes up with some too. I genuinely couldn’t speak highly enough about him. He’s a great lad too, very popular in the dressing room.

‘Kieran can play as a centre-half, there’s no doubt about it. He competes better in the air than I ever thought he could. It was only when I came back to Celtic that I realised that.

‘He will battle in the air and he’s a reliable defender. If we are ever dropping into a back three, then it wouldn’t be a problem for him.’

#1447. Arsenal transfer news on Germany winger: Is second choice enough?

Arsenal transfer news: Arsenal like Kevin Schade, but he isn’t the winger they want most. Football.London’s Tom Canton reports that the Brentford forward is on the shortlist for the left flank, with RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa ranked above him. Canton says the 24-year-old Germany international is certainly appreciated at the Emirates.

The ranking reflects an awkward summer for Mikel Arteta. Arsenal sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Vinicius Junior and signed only Christos Tzolis for about £34m.

Tzolis started the first five league games, then suffered a hamstring injury on international duty. Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke have covered since, and Madueke rescued a point in Saturday’s 2-2 draw at Newcastle, which left Arsenal six points clear for now.

Nusa, the 21-year-old Norwegian winger, has six goals and eight assists in 15 matches for Leipzig. Sky Sports reports that the Bundesliga club won’t sell him in January, so a summer deal looks more realistic, with Leipzig reportedly valuing him between £60m and £77m. Schade is the quicker route, but Arsenal asked about him in the summer and got nowhere, according to TEAMtalk. His contract runs until 2028.

Schade has scored three times in ten Premier League appearances from 2.44 expected goals, and his pace suits a side that already creates through Tzolis. He can play either flank or centrally. The weaknesses show elsewhere: no assists, three chances created in 781 minutes, seven completed dribbles at a 25% success rate and 43.8% of duels won. FotMob values him at about £47m.

Not in January, and certainly not as a consolation. Arsenal lead the league, Tzolis remains the first-choice left winger, and Madueke has just shown he can deliver there. Schade would add depth, but he wouldn’t add what Arteta lacks: a winger who beats his man and drags two defenders with him against low blocks.

Nusa builds his game on exactly that, and his output at Leipzig now justifies waiting until next summer. Schade’s returns suggest he would sit behind a fit Tzolis, which is hard to justify at a price Brentford would set after already refusing an approach.

A bid becomes sensible only if Tzolis breaks down again or Leipzig block Nusa completely, because Schade needs no time to adapt to the Premier League. Even then, anything above £50m would pay for potential rather than production, and a 25% dribble success rate tells Arsenal he isn’t the specialist they need.

#1446. A tale of glory or misery in Greece: All the key stats ahead of Olympiacos vs. Milan

AC Milan and Olympiacos will face each other for a fifth time this evening, with the Greek side hosting the Rossoneri in Athens.

The first two meetings came in 1959-60 and the other two were in 2018-19. In the European Cup clashes in 1959, the Rossoneri prevailed 5-3 on aggregate after drawing 2-2 in Greece and then beating them 3-1 back at San Siro. Giancarlo Danova scored a hat-trick in the second leg.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The most recent encounters were eight years ago, as mentioned. Patrick Cutrone (2) and Gonzalo Higuain fired Gennaro Gattuso’s side to a 3-1 home group stage win. Yet, in Piraeus the Diavolo lost 3-1 on the final matchday to drop to third and crash out.

➤ Olympiakos have won one of their four major European matches against Milan (D1 L2), winning the most recent meeting 3-1 in December 2018 in the UEFA Europa League. The Rossoneri have never won an away major European match in Greece in six attempts (D4 L2), failing to score in three of those matches.

➤ Olympiakos have lost just one of their last 13 UEFA Europa League matches (W8 D4), keeping nine clean sheets. In the group stages, they’re unbeaten in 11 games (W7 D4), conceding just twice.

➤ Milan have lost three of their four UEFA Europa League games this season (W1), including their last two without scoring. They’ve never lost three major European games in a row without finding the net. Olympiakos’ Jota Silva has had the most shots in the UEFA Europa League this season (17) – however, he is yet to score with any of those attempts, only landing two of them on target.

➤ Milan have never won a competitive game against a Greek side in Greece, losing 2 and drawing 4. However, they have lifted the Champions League trophy twice in Athens (4-0 vs. Barcelona in 1994 and 2-1 vs. Liverpool in 2007).

➤ Hosts Olympiakos have won each of their two previous Europa League contests at Stadio Georgios Karaiskákis this season. Olympiakos will be out to prolong a six-match home unbeaten streak in all competitions.

➤ Milan have one win and one loss on their travels in the competition this season in two contests. In their last six matches in all competitions, Olympiakos have won four and drawn two. They scored 17 and conceded five over that stretch, scoring first in four of the six contests. They had five first-half goals, while their opponents netted two times in the first 45 minutes.

➤ Milan have won four and lost two in their last six. They scored 14 and conceded nine in that stretch, netting first in four of the six. Most of their goals (10) came in the first half, while their opponents netted three times before the break.

➤ Armando González has caught the eye for Olympiakos in Europa League play. He is their top scorer with two goals, one of which has been the tone-setting first of the match.

➤ Alphadjo Cisse has been the leading attacking threat for Milan, scoring on three occasions in the current Europa League campaign, including one match-opening goal. He is tied for third in the competition’s scoring charts in 2026-27.

➤ The visitors have found it challenging to score in Europa League play recently, as they are scoreless in their last 198 minutes in the competition. They haven’t been on the scoresheet since a Gonçalo Ramos goal in their league phase win against Salzburg.

➤ Milan may face difficulty scoring yet again, as Olympiakos are in the midst of a shutout streak and haven’t allowed a goal in their last three Europa League matches, dating to a Kajetan Szmyt finish in their league phase win against Jagiellonia Białystok.

#1445. Alonso ready to sell £47m Chelsea signing for a Barca star

Chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet says Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and says he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and said needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

#1444. Liverpool track Swedish left-back with £38m price tag

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and plan to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

Iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

The bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

#1443. Queens Park Rangers vs Sheffield United - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:14

Separated by just two points around the top eight of the Championship table, Queens Park Rangers and Sheffield United will square off at MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday.

The hosts sit seventh having extended an unbeaten streak with an away draw in midweek, while their visitors sit a point off the playoff spots after a win and a draw of their own since the international break.

Queens Park Rangers return to MATRADE Loftus Road on Saturday with the hopes of extending an unbeaten run in the Championship and strengthening their position in the top eight.

In their second season under Julien Stephan, following a 15th-placed finish last time around, they currently find themselves seventh having earned 28 points from their first 17 outings, winning seven and only losing three of those with only league leaders Middlesbrough suffering fewer defeats.

The Hoops' success has largely come at the back, with only three teams conceding fewer than the 19 goals they have allowed, four of which came in an away defeat to Southampton at the end of October.

Stephan's men bounced back and headed into the November international break on the back of a draw against Burnley and a win over Lincoln City, before returning with a 1-0 away victory at Millwall at the weekend and a 1-1 draw against in-form Norwich City at Carrow Road on Tuesday having led through Harvey Vale.

With confidence to take from their return from the recent break, but just two points ahead of their visitors in the battle for playoff places, QPR will bid to make it five games unbeaten and bounce back to winning ways on Saturday.

Their visitors, meanwhile, head to the capital aiming to break into the playoff spots having also enjoyed a positive return from the international break.

After a slow start to their third straight Championship campaign, in which they set out to battle for promotion, Sheffield United seemingly hit their stride after the September and October international break, moving onto 22 points from 14 games with four wins and just one loss in a six-game span.

They would then go into the second break of the term on the back of a disappointing loss away at strugglers Charlton Athletic but bounced back in style on their return last weekend, hosting Watford and dishing out a 4-0 beating as Ben Brereton Diaz had them two up with an early brace and Jordan Ayew and Sydie Peck added second-half goals.

Southampton then visited Bramall Lane on Tuesday, and Chris Wilder's men looked to fall short to a solitary Lewis Dobbin goal, but they were eventually able to level and take a share of the spoils as Peck equalised in the 90th minute.

Now poised to crack the playoff spots with some momentum behind them, having earned 17 points in their last nine matches, Sheffield United sit just one point outside the top eight and two off Saturday's hosts, and they will hope to leapfrog QPR with another victory at the weekend.

QPR remain without defender Amadou Mbengue, who is sidelined with a long-term injury, while Jimmy Dunne should also miss out again having been absent for their last two games.

In Dunne's absence, Jake Clarke-Salter and Ronnie Edwards should partner up at the heart of a back four, while Nicolas Madsen also missed the trip to Norwich meaning Glen Kamara and Jonathan Varane will likely continue their midfield pairing.

Richard Kone and Rumarn Burrell will compete to lead the line, while Ilias Chair will hope to return from the outset in support after Kwame Poku, Harvey Vale and Koki Saito were preferred behind Burrell in midweek.

Sheffield United defender Femi Seriki is ruled out for the season through injury, while Matt Doherty, Ryan One, Joe Rothwell and Jamie Shackleton will likely remain sidelined.

They have two players returning, though, with Japhet Tanganga back available after suspension and the captain set to rejoin Liam Kitching at centre-back, and Ben Brereton Diaz back in contention for an attacking spot after being ineligible to play against parent club Southampton in midweek.

He could take the place of Jordan Ayew, who may be rested after being withdrawn as a precaution on Tuesday following two impressive displays, with Tyrese Campbell and Patrick Bamford also pushing to come in up top, while Kalvin Phillips will hope to return to the starting XI in midfield alongside Sydie Peck.

Queens Park Rangers possible starting lineup:

Charles; Adamson, Clarke-Salter, Edwards, Cirkin; Varane, Kamara; Chair, Vale, Saito; Kone

Sheffield United possible starting lineup:

Cooper; Choudhury, Tanganga, Kitching, Burrows; Chong, Peck, Phillips, Donovan; Brereton Diaz, Bamford

Both teams head into the weekend with confidence for what should be high quality and evenly-matched encounter.

Sheffield United have certainly improved since their disappointing start to the season, other than the loss to Charlton before the break, and we see them leaving MATRADE Loftus Road with a share of the points.

#1442. Juventus boss reacts to Manchester United’s midfield link: Is he worth £28m?

Tuttomercato carries Luciano Spalletti’s reaction to the talk linking Weston McKennie with Manchester United, and the Juventus head coach played it down. He spoke to the midfielder as soon as the story broke and didn’t think McKennie had hinted at wanting to leave, calling his comments a general remark. Spalletti said their relationship is as good as the one he has with everybody else, and everything felt calm once McKennie returned from international duty.

Those comments came from McKennie himself, who suggested during USMNT camp that Mauricio Pochettino could bring American players to Old Trafford. La Gazzetta dello Sport then reported that United’s new head coach wants him in January, though McKennie says he isn’t planning to leave and Fabrizio Romano insists United aren’t working on a deal.

Pochettino inherits a club in trouble: one win and eight points from ten league games, 18th place and Michael Carrick’s sacking after their worst league start in 40 years. The Argentine takes charge at Anfield today, before Wednesday’s Champions League trip to Sporting CP.

McKennie, 28, offers versatility: Spalletti has used him on both wings, at wing-back and even as a striker, and he managed eight goals and five assists in 38 appearances before signing his new deal in March. This season the output has dipped, with FotMob showing one goal, no assists and a 6.98 rating from eight Serie A starts. His contract runs to 2030, and FotMob values him at about £28m.

Not as a January priority. United’s problem is a team that loses control of matches, and McKennie is a runner who arrives in the box rather than a midfielder who dictates tempo. Put him next to a struggling back four and his versatility becomes a drawback, because Spalletti gets the best from him higher up the pitch, where his goals come from.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

#1441. Tottenham join race for Inter midfielder facing pay cut: Right move for Spurs?

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

The timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

Calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob shows three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

#1440. Arouca vs Rio Ave - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joshua Ojele | 26 Nov 2026 21:27

Still licking their wounds after their Taca de Portugal fourth-round exits, Arouca and Rio Ave return to action in the Portuguese Primeira Liga when they go head to head at the Estadio Municipal de Arouca on Saturday afternoon.

Rio Ave head coach Vasco Seabra will be out to haunt his former employers in his first return to the Municipal since switching teams in October after two years and 68 games in charge of the Arouquenses.

While Vitor Severino’s appointment has restored confidence in Arouca, consecutive defeats in their most recent two outings have raised fresh concerns, particularly after losing 2-1 to third-tier CD Mafra in the Taca de Portugal last Saturday.

The tie took a difficult turn for the Arouquenses when Moussa Camara and Leandro Alves put Mafra two goals up at the Estadio Municipal de Mafra, and while Ivan Barbero pulled one back in the 59th minute to spark a potential comeback, the hosts held on to see out the victory.

This followed a 1-0 defeat against Famalicao at the Estadio Municipal de Famalicao on November 6, when Paulo Moreira netted in the sixth minute of stoppage time to end Arouca’s run of three consecutive victories in the Primeira Liga.

Despite their recent slump, the Porto outfit can take pride in what had been a solid start to the Primeira Liga campaign, as they sit fifth in the league standings with 20 points from 11 matches, four points behind the Champions League qualifying places.

A disciplined defence has been key to Arouca’s promising start, as they boast the joint-highest number of clean sheets in the Primeira Liga while conceding just eight goals so far — only league leaders Porto (5) have allowed fewer.

Like the home side, Rio Ave saw their Taca de Portugal journey come to an end at the hands of a lower-tier side last weekend as they fell to a 1-0 loss against Liga 3 outfit SC Vianense on Sunday.

The visitors were guilty of a toothless display in attack at the Estadio Dr. Jose de Matos, with Moises Conceicao’s 33rd-minute strike proving decisive in sending Vianense through to the cup round of 16.

This was in keeping with their struggles in the Primeira Liga, where Rio Ave are on a three-game losing streak, suffering defeats against Famalicao, Academico Viseu and Braga, while managing just four points from eight games since August 28.

Off the back of a 12th-placed finish last season, Vasco Seabra’s men have found the going considerably tougher this time around and are one of the early contenders to go down, having collected just seven points from 11 games to sit 17th in the Primeira Liga table.

With the festive period approaching, Rio Ave will head into the weekend keen to kickstart a turnaround, and they will draw encouragement from recent results against Arouca, having picked up five wins and four draws from the last 11 meetings between the two teams since August 2021.

Arouca will take to the pitch without Spanish forward Miguel Puche, who continues his lengthy spell on the sidelines since sustaining a knee injury in April’s matchup against Estrela Amadora.

Barring any late fitness issues, Puche should be the only absentee for the Arouquenses, giving Severino the luxury of a relatively full strength squad to select from this weekend.

As for Rio Ave, goalkeeper Cezary Miszta remains sidelined with a back injury, while defender Nelson Abbey is also expected to sit out the trip to the Estadio Municipal de Arouca.

Brandon Aguilera, Pedro Amaral and Ze Carlos are all listed as injury doubts, leaving head coach Vasco Seabra with a few selection decisions to make ahead of Saturday's encounter.

With just nine goals scored, Rio Ave have plenty to do on Saturday against a defensively solid Arouca side, but we tip the hosts to take control of proceedings and come away with all three points in front of their home supporters.

Lille are considering legal ⁠action after defender Tiago Santos suffered a serious knee injury following an “uncontrolled and dangerous” tackle in Saturday’s match ‌against Le Havre.

Santos, 24, suffered a ruptured anterior cruciate ligament and meniscal tear in his right knee and was carried off the pitch on a stretcher after being tackled by Le Havre midfielder Amir Richardson during the first half of Lille’s 1-0 victory.

The referee gave a foul for the tackle but did not issue Richardson with a caution.

Lille said the ‌tackle merited ‌a red card ⁠and that they had asked the league’s governing body (LFP) to refer the matter to its disciplinary committee. The club are also seeking an explanation of ⁠the video review process undertaken by match officials.

“LOSC is exploring all possible legal avenues and reserves the right to take any legal action necessary to obtain compensation for its losses,” the ​club said. “It will support Tiago in ‌any steps he decides to take to defend his rights.”

Will Olivier Giroud receive a warm welcome back to the Emirates Stadium? The Frenchman spent six years as an Arsenal player but burned a few bridges when he left the club for Chelsea, and then celebrated wildly when Chelsea beat Arsenal in the Europa League final of 2019. Now 40, Giroud has shown remarkable longevity and is unquestionably one of the best strikers of his generation. But can he hurt this formidable Arsenal defence? It’s a tough ask.

Olivier Giroud back at the Emirates ❤️ https://t.co/TPBgcNDsVW

Arsenal pay tribute to one of the club’s greatest custodians this evening following the news of Ken Friar’s death aged 92. Friar worked in various roles at the club across more than 70 years, and a bridge from Drayton Park to Emirates Stadium is named in his honour.

A statue at the end of the bridge is a nod to the chance meeting the 11-year-old Friar had with Arsenal manager George Allison in 1945, while playing football outside Highbury with his friends.

As Sam Dean wrote earlier today, finishing the story: “Allison was so impressed by Friar’s enthusiasm that he told him to report to his office at 9am the next day. Friar did as he was instructed and his reward was a job offer: he became a messenger at the stadium on match days. He was paid 12 and a half pence per week.”

Friar was a long-serving member of the Arsenal board, before stepping back in 2020 and becoming life president.

Arsenal’s players will wear black armbands.

A post shared by Sam Dean (@samjdean_tel)

After signing his new Arsenal contract last week, Mikel Arteta described May’s Champions League final defeat as “poison in his veins,” and last season’s campaign demonstrated the benefits of finishing top of the league phase.

Arsenal enjoyed home second legs all the way through to the final after winning eight from eight, and in a 50:50 draw they fell into a considerably kinder bracket.

Sometimes it can be hard to gauge the importance of these league-phase matches, but Arteta will strive for another perfect record to give Arsenal the best possible chance of going deep in the competition again.

Fixtures against Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are likely to determine whether Arsenal finish in the top two, but there is still a job to be done against Lille this evening.

Arsenal have played against 10 different French opponents in European competition but have never faced Lille, who are managed by Davide Ancelotti, son of five-time Champions League winner Carlo.

Lille sell their best players every summer. After finishing third in Ligue 1 last season they lost Ayyoub Bouaddi and Matias Fernandez-Pardo to Manchester City and Newcastle United for a combined £130m. They have claimed 10 points from their first five league games of the season and led Paris St-Germain 2-0 before being pegged back in stoppage time.

Leading the line for Lille is 40-year-old Olivier Giroud, who scored 105 Arsenal goals in 235 appearances between 2012 and 2018. After leaving the Emirates, Giroud went on to score against Arsenal for Chelsea in the 2019 Europa League final, but he can still expect a warm reception.

Arsenal’s home record in the Champions League has been formidable since they returned to the competition under Arteta in 2023. They have won all 11 home group-stage or league-phase matches, conceding just three goals (two of those were shipped against Kairat Almaty in a dead rubber).

Arteta’s scope for rotation has been reduced by injuries to Piero Hincapie and Martin Zubimendi, but tonight’s game should offer Eberechi Eze and Viktor Gyokeres a chance to impress, while Jurrien Timber needs minutes to build his fitness.

#1438. GdS: Milan join Serie A rivals in race for 13-goal Monza sensation Varela

AC Milan have positioned themselves as one of the contenders in the race to sign Gustavo Varela, according to a report.

If someone had told Varela in August that three months later he’d be on double figures for goals in Serie A (11, 13 all competitions), perhaps even he wouldn’t have believed it. As a result of his exploits, La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm many top clubs in Italy are watching him with growing interest.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Napoli were the first team to make a move, but Milan are also in the mix, as are Inter and Juventus. That’s not all: several teams in the Premier League are following him, and worries about Moise Kean’s condition have seen Como enter the picture too.

More specifically, Napoli want to offload Lorenzo Lucca and have already made contact with Varela’s entourage. However, they must first sell to reach the figures Monza wants. Juventus also need a striker, but Financial Fair Play requires Juventus them to make a sale too.

Como spent €40m on Kean this summer but risk having to return to the market due to the Italian’s long lay-off. Inter are also interested in Varela, but they don’t need to strengthen their attack immediately.

Milan are looking for more goals and have their eye on Nicolo Tresoldi, but Varela could become a worthy alternative, considering he’s already familiar with Serie A. Compared to the other domestic competitors, the price matters least to the Rossoneri.

After scoring a gorgeous back-heel goal against Fiorentina, Varela was asked about his future: “The backheel goal was pure instinct. It’s not something I try in training. A great cross came in, I was right there near the goal, and I decided to give it a try.

“I continue to thank Monza for letting me be here. It’s all been crazy so far: I feel very lucky to be part of this team, and I only hope it can continue like this. Transfer rumors are part of football. I’m having a great time right now, and I’m just trying to enjoy the present without paying attention to the news.”

Unfortunately for Varela this feels impossible, considering everyone’s talking about him at the moment, and will continue to while he is scoring goals at the rate he is.

#1437. Manchester City’s £31m left-back wanted in Turin: Loan or sale in January?

CalcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

City want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

City paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

His strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

The weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

City should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

Otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

#1436. Arsenal eye Serie A’s 11-goal striker: Should they pay £26m?

Arsenal transfer news from Italy centres on Monza striker Gustavo Varela, with Gianluca Di Marzio reportingthat the Gunners are very interested. The 21-year-old Portugal forward has scored 11 goals in 11 Serie A games since joining from Benfica B in July. Barcelona are equally keen, Inter watch him live at every match, and Napoli are reported as his strongest Italian suitor.

The interest makes sense. Viktor Gyokeres, signed for £64m in 2025, has two goals in 15 appearances and none in the Premier League, while Kai Havertz has started 10 of 11 league games for three goals. Arsenal’s results haven’t suffered, but their number nine position has produced little.

Finishing is the selling point. FotMob‘s data has him scoring well above his expected goals for a Monza side that won only two of its first 10 league games, and he averages around three shots per 90 minutes. The weaknesses are just as clear: he wins 34% of his duels, completes 41% of his dribbles and ranks in the ninth percentile among forwards for defensive contribution, which clashes with the pressing Arteta wants from his striker.

Di Marzio says Monza will listen at around £22m to £26m, with the money earmarked for other signings, after paying about £3m including bonuses. Flashscore reports Benfica hold a 20% sell-on and a right to match offers, and Varela’s agents meet Monza this week.

Yes, but in the summer and only if Gyokeres leaves. Arsenal’s results are strong, so a January rush for a 21-year-old would add risk without fixing a crisis. A fee near £26m looks modest beside the £64m Gyokeres cost, and Varela’s goals-per-game record argues for the gamble far more than Gyokeres’ two in 15 does.

The real risk is suitability. He also scores for a struggling side, so his chances come in games unlike most of the Premier League games Arsenal play. Arteta needs a number nine who presses and wins duels, and Varela does neither well, so Arsenal would be buying a finisher and building the rest of his game themselves.

That is workable if Varela arrives as competition for Havertz rather than the first choice. Arsenal should also expect resistance beyond the price, because Benfica’s matching right and Inter’s summer plans complicate any early bid.

Watching him until June costs Arsenal nothing, and another 20 league games will show whether this form is real or a hot streak.

By Sam Varley | 26 Nov 2026 21:41

After returning to the top six of the League One table with a midweek victory, Bradford City will head to Adams Park to take on Wycombe Wanderers on Saturday.

The visitors sit sixth and within touching distance of the top two, while their hosts find themselves 15th on the back of a loss and a draw.

Wycombe Wanderers return to action at Adams Park on Saturday with the hopes of kickstarting a climb up the League One table in the midst of a disappointing run.

They spent the first five games of 2026-27 under Michael Duff, who now leads the visitors, going winless before he was replaced by Tom Hounsell who oversaw an upturn in form.

The Chairboys won three, drew one and lost one of their first five league outings under the new boss but have since put one more notch in the wins column in five further third-tier matches.

That came at home to Burton Albion alongside an FA Cup victory, before Hounsell's men lost a dramatic game to Oxford United last weekend, having led 3-0 through Jayden Wareham, Malik Mothersille and Aaron Morley and been reduced to 10 men with Dan Casey and Luke Leahy sent off before the hosts scored four goals in the final 20 minutes to snatch all three points.

Left wounded by that result, and now on the back of a midweek 1-1 draw with strugglers Bromley, Wycombe Wanderers find themselves 15th and will be keen to put another positive run together beginning with a home win at the weekend.

They meet a former boss who arrives at Adams Park in search of back-to-back victories as Bradford City manager to strengthen their standing in the playoff places.

Braford City's 2026-27 has also been a mixed one thus far, having built on their 2024-25 promotion and 2025-26 playoff loss in League One with a fast start under Graham Alexander, who departed in September, leaving them on 15 points from seven games.

Duff has since taken charge and overseen seven league matches, with the Bantams winning two, drawing four and losing one of those while keeping five clean sheets to move onto a league-high tally of 10 for the season in 15 League One matches.

Following consecutive dominant cup victories, winning 7-0 and 4-0, and a 2-2 draw against Doncaster Rovers, the Bantams headed into a second straight Yorkshire Derby on Tuesday at home to Barnsley and dished out a 3-0 beating as Stephen Humphrys scored a brace and Jake Beesley added a late third from the spot.

Now back in the top six after a blip in the early stages under Duff, while boasting the league's best defensive record and having scored 16 goals in their last four matches to begin to remedy their attacking struggles, Bradford City will bid to make it consecutive wins on Saturday to close in on the automatic promotion spots.

Wycombe Wanderers form (all competitions):

Wycombe Wanderers will remain without Armando Quitirna, Ewan Henderson and Danny Ings through injuries.

Dan Casey and Luke Leahy are back in contention after suspensions for their red cards against Oxford, though, and Casey should rejoin Connor Taylor at the back.

Wareham will continue to lead the line, having scored eight goals in 11 league appearances so far this season, while Caolan Boyd-Munce could again join Cauley Woodrow and Malik Mothersille in support with Fred Onyedinma having missed the last three matches.

Bradford City will field a similar starting XI from the 3-0 midweek win over Barnsley, with Bobby Pointon, Tyreik Wright and George Lapslie sidelined by injuries and key midfielder Antoni Sarcevic also set to miss out again.

They are without Ibou Touray, though, as he is suspended for an accumulation of yellow cards, and he may be replaced by Corey O'Keeffe or Josh Neufville, who has returned in the last two games after an injury layoff.

Macaulay Gillesphey got the nod over George Pratt in midweek at the back and should again join Aden Baldwin and Matthew Pennington, while Humphrys will lead the line after Tuesday's brace and Beesley and Nick Powell will battle to come in in place of Will Swan and Adam Phillips.

Wycombe Wanderers possible starting lineup:

Hazard; Grimmer, Taylor, Casey, Hagelskjaer; Morley, Scowen; Mothersille, Woodrow, Boyd-Munce; Wareham

McCracken; Pennington, Baldwin, Gillesphey; Neufville, Connolly, Morgan, O'Keeffe; Swan, Humphrys, Phillips

Bradford City are showing signs of returning to their best after a slow start under Duff, particularly improving their attacking output in recent weeks while maintaining League One's best defensive record, and we back them to come out on top against a Wycombe side lacking momentum.

#1434. Chelsea’s England playmaker on Man Utd’s radar

Chelsea transfer news around Cole Palmer has flared again, with Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival at Manchester United reviving the noise. Reporter Dean Jones insists the England playmaker’s future at Stamford Bridge is not in doubt, but he admits the sentiment around it is becoming harder to ignore.

Palmer, a boyhood United supporter, has been linked with Old Trafford before. United appointed Pochettino on 18 November after sacking Michael Carrick following one win in ten league games. The Argentine made Palmer one of his most used players at Chelsea, where the pair built a positive relationship, and Palmer scored 22 league goals in 2023/24.

Jones rates the chances of Palmer joining United as extremely low. United’s January budget stands at roughly £50m, and they want a left-back, a centre-back and a striker. A player FotMob values at €100m, roughly £87m, sits outside both the money and the shopping list. Jones also sees no sign that Palmer wants to leave, and says relations at Stamford Bridge would need to break down badly first.

Palmer has started all 11 of Chelsea’s Premier League games this season, playing 970 minutes for three goals, one from the penalty spot, and three assists. His 23 chances created include six big chances, and his 2.58 expected goals backs up the output. Xabi Alonso says, “The better Cole we have, the better Chelsea we have”.

Only ten of Palmer’s 31 shots have hit the target; he wins 46.9% of his dribbles, and he has collected two yellows and a red. Fitness worries more after an injury-hit 2025/26 that ended with him missing the World Cup.

No, but Chelsea should treat Jones’s condition as the real warning. Palmer’s contract runs to 2034, and United’s budget does not reach his valuation, so the danger lies in a deteriorating relationship, not a bid. That puts the onus on Alonso, Chelsea’s seventh permanent manager since 2021.

Morgan Rogers’ £117m arrival from Aston Villa creates the obvious flashpoint. If Palmer feels crowded out of the number ten role, or pushed wide right too often, the homesickness talk will return. Clear roles and managed minutes will protect him better than another forward.

The money belongs elsewhere. Alonso’s side beat United 2-0 on 31 October, then lost 1-0 at Sunderland eight days later, and defensive brittleness and thin squad depth keep undermining a front line that already scores. A back line that leaks goals will not.

#1431. Mainz 05 vs Union Berlin - prediction, team news, lineups

By Anthony Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 22:39, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 04:52

MEWA Arena will be the backdrop for a six-pointer in the lower reaches of the Bundesliga table on Saturday, when Mainz 05 host relegation-threatened Union Berlin.

Die Nullfunfer are desperate to avoid a sixth defeat on the bounce, while Die Eisernen are searching for their first win in six competitive games.

Urs Fischer rescued Mainz when he took the reins midway through last season, but his team are at risk of being dragged into a fight for their survival this time around.

Die Nullfunfer were downed 3-1 by Augsburg last Sunday, falling three goals behind before finding a way through via substitute Ransford-Yeboah Konigsdorffer.

That defeat has left Fischer's side 13th in the Bundesliga table with just 10 points from their 10 matches, a tally that has the club sitting a mere three points above 16th-placed Schalke 04 - and their 17th-placed opponents - in the relegation zone.

Mainz arrive for Saturday's clash having lost each of their past five matches across all competitions, conceding 14 goals in the process with defending that the manager described as "Slapstick."

To make matters worse, the hosts have failed to win any of their five home matches this term, losing four times and drawing once - a goalless stalemate with SC Paderborn on August 29.

Meanwhile, Mauro Lustrinelli's Union have endured a dire campaign so far and are languishing in the relegation zone, but they are far from doomed ahead of their trip to Mainz.

Die Eisernen are currently 17th with seven points, level with 16th-placed Schalke in the relegation playoff spot and within three points of Paderborn, FC Koln and Mainz, though their -18 goal-difference makes it improbable for them to climb out of the bottom three this weekend.

Lustrinelli's side were hammered 5-1 by RB Leipzig last Saturday, letting four goals in during a poor second half after heading into the break on level terms thanks to Michel Aebischer's equaliser.

That disappointment extended the Berliners' winless run to six games across all competitions, a stretch that features three defeats and three matches in which they failed to score.

Saturday's visitors have fared even worse on the road in 2026-27, losing four of their last five away games and conceding a worrisome 18 goals in those losses, not to mention their inability to find the back of the net in any of them.

Mainz will be without the versatile Dominik Kohr this weekend as he continues his recovery from an ankle injury, so expect to see Kacper Potulski, Danny da Costa and Stefan Posch start in Fischer's back three.

Elsewhere, right-sided forward Silas is closing in on return to action after spending eight months out due to a fractured tibia and fibula, though he remains a doubt for Saturday.

If the 28-year-old is unavailable, Sheraldo Becker and Phillip Tietz will start up top, supported by Ransford-Yeboah Konigsdorffer and Nadiem Amiri.

As for Union, they are missing a concerning number of defenders, including centre-backs Zeno Van Den Bosch (suspended for accumulating yellow cards), Stanley Nsoki (calf), and Felix Uduokhai (thigh), not to mention that right-back Josip Juranovic is sidelined due to illness and left-back Andrik Markgraf remains out with a knee injury.

In their absence, Marvin Friedrich and Leopold Querfeld look set to operate at the heart of the visiting backline, flanked by full-backs Christopher Trimmel and Derrick Kohn.

Further forward, wingers Livan Burcu and Robert Skov are both injured, while midfielder Rani Khedira is unavailable after feeling physical discomfort following the loss to RB Leipzig.

Thankfully for the capital club, Kastriot Imeri, Andras Schafer and Michel Aebischer should be on hand to start in the centre of the park, lining up behind Oliver Burke and Andrej Ilic.

Mainz will be desperate to avoid yet another defeat, and while that aim could be realised against their fellow strugglers, a win seems unlikely due to their dire record on home turf.

Union have been particularly poor on the road this season, and their lacklustre defending means they will realistically need to score at least once to prevent a loss.

#1430. Freddie Potts on the pain of leaving West Ham, why he had to move on this summer, upsetting the odds in the Champions League with Club Brugge - and why they don't fear Liverpool!

Published: 08:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:15 EST, 24 November 2026

There are few transfers that get West Ham supporters talking quite like the sale of an academy graduate.

Who can forget the uproar after Grady Diangana joined West Brom in 2020, when club captain Mark Noble released a public statement voicing his anger and disappointment at the move.

Noble’s thoughts were echoed by team-mates at the time, while supporters were similarly up in arms at the sale of the winger.

So, when Freddie Potts joined Club Brugge for £10million on the eve of the season to mark the controversial departure of another product of the proclaimed Academy of Football, you can imagine the reaction.

Potts represented more than a graduate. A boyhood West Ham fan whose dad Steve is a club legend and still serves as a first-team coach, he joined the academy aged six. His brother Dan also came through the ranks.

The midfielder had just enjoyed a breakthrough campaign despite West Ham’s relegation, and many felt he was the perfect player to build their Championship promotion push around.

Freddie Potts is shining in Belgium with Club Brugge after joining from West Ham in the summer

Potts joined the Hammers academy aged six and enjoyed a breakthrough year last season

Hammers favourites Kevin Nolan and Tony Cottee weighed in with their disapproval at his sale, while celebrity fan Ray Winstone expressed his shock and anger live on talkSPORT.

‘Of course you see it (the division about the move) on social media,’ Potts tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘Every player does. But even though last season was tough I always felt I had a connection with the West Ham fans.

‘No matter if I played well or bad I always felt I understood what it meant to play for West Ham. It's a great club with great fans and people. In the end, I had to do what was best for me. I wanted to play this season, and I felt like this was the best place to do that.’

Potts, 22 at the time of his exit, admits it was extremely tough and emotional for him and his family to leave a club he had been at for 16 years.

But, during pre-season he became aware he wasn’t likely to play as much as he wanted to under Nuno Espirito Santo.

‘In the end it’s the manager’s decision,’ Potts says. ‘I wasn’t getting the minutes I wanted. The feeling was that I wasn’t guaranteed to be in the plans as much as Club Brugge were promising me, so I thought it was best for me to move.

‘It was very hard. West Ham have been my club my whole life and I have a lot of love for West Ham. But I had to take into account what was best for my career and I’m loving it at Brugge. It’s a really exciting place full of great people and a great manager.’

Potts had multiple options in the summer, including Premier League interest, yet the chance to play in the Champions League and compete for titles with Brugge attracted him.

Their record of developing young players and a talented squad that includes the likes of Carlos Forbs and Nicolo Tresoldi was equally compelling, and the midfielder hasn't looked back.

Potts started Brugge’s first 10 league games, missing their final one before the international break due to suspension. He returned at the weekend as they thrashed Mechelen 5-1. Ivan Leko’s side are one point adrift of Union Saint-Gilloise at the top of the Belgian Pro League, and they have also impressed in the Champions League.

In Europe, Brugge have beaten Inter Milan, PSV and Lens on their way to nine points from 12, only narrowly losing 3-2 to Aston Villa. Potts has started each match, including their memorable 4-3 win against Inter at the San Siro, and they host Liverpool on Wednesday.

‘It's a really good group of lads,’ he says. ‘Everyone speaks English as well which helps me. It's a good team and we're happy playing with each other.’

He is clearly enjoying life and is just the fifth English player in history to play for the club. Potts did take time to settle though, and admits he initially suffered from homesickness.

‘I found it difficult because East London and Essex have been my home for my whole life,’ he says. ‘West Ham was my life. It was tough in terms of moving into a new language and everything but you get used to it and I’m really enjoying it here. It’ll be strange going back home to England.'

Potts has been a regular and has had a key role in Brugge's impressive early exploits in Europe

Brugge have beaten PSV, Lens and Inter Milan, and they take on Liverpool this Wednesday

Potts’ family have popped over to see him and he has enjoyed exploring his new surroundings. He is yet to learn the local language and scolds himself for being lazy for relying on English, although he has picked up little bits of Flemish.

He has immersed himself in the culture too, and reveals he has tried the world-famous Belgian fries and a few local beers, albeit only when he has enough time to recover between games.

Despite his new life in Europe, Potts remains a West Ham fan and tries to watch them on TV every week.

He has been surprised by their struggles on their return to the Championship for the first time in 14 years, with Nuno paying the price by losing his job. Former Hammers midfielder Scott Parker has since taken the reins.

‘I still think they're playing well,’ Potts says. ‘They've got a great team and Scott Parker is a really good manager. You get ups and downs but I still 100 per cent think West Ham will get promoted this year.'

Potts’ stay in the Hammers first team may have been brief, yet there were still plenty of highs, not least a storming performance on his first Premier League start. That came in a win over Newcastle last November in the Hammers’ first home victory of the season. He was also coached by his dad, an experience he jokes had positives and negatives.

He left West Ham after realising he was unlikely to be first choice under Nuno Espirito Santo

Potts is a boyhood West Ham fan and is fully expecting them to get promoted this season

Attention now turns to Brugge’s clash against Liverpool. It promises to be a tricky challenge for Andoni Iraola’s side against a team who are determined to prove themselves on the European stage.

The two teams are level on points in the league phase, and Potts is keen for his side to take another scalp.

‘I don't think there's much difference in the way we've been performing in the Champions League,’ Potts concludes. ‘It'll be difficult for them to come to our place as well.

‘They're a great team, but we're going to approach it like we have with every Champions League game. We've gone away and beaten Milan, we've beaten PSV away. These are top teams.

‘Results like that give you a boost of how far you can go. You don't want to look too far ahead but every game in this competition is a chance to show everyone what you can do.

‘Liverpool will be a tough game but we've proved it against top teams before and we're going in thinking that we can do it again.’

In his place, Jashari will have a new chance at being the midfield anchor. The 24-year-old Swiss midfielder arrived in the summer of 2025 thanks to Igli Tare, who pursued him for two months, then snatched him from Club Brugge for €35.7m.

Jashari hasn’t quite blossomed yet and his story has been a complicated one. It started with a fractured fibula that sidelined him for two months at the end of August in his first season, while Adrien Rabiot’s arrival and top performances gave him extra competition.

Ultimately, Jashari made 17 appearances in his first season nine of them as a starter, with zero goals and one assist. Under Massimiliano Allegri, the former Luzern player racked up 880 minutes, but now under Ruben Amorim he’s already at 666, and it is destined to rise.

#1427. Celta Vigo 1-2 Bournemouth: Cherries become third club to achieve rare feat with latest Europa League win

By Ben Sully | 26 Nov 2026 22:46, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 02:25

Bournemouth have become just the third team to win their first five main draw matches in a major European competition.

The Cherries travelled to Vigo with a perfect record in the competition after beating Real Sociedad, Sturm Graz, AC Milan and Sparta Prague.

Their impressive record looked set to end when they went a goal and a man down inside the first quarter at Balaidos.

Bournemouth showed character to recover from Bafode Diakite's red card by staging a dramatic second-half turnaround that started with Alvaro Rodriguez's equaliser.

Rayan then netted a 78th-minute winner to fire the Cherries to a 2-1 victory, sending them into an outright lead at the top of the Europa League league phase with the only 100% record out of the 36 teams.

Not only have they significantly boosted their chances of securing a top-eight finish, but the Cherries also became the third team to win their first five main draw games in European competition.

German side Nurnberg were the first team to achieve the feat on their way to reaching the quarter-finals of the 1961-1962 European Cup.

Armenian side Ararat Yerevan replicated the feat when they won the first five games of their UEFA Cup campaign in 1972-1973 before losing on penalties to Kaiserslautern in the last 16.

As well as joining Nurnberg and Ararat in an exclusive group, Bournemouth also became the first Premier League side in three years to win a competitive game after trailing at half time while being a player down.

Prior to Thursday's win, Liverpool were the last team to achieve that feat when Darwin Nunez netted a late brace in a 2-1 victory after Virgil van Dijk had been sent off in the first period.

#1423. Senegal KEEP Africa Cup of Nations title: Champions see crown restored in huge CAS verdict despite walking off the pitch in chaotic final against Morocco

Published: 09:30 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 14:47 EST, 24 November 2026

Senegal have been reinstated as Africa Cup of Nations winners after succeeding with an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), ten months after they beat Morocco in Rabat.

The ruling follows a controversial final in which Senegal initially won 1-0 after extra time, only for the result to be overturned following an appeal to Confederation of African Football (CAF) by the Moroccan Football Federation.

Two months after the final, the CAF appeal board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match because their players had walked off the pitch in protest over a controversial penalty decision.

Morocco were subsequently awarded a 3-0 victory and the title. Despite that, Senegal refused to hand the trophy over.

That decision was based on Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON regulations, which state that leaving the pitch constitutes a forfeit.

However, following an appeal to CAS, Senegal have been reinstalled as champions, with the court ruling that FIFA's law that the referee’s decision is final takes precedence over the competition regulations.

Therefore, because the officials did not enforce the competition regulations at the time, there were no grounds to overturn the result.

The Moroccan FA, though, have not given up and have vowed to take the matter beyond CAS after questioning the integrity of panelist Ulrich Haas.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has restored Senegal as Africa Cup of Nations winners after they were successful in their appeal

Morocco were awarded a 3-0 victory two months after the final, after it was ruled Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch in protest over a late penalty decision

Senegal fans clashed with security in Rabat after the controversial penalty decision

Ruling in favour of Senegal on Tuesday, CAS said: 'In the Panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the Referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.

'As such, the Panel considers that the Referee’s decision was covered by the "field of play" doctrine.

'Since Articles 82 and 84 of the AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case.'

A statement from the Moroccan FA later added: 'We take note of the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport regarding the appeal filed by the Senegalese Football Federation against the decision of the CAF Appeals Committee, relating to the final match of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations. In this context, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation expresses its surprise and protest at the failure to take into account its demand to arrange the necessary legal consequences for practices that would compromise the integrity and credibility of the arbitration procedure, especially what has been confirmed regarding communication between the German referee Ulrich Haas (who sat on the CAS panel) and the president of the Senegalese Football Federation, 48 hours before the decision was issued.

'The Royal Moroccan Football Federation also notes that the decision did not take into account the approach recently adopted by both the International Football Association Board (IFAB) and FIFA, regarding players leaving the field of play without the referee’s permission, and the resulting disciplinary responsibilities and penalties.

'Accordingly, the Royal Moroccan Football Federation confirms its intention to pursue all available legal avenues to appeal the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport.'

The chaos was triggered by events at the end of normal time, when referee Jean Jacques Ndala awarded Morocco a contentious penalty in the 98th minute after being called to the monitor by the video assistant referee to review El Hadji Malick Diouf’s challenge on Brahim Diaz.

The decision came just minutes after Senegal had seen a goal ruled out.

Furious with the penalty decision, Senegal manager Pape Thiaw instructed his players to leave the pitch in protest.

After a 17-minute delay, the team eventually returned, with former Liverpool forward Sadio Mane earning praise for remaining on the pitch and encouraging his teammates to continue.

In the dramatic aftermath, Real Madrid forward Brahim Diaz saw his Panenka penalty stopped by Senegal goalkeeper Edouard Mendy, before Ndala brought normal time to an end.

Senegal went on to score early in extra time, which has now led to a second title in the past three editions of the tournament with their 1-0 victory eventually confirmed in the courtroom.

The low point came on November 1, when Twente won 9-0 at Woudestein, the heaviest league defeat in the club's history, with Nesto Groen sent off after five minutes.

A 1-0 home loss to Go Ahead Eagles on November 7 left Excelsior without a league goal in four games, and they had conceded 20 times in five league matches before the Feyenoord win, leaving a goal difference of -12 from 13 games.

Henk Brugge, in his first permanent head coach job after succeeding Anthony Correia in May, has Telstar 16th on the Eredivisie table with 10 points from two wins, four draws and seven defeats, with 19 goals scored and 28 conceded.

Telstar went ahead after 16 minutes against PEC Zwolle on November 21 through a Simon Graves own goal, but Dylan Mbayo scored twice before half time and Ibrahim Cissoko added a third after a poor back pass from Gabi Caschili.

That 3-1 home defeat means Telstar have gone 17 matches without beating Zwolle in all competitions, and Brugge admitted afterwards that his side may have played the better football but defended badly at key moments.

Telstar have scored in each of their last six league games, 14 goals in all, but they conceded 16 across those matches, including a 4-2 win over Utrecht and 2-2 draws with ADO Den Haag and at Fortuna Sittard.

The defence is the problem at BUKO Stadion, where Telstar have conceded 20 goals in seven league games this season.

Away from Velsen-Zuid, Telstar have taken one point from their last three league trips, losing 1-0 at AZ Alkmaar and 3-2 at Go Ahead Eagles before the 2-2 draw at Fortuna Sittard, and Tyrone Owusu leads the team with five goals this season.

Excelsior have no reported injuries or suspensions, with Groen available again after serving his ban by missing the Go Ahead Eagles game and the trip to Feyenoord.

Sliti, who has three league goals, feared a bruised or broken thumb after Netherlands Under-21s duty on November 17 but started at De Kuip, so Alireza Jahanbakhsh and David Garden remain options from the bench.

Noah Naujoks is back in the midfield after a long injury absence and started alongside Lennard Hartjes, who has suffered three cruciate ligament tears in his career, two of them at Excelsior.

Telstar have no confirmed absentees, with Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes both returning from injury as substitutes against Zwolle, on 57 and 84 minutes respectively, even though some previews still list them as out or doubtful.

Nokkvi Thorisson and Jeff Hardeveld, who both came on after 57 minutes against Zwolle, are options to start in attack.

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Naujoks, Hartjes, Yegoian; Sliti, Dominguez, Thorsteinsson

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Martha, Owusu, Demircan; Brouwer

Excelsior showed at Feyenoord that the goals have returned, with a side that had scored once in five league games finding the net three times against the division's second-highest scoring attack, including a Widell header from a corner and a Dominguez finish after a midfield giveaway.

Telstar have scored in six straight league games, so a clean sheet is unlikely for an Excelsior defence that has conceded 31 times in 13 matches, but Telstar have taken one point from their last three away games and let in 20 goals in seven home league games, which suggests their backline will struggle with Dominguez and Sliti.

The counter-argument is the 9-0 Twente result, yet that came with Groen sent off after five minutes, while the draws in both meetings last season show Telstar can score at Woudestein, so Excelsior should edge a match in which both sides concede.

#1415. Juventus fined €5,000 for Florence kick-off delay but carry no suspensions into Venezia

Serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

Juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

The rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

Only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti said afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

The ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.
