#1414. Carrick’s United are in crisis and now spotlight is on Wilcox

Michael Carrick had urged his Manchester United players to come out and fight. But nobody could have imagined quite how Lisandro Martínez would interpret that message.

By the end of an extraordinary evening in Madrid, where United went 1-0 down inside a minute and never recovered against Atlético Madrid, Martínez had blown the lid off any pretence of all being well at the club as he launched a lacerating assault on the club’s executives.

United had come into this getting battered from all sides and when Pablo Barrios put Atlético ahead, Jamie Carragher’s pre-match assessment about how things could get “very messy, very quickly” for all involved at Old Trafford must have been ringing in the ears of the travelling supporters.

ATLETICO ARE AHEAD IN JUST 53 SECONDS! ⚡️ A nightmare start for United at the Metropolitano Stadium 😬 https://t.co/TdOwoXxopn

They certainly know how to make life difficult for themselves. Leny Yoro’s 74th-minute red card pretty much ended hopes of them taking something from the game.

Ademola Lookman scored Atlético’s second soon after and Carrick was staring at another defeat. And so they now move on to a big game at Leeds on Sunday. This was not the result Carrick would have wanted – and that is before what happened off the pitch.

Ademola Lookman PUNISHES a 10-man Man United 💥 https://t.co/GHKYIHGhNC

Another defeat intensified the pressure on Carrick but Martínez left nobody under any illusions that he felt the finger should be pointed not simply at another manager or the players, but the hierarchy above him.

It was extraordinary to see a player speaking out so publicly in this fashion against his own bosses.

But Martínez pulled no punches, even going as far as singling out Jason Wilcox, the director of football, as he criticised the club’s summer transfer business and effectively accused the club of failing Carrick and the players in the window.

To what extent Martínez’s comments mirror the views of the wider dressing room is unclear, but you have to wonder where Carrick and United go from here.

On the one hand, Martínez was providing a show of support for his manager by attacking the people above him. At the same time, he has presented Carrick with a disciplinary problem to address.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

And United have enough troubles as it is without a senior member of Carrick’s dressing room turning so squarely against the club’s power brokers.

Martínez was probably only giving voice to what many fans have been saying since an underwhelming transfer window closed with more questions than answers. But for a player to talk in such blunt, excoriating terms resonated more loudly than anything a supporter or United’s most caustic critic could say.

The message was simple: you can sack all the managers you want but until you pull together a squad worthy of United’s name and give the man at the helm the tools to compete, the club will struggle to escape this cycle of mediocrity.

No one can reasonably argue United’s window was a success. They went into it with the hopes of landing Elliot Anderson and other premium midfielders but ended up going for numbers over proven quality or pedigree. Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba were not a trio of signings anyone expected at the start of summer, not even the club itself.

There were glaring issues to address in defence, not least at left-back, and at centre-forward but a quality alternative to Luke Shaw never materialised and no back-up was signed for Benjamin Sesko, who was missing for four months with a shin injury that has since resurfaced and which could keep him out for a while yet.

Having done so well to lead United to third and take them back into the Champions League, Carrick would have expected further backing than he got in the summer. Ever the company man, he has been too polite to criticise that lack of investment. But the cat is out of the bag now Martínez has had his say.

It now places the spotlight on Wilcox. United head to Elland Road on Sunday and that was the scene of Rúben Amorim’s final meltdown as manager. Two days after he blew up in a meeting with Wilcox at United’s Carrington training base, Amorim took aim at the director of football and others at the club, demanding they “do their job” and repeatedly declaring that he had come to Old Trafford to “be the manager, not to be the coach”.

It is remarkable to think that, 10 months on, United head back to Leeds with just as many questions as there were back then.

United’s worst start to a league season for 40 years has ensured Carrick is already under pressure, but Martínez is very much of the view that it is no longer enough for the manager and the players to keep carrying the can and that the credibility and suitability of those who recruit the players and make the decisions must now be called into question.

That Martínez picked this game to speak out was interesting. United, lost, yes, and the manner of Atlético’s opening goal from Barrios after 53 seconds was shocking. But United at least went down fighting on this occasion and had fashioned enough good chances to at least draw level before Yoro’s harsh 74th-minute red card swung a delicately poised match decisively in Atlético’s favour.

Lookman made it 2-0 soon after, but Atlético, having looked like they would run all over United in those opening 10 minutes, were made to work hard for their victory.

United cannot keep shooting themselves in the foot like they did in the first minute. Carrick had gone with a three-man midfield to shore things up and made his team more comfortable and yet they were opened up in double quick time by two passes through the middle.

Still, you only needed to look across at United’s opponents to appreciate how chaotic it had become at Old Trafford.

Diego Simeone’s reign at Atlético covers a period stretching two years longer than the post-Ferguson era and in many ways his teams have represented everything United have not been in that time: well constructed and thought through, unified, stable, organised, hungry, aggressive, uncompromising and with a flash of devilment.

If United were not in crisis before this, they are now.

Lisandro Martínez did NOT hold back after United's loss to Atletico 😬👀 https://t.co/OGo25Pzd30

[The performance] was a little bit mixed. It’s a tough enough place to come and the start we had put us in a difficult situation. I thought we grew into the game, had four big chances and [score one or more] and the game looks really different. They were really good chances.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Champions League tie between Atlético Madrid and Manchester United from the Metropolitano. The two sides had contrasting fortunes in their opening fixtures in this competition, Man Utd beating Azerbaijan’s Sabah 4-0 at Old Trafford a month ago while Atléti were defeated by Liverpool who came back from 1-0 down to win 2-1.

But domestically it is the other way round – Michael Carrick’s side have made the club’s worst start in the league for 40 years with one win, three draws and two defeats and have been knocked out of the League Cup. Those of us who watch them regularly – purely because of occupational obligations in this instance – have been surprised by how poor they have been. The results have been bad but the performances even worse.

They seem to lack players who can play on the front foot, who have the athletic dynamism required in this league and too many self-indulgent forward players who either can’t be bothered to help out their team-mates or cannot concentrate long enough to do so. Spooked by their lack of pace in defence and midfield, they are hidebound by caution, dropping ever deeper, ever more reliant on counter-attacking despite the blatant disconnect between the front four and back six. If they drift through this match and Sunday’s trip to Elland Road, Carrick may join the long list of Ineos-driven managerial mis-steps.

Atlético have won six of eight in La Liga and have been defeated only once. They are five points behind Barcelona in second and have score 18 goals and let in eight, which may seem a curious thing to include in a preview but it is done to emphasise that many fans’ perception of Diego Simeone’s team are out of date. Back in the days of Diego Godín, Gabi, Juanfran et all, six wins a draw and a defeat would have had goals for of about 10 and goals against of maybe three.

Simeone is a martinet about attitude not systems or styles and his team have evolved, with the World Cup-winner Alex Baena, who has scored four goals so far, driving them on. He has reintegrated Julián Alvarez, too, after his brazen attempt to force a move to Barcelona so incensed Atléti fans that it seemed they would drive him out of the club. Simeone refused to let Alvarez get his own way and he is now buckling down. Ten years ago Simeone would have bitten his head off.

The one surviving veteran in the squad from that first of El Cholo’s Liga winning sides and the two Champions League finals, victory in which would represent Simeone’s crowning achievement, is the midfielder Koke. Remarkably, if he features today, the 34-year-old midfielder will be making his 750th first-team appearance as an Atlético player.

#1413. FC Koln vs Elversberg - prediction, team news, lineups

By Sebastian Sternik | 26 Nov 2026 23:26

FC Koln will be looking to end their five-game winless run in the Bundesliga when they welcome newly promoted Elversberg to the RheinEnergieStadion on Saturday afternoon.

The Billy Goats will take confidence from their impressive draw against Bayern Munich, while the visitors arrive having lost five of their last seven matches across all competitions.

Frustration has been a recurring theme throughout Koln’s first 10 league games, with Rene Wagner’s side sitting just three points clear of the bottom three despite losing only four times.

Several sides above them in the table have suffered more defeats, but Koln’s joint-high number of draws has prevented them from making a serious push up the Bundesliga standings.

However, their 1-1 draw away to Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena last Friday night was certainly one point worth celebrating.

The Billy Goats ended their six-match losing run against the bruised German champions, and allowed Borussia Dortmund to reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga.

Buoyed by that performance, Koln will now be targeting their first league victory since early October, which would bring an end to their five-game winless run in the competition.

The hosts will be further encouraged by the fact they won three of their six home games across all competitions this season, scoring 12 goals along the way.

Since collecting seven points from their opening four Bundesliga matches, Elversberg have begun to discover just how difficult life in Germany’s top flight can be.

Representing a town with a population of around 13,000, the newly promoted side were always likely to face an uphill battle against German football’s biggest clubs.

Their recent form has underlined the scale of that challenge, with Elversberg suffering five defeats in their last seven matches across all competitions.

On a slight positive note, all but one of those losses have come by a single-goal margin - a stat which shows just how competitive the Black and Whites have been.

That narrow pattern continued in their most recent games, as Vincent Wagner’s side endured a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund before losing 1-0 to Freiburg last Saturday.

Despite that latest setback, Wagner believes his men delivered their best defensive performance of the season, restricting Freiburg to just one shot on target.

Results may have dipped, but the supporters have continued to show their backing, with around 5,000 expected to make the trip to Cologne - almost 40% of the entire population of the town.

Meanwhile, Wagner has already hinted that the club could explore the January transfer market, with sporting director Christian Weber understood to have a recruitment plan in mind.

Koln have one or two selection concerns heading into Saturday’s clash, mainly regarding the availability of Ragnar Ache.

The 28-year-old has been sidelined with a thigh injury since the start of October and, despite returning to training five weeks ago, is yet to make an appearance.

Head coach Wagner described Ache as “fit, training and eager”, although his lack of match action continues to leave a big question mark around his name.

Fellow striker Thijs Dallinga is a more definite absentee, having been ruled out for the remainder of the season with a torn cruciate ligament.

This means that Wagner could turn to either Marius Bulter or Malek El Mala to lead the attacking efforts alongside Said El Mala.

There are also concerns over captain and goalkeeper Marvin Schwabe, who landed awkwardly during last Friday’s draw with Bayern Munich and missed training on Monday and Tuesday due to back pain.

Veteran keeper Ron-Robert Zieler could replace him, though it is worth noting that the 2014 World Cup winner has not tasted competitive action in a little over 12 months.

When it comes to Elversberg, the visitors are almost injury-free, with the exception of Nicholas Mickelson, who returned from international duty with a knee problem.

There are also slight doubts over the availability of Lasse Gunther and Nicolas Kristof, who are both struggling with colds.

Noah Darvich, who is suffering from muscular problems, is a doubt and a decision over his availability could be made as late as Saturday morning.

Zieler; Schmied, Simpson-Pusey, Krauss; Sebulonsen, Okon-Engstler, Sosa; Maina, Moore; Bulter, S. El Mala

Kristof; Gyamerah, Pinckert, Rohr, Gunther; Keidel, Poreba; Petkov, Onyeka, Krattenmacher; Mokwa

Everything points to a close game in Cologne, with the hosts performing well on home soil and the visitors seeing most of their games determined by single-goal margins.

Koln will be buoyed by their result against Bayern Munich and we are backing their momentum to continue with a narrow win over a plucky and dangerous Elversberg side.

#1411. Aston Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Unai Emery can make up his mind on his best XI and tactics as substituting John McGinn backfires in Galatasaray defeat, writes TOM COLLOMOSSE

Published: 15:24 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 16:26 EST, 24 November 2026

Aston Villa made a miserable return to Istanbul as they wasted a wonderful opportunity to put one foot in the last 16 of the Champions League.

In the city that saw them lift the Europa League in May, Villa produced a limp display against a Galatasaray side missing star centre-forward Victor Osimhen. Villa failed to register a shot on target and are now without a win in six games in all competitions.

Substitute Deniz Gul headed the only goal 13 minutes from time as Villa boss Unai Emery cut an angry figure on the touchline and was booked late on. He also appeared to have a tense exchange with midfielder Ross Barkley.

Here Daily Mail Sport's TOM COLLOMOSSE looks at the key moments from another unconvincing Villa display.

Aston Villa left John McGinn out of the starting XI last Saturday and dropped two points in a drab 0-0 draw with Sunderland.

The skipper was back here but three minutes after he was taken off, Villa conceded. Careless defending at a corner allowed Gul to head home, though he took an accidental boot in the face from Nicolas Jackson that required lengthy treatment.

Unai Emery's decision to substitute John McGinn backfired as Aston Villa lost at Galatasaray

Villa conceded three minutes after Emery decided to take off his captain (left) in Istanbul

Deniz Gul scored the only goal of the game with a close-range header on Tuesday evening

With McGinn on the field, Villa would surely have defended the corner better. Jackson's attempted clearance was poor and when the ball looped to Gul, others were too slow to spot the danger.

McGinn and Tyrone Mings are the leaders of this squad and in a period of such change, their role is more important than ever. Though Mings played here, he is no longer a regular starter.

While Emery's wish to protect McGinn is understandable, right now it is a luxury he cannot afford.

Aston Villa (4-2-3-1): Suzuki 6; Harwood-Bellis 6, Lindelof 7, Mings 6, Maatsen 5; Kamara 7 (Buendia 82), J Gomes 6 (Goretzka 66, 6); Alysson 5 (Mbaye 66, 5), McGinn 7 (Barkley 74, 6), Manzambi 5 (Hemmings 74, 6); Jackson 5.

Jackson has nine goals in 15 appearances for Aston Villa - but he has also picked up four yellow cards. Needless bookings proved the forward's downfall during his time at Chelsea and while he has been calmer at Villa, there is still work to do.

During one clash in the first half with Gala defender Davinson Sanchez, Villa boss Unai Emery raced to the edge of his technical area to stop Jackson talking his way into the book. Emery succeeded that time, but not long afterwards, Jackson was punished for a needless tussle with Wilfried Singo.

Jackson plays on the edge. That is a big part of his game. He is also 26 next June and has enough experience to understand when to step into an argument and when to hold back. Emery does not count on Tammy Abraham much these days and Brian Madjo is raw, so he needs Jackson to keep his cool.

The Senegal forward was not the only one to test the patience of referee Daniel Siebert. Joao Gomes was lucky only to be booked for bringing down Yunus Akgun and then grabbing his opponent, while John McGinn was furious that Aleksey Batrakov escaped with a booking for appearing to kick out at the Villa skipper.

Nicolas Jackson's ill-discipline is a concern, with the striker having collected four yellow cards

For most of the last four years, any Villa fan could have written down Emery's first choice XI. Not these days, as Emery still seems to be searching for the ideal formula.

His uncertainty is understandable after losing five key outfield players in the summer but Villa's fortunes this season may depend on how quickly Emery can make up his mind.

Zion Suzuki is the clear first choice in goal and then of the 10 outfield players, how many are lock-ins? Matty Cash and Victor Lindelof in defence. Boubacar Kamara in the middle. John McGinn and - probably - Johan Manzambi in the three-man attacking line, and Nicolas Jackson as centre-forward.

That leaves four spots still up for grabs and not enough of those players are doing enough to convince Emery they deserve the shirt.

Hoping to create some separation in the top half of the Scottish Premiership table, Dundee United will welcome St Johnstone to Tannadice Park on Saturday.

The Tangerines could make it nine games unbeaten this weekend, while the Saints are keen to bounce back from defeat last time out.

Jim Goodwin's Dundee Utd have proven immensely resilient this term, and arrive full of confidence having lost just once on home turf in the league.

Adding to that feeling is the fact the Tangerines thrashed Hibernian 4-0 on the road last Saturday, thanks to a brace from Zachary Sapsford and second-half efforts from Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall.

That victory has Goodwin's side fifth in the Scottish Premiership table with 20 points from their 13 matches, a tally that sees them three clear of city rivals Dundee in seventh having played one game fewer.

United will be aiming to distance themselves from the bottom half this weekend, though it is notable they have drawn as many matches as they have won in 2026-27, including three of their last five.

The hosts also kept just one clean sheet during that spell while conceding six goals in the process, letting in two in the 3-2 home win over Aberdeen, and two in the 2-2 stalemate at Celtic on October 28.

Meanwhile, Simo Valakari's St Johnstone are feeling the pressure from their rivals, and face a tough test to stay in the top half this weekend.

Knowing that they are at risk of dropping down into the bottom six, fans of the visitors will also be concerned after seeing their team score the fewest goals of any team in the top half (18).

In their absence, Jesse Randall and Daniel Bennie look set to support striker Zachary Sapsford up top on Saturday, with Joshua Rawlins and Kevin Ciubotaru offering further width from full-back.

As for St Johnstone, they are missing centre-back Morgan Boyes, who has a calf injury to contend with, though Danny Finlayson and Bozo Mikulic should be on hand to start at the heart of the visitors' defence.

At the opposite end of the pitch, winger Unax Alvarez has a calf injury of his own, and attacking midfielder Jamie Gullan is sidelined due to a groin problem.

#1408. Thuram and Locatelli absences leave Juventus midfield thin for four games in 12 days

Khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

Two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

The table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

The profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

#1406. Juventus and Torino the only Serie A sides without a penalty either way after 11 rounds

Eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

That makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the new refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

The contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

The case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

Luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

The run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

The schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

#1404. Alejandro Garnacho's nightmare Aston Villa loan continues: Struggling star is left at home as Unai Emery picks TWO goalkeepers on bench for Galatasaray defeat before sending warning to ex-Man United winger

Published: 17:00 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 17:05 EST, 24 November 2026

Alejandro Garnacho's future at Aston Villa was plunged into further doubt on Tuesday as he was overlooked for their defeat at Galatasaray.

The Argentine joined on loan from Chelsea last summer with a £43million obligation to buy, triggered when certain targets were hit.

Yet Garnacho has yet to start for Villa and was not even on the bench in Istanbul, even though two goalkeepers were named.

Asked whether Garnacho was fit for this match, Villa boss Unai Emery said: 'Today I think the best players to play with us, to be with us, were here.'

Daily Mail Sport has reported regularly this season that Garnacho may not see out his loan spell and now that looks increasingly likely to be the case.

There is not thought to be a break clause in the loan but if Chelsea and Villa agreed to cancel it, that would allow Garnacho to go elsewhere in January.

Alejandro Garnacho was not in the Aston Villa squad for their defeat at Galatasaray on Tuesday

Villa boss Unai Emery chose to include two goalkeepers on his bench instead of picking of him

Villa had a similar situation with Harvey Elliott. The midfielder joined on loan from Liverpool in summer 2025 but barely played.

Emery decided quickly that he did not want to sign Elliott permanently and could not risk triggering the appearance clause that would have seen him join Villa for £35m.

Villa are now without a win in six and Emery admitted: 'The next challenge against PSG at home will be huge. If we can recover the three points we lost today maybe we still have a chance to reach the top eight but we are not favourites.'

Emery also bemoaned the home side's time-wasting tactics after Deniz Gul headed them into a 77th-minute lead.

He said: 'I am not blaming the referee but he was unfair with us by adding only five minutes. After they scored it was impossible to play.'

#1403. Zhegrova plays 82 minutes in Kosovo’s 0-0 with Israel before Dublin decider for second

With Edon Zhegrova in the starting line-up, ten-man Kosovo held Israel to a goalless draw, a result that leaves them second in Nations League Group B3. The run-out gives a Juventus forward who rarely starts for his club valuable match fitness while Pierre Kalulu is injured.

In Pristina, the Juventus forward Edon Zhegrova was Kosovo’s main attacker against Israel.

Zhegrova tested Israel’s defence a couple of times in the first half but faded after the break, according to TuttoJuve. Dion Kacuri came on in his place.

Below Kosovo, Ireland have 5 points and Israel 3. Austria beat the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on the same Saturday.

Kosovo’s campaign has been uneven. They opened by beating the Republic of Ireland 1-0 on 24 September. Three days later they lost 3-1 away to Austria on 27 September. On matchday 3, they had also drawn 0-0 with Israel.

The final round pairs the Republic of Ireland with Kosovo and Israel with Austria. That leaves Ireland, sitting just below Kosovo, hosting the side directly above them. Zhegrova is set to be central to Kosovo’s hopes of holding on to second place.

For Juventus, the significance lies in the minutes. Zhegrova has started only once since joining the club. He sits low in Spalletti’s pecking order and has mostly featured in short spells off the bench.

More than 80 minutes as Kosovo’s focal point gives him match fitness. That could prove useful before Juventus face Venezia in Serie A and Omonia in the Europa League.

The squad is stretched. Scans at J|medical on 9 November found a low-grade injury to Pierre Kalulu’s left biceps femoris. The defender had felt muscle discomfort in his left thigh after the draw at Fiorentina. France withdrew him from their squad. The midfield is also short of bodies.

Spalletti has made clear he sees potential in the winger. “Edon se si completa un po’ può diventare un crack,” the coach said. If Edon rounds out his game a little, he can become a star.

First comes Dublin. Kick-off at the Aviva Stadium is at 7.45pm UK time, with second place in the group at stake.

#1402. Auxerre vs Marseille - prediction, team news, lineups

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00

Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.

After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.

After a rough start to the 2026-27 campaign, it appears as though Auxerre are doing just enough to get by domestically.

Will Still’s men lost their first three matches of this top-flight season, but have since collected points in six of their last eight league fixtures.

That has them just a point above Strasbourg who are in the relegation playoff spot heading into matchday 12 with Auxerre just three points above Angers, who are in the last automatic relegation position.

So far this season AJA have yet to lose a Ligue 1 fixture when netting the opening goal, with their draw versus Monaco last week being the first time they dropped points in that position.

They lead the league regarding fouls per match (16.1) while allowing the joint-most goals in this competition after 11 matchdays (25).

AJA have points in three of their last four Ligue 1 fixtures at home, with their last win at Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps occuring in September against Brest (2-1).

Marseille will hope their late collapse against Le Mans serves as a temporary speed bump and a wake-up call going forward.

Bruno Genesio’s side bounced back well in midweek, defeating Levski Sofia 1-0 in Europa League action, putting them into the knockout places in that competition.

Clean sheets like the one they collected on Thursday have been rare for OM in Ligue 1, as they have conceded a 2.40 xG average following their defeat to Le Mans in the top flight.

Fortunately, they are balancing that out with plenty of goals, averaging the second-most goals per game in Ligue 1 (2.2) heading into matchday 12.

After 11 matchdays, only three points currently separate them from the top three and a place in next season’s Champions League.

Les Olympiens will seek a third successive triumph versus Auxerre in this competition, having won both Ligue 1 meetings against them last season 1-0.

Both Bryan Okoh and Assane Diousse will miss this match for Auxerre as they recover from cruciate ligament tears, while Sekou Fofana has a groin strain and Danny Loader is questionable with an ankle injury.

Romain Faivre scored their only goal on matchday 11, the second of the campaign for the man currently on loan from Bournemouth.

At Marseille, Derek Cornelius is still recovering from a hip problem, Emerson Palmieri is questionable with a knee injury and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is questionable because of an illness.

Amine Gouiri scored the winner in their Europa League victory on Thursday, becoming the first OM player to net in five successive competitive fixtures since Florian Thauvin in 2018, while he and Igor Paixao scored in their defeat to Le Mans.

Nardi; Diomande, Tuanzebe, Siwe; Senaya, Ahamada, Danois, Oppegard; Faivre, Lascary; Archer

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Kamissoko, Nnadi; Gomes, Maupay, Paixao; Gouiri

These are two of the most inconsistent defensive units in the league, and in a match which could be wide open for that reason, we believe the quality of the visitors, who have fared well in those kinds of matches this season, will enable them to prevail.

#1401. Çelik pulled from Türkiye XI with left hamstring tightness as Kalulu is already out

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

An Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

The league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

#1400. Amorim explains selection choices, Ferencvaros lessons and responsibility to win consistently

AC Milan head coach Ruben Amorim knows that results are needed in Europe, but once again stressed that he foresees a ‘long-term project’.

Milan have racked up just three out of 12 points in the first half of the league phase, meaning they really need to change gear if they are to progress into the next round. Tonight’s game is another very tough one on paper, given Olympiacos have 10 points on the board and are in the top eight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amorim has named a strong starting line-up featuring the likes of Mario Gila, Koni De Winter, Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos and the top scorer Alphadjo Cisse. However, what doesn’t help the cause at all are the nine injury absentees, which is noticeable when looking at the bench.

The head coach spoke to Sky in the build-up to kick-off in Greece to shed light on his selections and the importance of learning lessons in Europe. MilanNews relayed his words.

You’ve gone with an attacking side tonight…

“In football, you have to defend and attack. We have to defend with 11 men and attack with 11 men. The players know what positions they have to occupy and are ready.

“We have to be more compact, and even with these attacking players on the pitch, we can defend better than in other Europa League matches.”

Did the players learn their lesson after Ferencvaros?

“I think they understand. We’ve seen videos, we’re working. Against Ferencvaros, we were sluggish because we weren’t compact and focused on the details. In Europe, we need to raise our game and do what we’ve done several times in Serie A.”

Are you ready to prove you can play three good games in a row in a week?

“I think we have to be a great team. To be that, you have to win both in Serie A and in Europe. We have that responsibility. Results matter a lot, obviously, but we’re on a long-term project. We need to understand if we can play during the week, and today will be an additional test.”

#1399. Chelsea transfer news: Blues 'closely monitor' Boca Juniors centre-back ahead of 2027

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11

Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.

The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.

After making his senior bow in August, the former captain of Boca’s reserve side swiftly established himself in the first team and helped the club win the Copa Sudamericana in Barranquilla last week.

Herrera impressed in the 2-0 final triumph over Atletico Mineiro, completing 56 of 58 passes and recording nine clearances as Boca kept a clean sheet.

Argentine publications El Crack Deportivo and Clarin via Sport Witness report that Chelsea scouts are closely assessing Herrera's physical and technical progress as part of the club’s continuing recruitment drive in South America.

The 1.80m right-footer has earned plaudits for his speed, aerial strength and composure when playing through the opposition’s press from the back.

Herrera showed his eye for a decisive moment on October 25 by scoring his first senior goal with a late winner against Independiente that secured Boca's place at the top of the annual league standings.

The youngster's growing standing has attracted praise from some of Argentina’s most respected figures: Boca's record appearance-maker Roberto Mouzo has likened him to 1978 World Cup winner Alberto Tarantini, while Oscar Ruggeri has called on national team manager Lionel Scaloni to give him senior minutes straight away.

Chelsea are not the only club following the youngster. Barcelona are reportedly seeking scouting reports ahead of January, while Benfica, Borussia Dortmund and Porto have also been linked with him.

Despite increasing interest from England and elsewhere in Europe, a move to prise Herrera away from La Bombonera in 2027 is unlikely to be straightforward.

Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme is determined to keep the heart of his trophy-winning squad together as the club prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

Head coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena has also told the board he wants the defender to stay, praising his strength in one-on-one duels and his willingness to learn from more experienced team-mates.

Boca have yet to receive a formal offer or begin transfer talks, putting the club in a strong position to resist early approaches while Herrera continues to develop in Buenos Aires.

United agreed with the federation that the staff would be released once those national-team duties were over. Pochettino became USA head coach in September 2024. His record with the national team stands at 21 wins, 12 defeats and two draws from 35 matches.

The comments land awkwardly in Turin. Reports had already linked United with a January move for the American. Juventus regard him as central to Luciano Spalletti’s plans and are reluctant to let him leave mid-season, ESPN reported.

His contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

McKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

The club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

The timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Thuram is out until 2027 after knee surgery. Captain Manuel Locatelli also faces a long absence after twisting his right knee against Milan. He had surgery in Lyon on 8 September to repair the external meniscus, and Corriere dello Sport put his lay-off at five to six months.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are reportedly facing a fee of at least €80m (£67m) if they are to tempt teenage defender Joane Gadou away from Borussia Dortmund.

The 19-year-old French centre-back has made a swift breakthrough in Germany after joining from Red Bull Salzburg for €20m (£16.8m) last summer.

Dortmund believe they have found another exceptional prospect with the potential to make his mark on the international stage, and his estimated market value has reportedly already risen by 40% to €28m (£23.5m) according to Sport Witness.

The former Paris Saint-Germain academy player, recently linked with Liverpool, is under contract for the long term and has no release clause, leaving the Bundesliga club firmly in control of his future.

The leading Premier League clubs are likely to have stepped up their interest after Gadou delivered a commendable performance in Tuesday's 1-1 Champions League draw with Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium.

Viktor Gyokeres put the hosts ahead inside the opening 10 minutes, but Gadou supplied the match’s defining moment in the 55th minute, earning Dortmund a valuable point.

The teenager surged forward from his own half, fended off two Arsenal challenges and played a decisive pass for Maximilian Beier to equalise.

In his 89 minutes in North London, Gadou also made four clearances and completed 19 of his 22 passes, drawing warm praise from head coach Niko Kovac.

"We signed him because he is composed in possession and can contribute going forward," Kovac said. "He can break the lines and regularly create chances for the strikers. He is also very quick with the ball. It was a truly impressive performance.”

Bild via Sport Witness reports that Dortmund will not consider offers below four times the €20m (£16.8m)they paid Salzburg only months ago.

The club’s firm position is intended to discourage bids in January as Kovac's side aim to retain their key players for the second half of the 2026-27 campaign.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are not the only clubs linked with the Frenchman: former side Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid are also reportedly interested.

#1395. The two things Roberto De Zerbi demanded from Luca Williams-Barnett's first Tottenham start as 18-year-old star signs new lucrative deal, writes MATT BARLOW

Published: 08:08 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EST, 24 November 2026

Having summoned Luca Williams-Barnett to his office to let the teenager know he would be making his first Premier League start, Roberto De Zerbi could not resist a little bit of fun.

De Zerbi cast a serious demeanour and told him he had weighed the options and figured the best course of action would be 60 minutes with the Under-21s.

Williams-Barnett did not hide his disappointment. 'Why, do you think you are ready to start for the first team?' asked the Spurs boss. The 18-year-old said he thought so.

De Zerbi cracked a smile and told him he was in the team against Ipswich but demanded two things in return.

First, that his young star would play with freedom as though 'in the park with friends' and second that he would work without the ball in the manner of the world's best players in his position, such as Lamine Yamal.

This is where the comparisons to Yamal emerged soon after Williams-Barnett lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. On Tuesday, he was rewarded for his progress with a new contract at the club.

He said: 'This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

Luca Williams-Barnett scored his first Premier League goal for Tottenham on his first start in the top flight

The talented academy youngster may not be lightning fast but he has pace and creates goals

'Spurs is a family to me. I've been here for so long – it's a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

'The club has trusted and believed in me, now I'm ready to repay that.'

Hopes are indeed high. Similarities with Yamal are evident in physique, his fluency of movement on the ball and the bursts of pace, the way they look to play. Even the hairstyle.

Just as Yamal, a left footer, likes to operate wide on the right for Barcelona and Spain, De Zerbi deployed Williams-Barnett as a right footer on the left, although most of his youth career has been spent centrally in the No 10 position.

He does not possess what you would consider in modern football to be exceptional pace, but he is quick, and his strengths are on the ball. He likes the ball. He creates. And he scores goals.

From wide on the left against Ipswich, he scored within 15 minutes, darting in at the back post to finish, and created the second for Dominic Solanke, with a 60-yard run from inside his own half and cross with his left foot.

His brilliance lit up the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there has not been a lot to celebrate in the last 18 months. Terrible home form was the crux of last season's relegation fears.

Here, they rose to salute a new talent, one of their own. One De Zerbi believes has the attitude to match his outrageous talent. Confident, certainly. Aware of his natural gifts and his technical skills. Perhaps bordering on arrogance when on the pitch.

De Zerbi was pleased to see Williams-Barnett, in a seat nearby on the team bus from the training ground to the stadium, watching YouTube clips of Ronaldinho, Eden Hazard and Neymar.

The Spurs boss, who has faith in the power of inspirational video footage, took this as a positive sign. The youngster was relaxed but more than this he had a passion for football and always looking to learn.

'I'm positive about his character and behaviour because I've been working with him for three or four months and I know him enough,' said De Zerbi, whose tactical instructions involved James Maddison operating closely to Williams-Barnett, a kindred spirit in a footballing sense able to talk him through the game.

When the teenager set off on the swaggering run for Solanke's goal, Maddison could be seen nearby urging him forward into the ocean of space left open by Ipswich.

The 18-year-old had rival clubs circling but Spurs have now tied him down

Born and raised in Luton, Williams-Barnett comes from a strong, grounded family - which will only help as he looks to assimilate into the senior side

Spurs have prioritised Premier League experience in the transfer market under De Zerbi to create a more mature dressing room environment. Signings such as Andy Robertson have been key to this.

The policy is not purely for the benefit of academy graduates stepping into the first-team environment, but it does help when it comes to setting the standards required in elite sport.

Anyone gifted enough to break into the Spurs squad will have been feted as a star through the youth development phase and well rewarded to resist others trying to lure them away.

Williams-Barnett was under contract until 2028 but his new deal means clubs circling must now look elsewhere.

It is easy for impressionable teens to become conceited in this situation. Williams-Barnett has had discipline and time-keeping issues but most at Spurs speak of a young man devoted to his football from a strong, loving family who are sure to keep him grounded.

He was born and raised in Luton, starting out in Luton Town's pre-academy to Under 10s, before Spurs paid a small fee for him.

His father Jonathan Barnett was a central midfielder in Step Three of non-league football, known as 'Jono' and playing for various clubs in the region including Dunstable Town and Arlesey Town and renowned for his passing, set pieces and with an eye for goal.

Although more of a dribbler, Luca grew up with football in the family, polishing his technical skills with his dad in the back garden. 'He is from a very good family and it's crucial for this type of players,' said De Zerbi.

Spurs have been here before, of course, with talented teens breaking through with N17 at their feet.

There was Mikey Moore's wonderful cameo against AZ Alkmaar after which Ange Postecoglou called for patience and commonsense, and Maddison went on TV and said it was 'like having Neymar on the left wing'.

There was Jose Mourinho taking the match ball from Son Heung-min, who had just scored the most incredible solo goal against Burnley, and handing it to Troy Parrott on his Premier League debut.

There was Mauricio Pochettino dubbing Marcus Edwards his 'mini Messi'. Pochettino soon came to wish he had not burdened Edwards with such lavish praise.

The pitfalls are well known and progress is rarely a smooth upward trajectory. It is a balancing act between maximising potential and getting carried away.

De Zerbi is quietly confident Williams-Barnett has what it takes to handle the hype.

On the new deal, thought to be for five years, the manager said: 'Luca is a player I think the world of, and I'm so happy that he has signed a new contract.

'He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

'Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

'The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.'

READ MORE: The next Lamine Yamal? Why no? Roberto De Zerbi sets a high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW

#1394. Arsenal transfer news: Championship club prepare offer for Ethan Nwaneri, underused at Dortmund

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:25

Ethan Nwaneri was the breakout star of Arsenal's 2024-25 season, but he has endured a difficult period for several months.

Short of game time at Arsenal, the 19-year-old Englishman was loaned to Marseille in the second half of last season. It was an underwhelming spell, during which the winger started only four times and was labelled a flop.

This season, Arsenal decided to send him out on loan again, this time to Borussia Dortmund.

However, the England Under-21 international no longer really features in the plans of Niko Kovac. Although he was used on many occasions at the start of the season, Nwaneri has not been in Dortmund's starting line-up since 17 October, away to Union Berlin (0-0).

Since that game, he has made a string of appearances in the final minutes of matches and has been left on the bench for the big games, against Bayern Munich (2-2) and Arsenal (1-1).

As a result, the player, who belongs to Arsenal, has played only 29 minutes in the German club's last seven outings, which is insufficient game time. This situation could also benefit West Ham United.

According to FootballTransfers, West Ham are preparing a loan offer to bring Nwaneri to the club in January.

The London club, 13th in the Championship, are looking to strengthen their squad in an attempt to return to the Premier League. However, the deal is far from straightforward, as Arsenal will first have to recall their youngster from Dortmund.

The British outlet points out that Nwaneri's loan at Borussia Dortmund does not include an option or obligation to buy. Arsenal have a recall clause which gives them the possibility of bringing their youngster back in January.

However, the Bundesliga leaders paid a loan fee, reportedly between £3.4m and £4.3m (€4m-€5m), and are covering the player's wages. Therefore, if Arsenal activate the recall clause for Nwaneri, they would have to reimburse the loan fee to Borussia Dortmund.

It therefore remains to be seen whether Arsenal will be prepared to give up that compensation to allow their talented youngster to join an environment more conducive to his progress, and whether the London club will demand another paid loan this winter.

West Ham are, in any case, lurking and ready to position themselves for the deal.

#1393. Juventus sell out Venezia game as Omonia sales pass 35,000

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

General sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

This season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

The Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

Taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

Barcola is the scorer, but the initial danger was instigated by Ngumoha, dribbling around the outside of the LASK defence and into the box where he is tackled. The ball breaks free to Koumas, and he sets it back for Barcola to find the far corner. Liverpool now in command.

The goals have been coming from Liverpool and, really, it should be a night for them to plunder a hatful. LASK have loud supporters and the atmosphere being created is typically of one of these smaller European stadiums but Liverpool are miles better than LASK and should rip them apart. Bradley Barcola looked like a weight had been lifted as he got his first goal and you would now like to see him get a couple more – it’s certainly possible for him to do so.

A Van Dijk-esque header you could say, and Liverpool have punished LASK’s jittery set-piece defending. Good delivery from Tsimikas, and Araujo rose highest around seven yards out to plant a header byone Jungwirth.

Some harrying from Gravenberch is enough to win Liverpool another corner, their fifth of the game so far. The goalkeeper was shaky again, but the ball glances off a LASK head and out for another corner.

LASK are targetting Liverpool’s left flank with direct balls forward, and the big centre-forward Adeniran caused Jacquet all manner of problems near the touchline but his touch ran away from him in the box.

The another good Barcola run is found, but his shot is screwed just wide of the near post. Barcola and Wirtz certainly more involved so far.

Diligent defending from Jorgenson to halt the progress of Barcola after a burst into the penalty area from the left. From the Liverpool corner, LASK goalkeeper Jungwirth was uncertain but Araujo could not not get enough on the header.

There really is something incongruous about seeing Kostas Tsimikas wearing the Liverpool captain’s armband. The reason Alisson doesn’t wear it is because if there is a decision that requires him to talk to the referee in the opposition area, he would be miles from his own goal and potentially vulnerable. Liverpool starting to turn their screw now. First, Wirtz skipped through a couple of challenges and fired a low shot straight at the goalkeeper before Ngumoha, playing on the right, drops a shoulder and drives to the byline, standing up a dangerous cross.

Liverpool struggling to clear their lines from the corner, and Schopf scoops a shot over the bar from the edge of the area.

Lewis Koumas looking dangerous again, peeling behind LASK’s defence and rounding the goalkeeper Jungwirth on the corner of the penalty area, but he was forced wide and had to settle for a corner which the goalkeeper claims.

Kostas Tsimikas captains Liverpool tonight, not words I ever expected to type but it is a team short of experience. Liverpool enjoying all of the possession so far, LASK are defending in a 5-2-3 shape, so Liverpool’s full-backs should have some time and space. Gravenberch does well to win a foul in midfield.

The home team play in all red, so Liverpool are in their white away strip. It looks like there is some Liverpool support among the locals/neutrals in the home end.

Subs: Schutzenauer, Schillinger, Freckleton, Ljubicic, Kalajdzic, Verhaeghe, Elfadli, Flecker, Kane.

A young Liverpool team has been selected to face Linz – the third youngest, according to Opta, that the club have fielded in the Champions League – and Andoni Iraola is being mindful of players such as Virgil van Dijk and Alexis Mac Allister being overburdened ahead of Saturday’s trip to Brentford.

One novice who certainly deserves his starting spot is Trey Nyoni, the England Under-21 international has impressed in the opportunities he has been given so far this year. Watch out for his calmness on the ball and the efficiency with which he uses it.

He should get more chances in the next 10 days, as it is difficult to see Dominik Szoboszlai being ready at least until the home match against Brighton on Sunday week.

Asked about Liverpool’s youthful team, Iraola said: “For me Trey [Nyoni], [Lewis] Koumas and Rio [Ngumoha] are young players coming in from the academy but they are first team players.

“They are first team players because we trust them, and in our situation, where we have some injuries, and we come from playing three days ago. I think they can play well, and I hope they do well.”

24 - Liverpool's starting XI against LASK has an average age of 24 years and 186 days, their third-youngest ever for a UEFA Champions League game, older only than September 2001 v Borussia Dortmund (24y 136d) and December 2020 v Midtjylland (24y 26d). Knocks. https://t.co/4JeW73N87k

Subs: Mamardashvili, Woodman, Gomez, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Munoz, Chambers, McConnell, Danns, Sonni-Lambie, Lucky

It is early days for Bradley Barcola but is has been an underwhelming start to his Liverpool career. The winger was a rotational player at Paris St-Germain, as he is for France, so Liverpool spending £120m is a gamble on his raw athletic attributes and the hope that he pieces everything together.

As Dominic King writes in this piece: “Barcola had no control over the price that Richard Hughes, Liverpool’s former sporting director, brokered with Paris St-Germain for his release. But something he can control is public perception and, with no goals or assists so far, opinions are starting to form.”

Of the five Premier League teams in the Champions League this season, Liverpool have the friendliest league-phase fixtures and they can secure back-to-back wins against Austrian side LASK in this evening’s early kick off.

Having already vanquished one of their pot one opponents by beating Atletico Madrid at Anfield, Andoni Iraola’s team really should be targeting one of the top spots.

They travel to Linz without some key players, though. Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai missed the defeat by Manchester City and remain sidelined, while Hugo Ekitike is a long-term absentee.

There were positive aspects to Liverpool’s performance against City, but they collapsed like a deck of cards after Ryan Gravenberch’s harsh second yellow card.

Tonight’s game is one they should dominate, and it is a presentable opportunity for Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola to kick-start their seasons and respond to the recent criticism of their performances. Iraola hopes to have a stronger squad to choose from at the weekend, when Liverpool face a stringent test at Brentford. This is the second of nine matches in 28 days for Liverpool.

“You don’t have a lot of time to train,” said Iraola. “You try to prepare the games now a lot of times just with the videos and the tactics boards, just a little bit outside. You have to prioritise the freshness of the players.

“Especially now we are playing four games in 10 days, it’s keeping all the legs, all the energy in the games.

LASK are currently third in the Austrian league, but booked their place in this season’s Champions League proper with a remarkable comeback from 4-0 down on aggregate against Celtic.

They have injury problems of their own to contend with George Bello and Moses Usor limping off in the weekend’s defeat by league leaders Rapid Wien and Ramiz Harakate tearing his anterior cruciate ligament in July.

They do play on a grass pitch at the Raiffeisen Arena though Kasper Schmeichel, the former Celtic goalkeeper who was working as a TV pundit for the game, was critical of the playing surface.

#1389. 'Weighed a little on the team', former Lyon team-mate gives Rayan Cherki verdict

By Axel Clody | 27 Nov 2026 06:53

Rayan Cherki made a strong impression on Jeffinho during their time together at Olympique Lyonnais in 2023. Appearing as a guest on the Charla Podcast, the Brazilian forward first praised the technical qualities of the current Manchester City player, before describing a much more divisive character.

'Rayan Cherki. What a player! He is a bit annoying, but he strikes the ball and drives it with both feet. He is very strong' - he explained.

Jeffinho then went on to explain what could bother him about the Frenchman. 'You can see it in the way he plays. He dribbles and looks at the others' - the Brazilian said, naming Bradley Barcola among the best players he has played alongside and liked.

The testimony becomes even more interesting when he discusses relationships within the Lyon dressing room.

According to Jeffinho, Cherki belonged to a fairly closed group that also included Corentin Tolisso, Alexandre Lacazette and Anthony Lopes. The Brazilian describes a 'small clique' of important players who stayed together a lot and, in his view, had real influence in the team.

At the time, Lyon's management had nevertheless denied the existence of a 'Lyonnais gang'.

Asked about the player with the most assertive temperament in this circle, Jeffinho naturally named Cherki.

He explained that the group 'weighed a little on the team', while not hiding that their attitude could sometimes annoy him. His testimony remains nuanced, however: with each criticism of the Frenchman's behaviour, the former Lyon player returns to his immense quality as a player.

Jeffinho also extended his judgement to Cherki's current situation at Manchester City. 'Cherki plays extremely well, but you also have to respect the others' - he said, before suggesting that his attitude could sometimes have a negative impact on his team.

A very personal view of the attacking midfielder, but one that above all sheds light on the relationships he observed in the Lyon dressing room.

#1388. Olympiacos 2-4 AC Milan: Hutchinson inspires remarkable comeback in Greece

AC Milan produced a stunning come-from-behind victory against Olympiacos, scoring four times unanswered to win 4-2.

It looked like being another miserable European night for Milan, as they fell two goals behind inside 50 minutes. The first was given as a Mike Maignan own-goal after Lorenzo Pirola’s header from a corner hit the crossbar then the goalkeeper, then Jota Silva doubled the advantage.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Out of nowhere, Milan mounted a comeback inside 15 second-half minutes. Omari Hutchinson inspired it, scoring a wonderful solo goal to halve the deficit, then setting up Alphadjo Cisse for the equaliser, and also providing the assist for Christian Pulisic’s goal off the bench.

Diego Moreira finished a counter-attack right at the end of the game to make it 4-2 and seal the result, one that was very much needed for Milan given their start in the competition. The play-off hopes have been dealt a big boost, while the top eight could still be a possibility too.

Amorim made four changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Frosinone on Sunday. Two were enforced due to injuries, with Ardon Jashari replacing Luka Modric and Pervis Estupinan taking Davide Bartesaghi’s spot. Meanwhile, Alphadjo Cisse and Omari Hutchinson came into the attack.

The first shot of the game took less than two minutes to come and it provided an example of the intense pressing that the home side have become known for, though Freuler’s effort from distance was a speculative one that sailed comfortably over.

Milan began to string some nice moves together, and they had a couple of attempts of their own from just beyond the edge of the box miss the target. The first came from Cisse, who cut inside and curled one well over and wide, then Jashari concluded a promising attack with a wild shot.

There were two moments of panic in quick succession for Milan. The first was when a cross from the right evaded everyone and fell to Martins, though thankfully his touch let him down in a dangerous area. Then, Goncalo Ramos had a rough fall and seemed to jar his knee, but he got up and played on with a grimace.

The first shot on target fell to the home side and it came after Sankhoun Diawara lost possession inside his own half. Jota Silva picked up the ball and fed Pedersen, whose attempt was thankfully down the middle and caught by Mike Maignan.

Olympiacos continued to have the better of the scoring chances, as Martins began to find his range. Firstly he shot from distance but weakly and straight into Maignan’s arms, but then the Frenchman had to made a brilliant save at full-stretch to keep out the Portuguese’s strike.

The trend of tame efforts from around 20 yards out continued midway through the first half up at the other end. Ramos won an aerial duel and collected it to try and gallop in behind, eventually laying it off for Moreira who didn’t really test Ortega.

Right on the half-hour mark, the home side took the lead. A corner kick from the left was defended awfully in truth, with Pirola getting the better of Diawara in a central area to head off the crossbar, off Maignan and in from six yards out. Going behind in the Europa League is by this point an all-too-familiar feeling.

Milan were inches away from getting themselves level quickly as Pirola turned from the hero in one goalmouth to the hero at the other. A ball over the top found Cisse’s run in behind and Ortega came darting off his line but the ball squirmed through. The Italian somehow got a shot off from the floor that was rolling into the net but for Lirola’s last-ditch sliding clearance for a corner.

There was a flash point towards the end of the half which saw De Winter and Jota Silva both go into the box. A long ball over the top was eventually followed by play being blown dead for offside, yet the pair had a stand-up wrestling match for about 20 yards, until they both even ended up off the field.

In the first of two minutes added on at the end of the half, Pirola had a chance to actually get his name on the scoresheet after the opener was labelled an own-goal. Some dire defending down the right ended with a cut-back that the former Inter youth academy man fired over from inside the box.

Amorim chose to make two changes at the break, as the American duo Christian Pulisic and Yunus Musah came on. Ramos and Estupinan were the ones to make way, with Cisse going up front and Moreira switching over to left wing-back.

Within four minutes of the restart, Olympiacos doubled their lead after yet more calamitous defending. De Winter continued his trend of failing to strong together multiple games without errors as he played a stray pass out from the back, allowing Freuler to play though Jota Silva, who fired past Maignan first time.

De Winter then gave away a sloppy foul when it looked like he had brought a ball under his control and Amorim had seen enough, bringing Fikayo Tomori on for the Belgian.

Just as it looked like getting out of hand for Milan, Hutchinson scored a goal from nothing. Having seized possession inside his own half, the Englishman went on a brilliant solo run down the right where he was nearly clipped down twice, before jinking inside onto his preferred left foot and finding the bottom corner with a precise low shot.

Milan built on the goal that got them back into it, and six minutes later they drew themselves level. A sustained period of possession inside the Olympiacos half saw the ball worked nicely down the right side for Hutchinson to cross perfectly onto the head of Cisse at the far post, who headed in from a few yards out for his 10th of the campaign.

As if things couldn’t get any more dramatic, Milan completed the comeback as they made it 3-2 with 20 minutes left on the clock. Hutchinson was again the man who did all of the hard work, getting the ball on the touchline and sitting his marker down before driving to the right edge of the box and standing up a cross for Pulisic. The substitute struck his volley perfectly, nestling it inside the post.

Milan made their final two changes either side of the third goal, with Filippo Terracciano replacing the cautioned Diawara, then Christian Comotto coming on for Cisse.

It was the Omari Hutchinson show in the second half, and the on-loan Nottingham Forest man should have had yet another assist when he darted past his man to fire in a low cross that squirmed to Moreira but was skewed wide.

With just a couple of minutes left there were huge penalty shouts from the Greek side after a header struck Tomori, though replays showed it hit his shoulder. The Rossoneri broke from that corner and had a four-on-one, however Hutchinson stumbled when playing the final pass, and Pulisic sent Moreira’s square pass into the stands.

The finale to the game saw Milan finally kill it off. Olympiacos had a corner that produced a scramble inside the box, which eventually saw Hutchinson emerge with it and lead another counter. He found Pulisic down the left who slid it across for Moreira on the right, and the former Strasbourg man settle it well, cut inside and fired into the bottom corner for the final act of a dramatic night.

#1387. Ferrero sets Juventus ambition to be what it once was, as €200m capital raise runs

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero set out the leadership's view of the rebuild at the Brussels launch of the club's European Union fan club. He spoke while a capital raise of about €200m is open and a UEFA settlement limits spending.

Juventus president Gianluca Ferrero went to Brussels on 18 November with a clear message for supporters. Restoring the club to its former self is its absolute ambition, he said, adding that the club is following the path set out by its chief executive and is confident this can happen. He spoke at the opening of the Juventus Official Fan Club European Union, which is chaired by MEP Sandro Gozi. The timing gives the statement weight.

The new supporters’ club opened at the Iosono il Piemonte event space. Its stated purpose is to link Juventus supporters with the institutional centre of Europe.

Before the opening, the delegation went to the European Parliament with Gozi. Chief Club Affairs Officer Giorgio Chiellini led the group alongside Ferrero. Piedmont regional president Alberto Cirio attended the opening, as did MEPs who have joined the fan club.

The visit showed Chiellini’s work on the club’s relations with institutions and European football. It also gives supporters an official club in Brussels.

The financial backdrop is demanding. Juventus posted a consolidated loss of €66m for 2025/26. On 12 November, the board approved the offer, using part of the €250m authority granted by shareholders at the extraordinary meeting on 3 November.

The offer involves up to 208.5m new shares at €0.96 each. Shareholders can buy one new share for every two they hold. The price is 28.36% below the theoretical ex-rights price, based on that day’s share price. The remaining €50m of the authority can be used in later financial years, depending on the club’s financial needs and investment plans.

The spending limits come from UEFA. European football’s governing body fined Juventus €20m for breaking the football earnings rule. Of that amount, €14m is conditional. The club agreed a three-year settlement with annual targets. It also faces limits on registering new players on its UEFA List A.

Those are the limits within which Ferrero’s ambition must be pursued. Any improvement in the squad has to fit within the annual targets agreed with UEFA.

Subscription rights can be traded on Euronext Milan until 25 November, and the offer closes on 1 December 2026.

#1384. FIFA, concern after the cyberattack

“FIFA confirms that it has been the victim of a criminal cyberattack resulting in unauthorized access to a limited number of personal and professional information. » This is how the FIFA spokesperson commented on the cyberattack which targeted the computer system of the governing body of world football.

Quoted by the sports media, the Reuters agency indicated that the files in question would not have been violated. In reality, only 0.1% of all FIFA data would have been affected. And these famous files would not be part of it.

As a reminder, Gianni Infantino remains under threat of a summons and a hearing before the North American authorities concerning his plan to sell shares in the World Cup. FIFA, for its part, completely rejected the accusations made against it.

In the meantime, the current Italian-Swiss-Lebanese boss presents himself as the big favorite for his own succession, during the FIFA presidential election scheduled in Morocco on March 18. Four candidates facing him, including Philippe Diallo, the boss of the French Football Federation (FFF).
